summary: The engine is unusually disciplined for a portfolio game: a seeded mulberry32 PRNG is threaded through state, the reducer is effectively pure (offer() spreads a fresh haggle before mutating it, so no aliasing into prior state), and the UI gates (affordable = gold >= floor, max = min(ask, gold), Quick-deal disabled when unaffordable, final-offer hides Pay when broke) chain together to make the dreaded "can't-afford soft-lock" actually unreachable — completeBuy's can't-pay branch is correct defensive dead code. StrictMode double-invoke is handled: lore banking is idempotent via an includes() guard, end-of-run banking via an endRecorded ref. That said I found one genuine determinism leak (sleep() consumes a draw from a stale RNG chain after generateDay re-seeds, and never persists it), one real gameplay-correctness bug (only one rapport tier unlocks per night even when the player crossed two — a "lost" backstory card and a swallowed perk), a handful of medium issues around RNG double-seeding semantics, the goldUp effect missing rent-night and skipping the flourish on equal-gold, and several minor robustness/dead-code items. No crashes, no soft-locks, no localStorage corruption hazards. Records persistence is sound; corrupt/blocked storage degrades gracefully. The headline risk is the multi-tier-skip bug, which silently withholds story content and a perk the player earned — exactly the kind of thing that erodes trust in a "fair dealing earns reward" game.

findings.title: Crossing two rapport tiers in one day silently swallows the second perk AND its backstory card
findings.problem: sleep() unlocks at most ONE tier per night: `const tierDef = RAPPORT_TIERS[state.tier]; if (tierDef && next.rapport >= tierDef.at) { next.tier = state.tier + 1; ... next.phase = 'backstory'; return next; }`. It checks only the current tier and returns immediately. If a strong trading day pushes rapport across two thresholds at once (early gaps are small: 12→28 is +16, and a wanted-fair sell is +3, +1 streak, across 6 bag slots a 16+ jump is achievable), the player has earned tier N+1 but only N is granted. The next tier waits for the NEXT sleep — but its `at` is already passed, so it triggers the following night regardless of further play, meaning the perk (e.g. +2 slots, discount) and the real bio card are delivered a full day late, or near the win/end can be lost entirely (e.g. if you cross 46 and 66 on the morning of day 8, you win on day 9 having seen only one of the two cards). Because the whole rapport system is framed as 'fair dealing reveals who Kaito really is', withholding earned story content is a direct hit to the core promise.
findings.recommendation: Loop the tier check instead of a single if, draining all crossed tiers and queueing their cards. Simplest correct shape: keep advancing while `RAPPORT_TIERS[next.tier] && next.rapport >= RAPPORT_TIERS[next.tier].at`, applying each perk, and push each crossed tierDef onto a `pendingTiers` array; show them as a small stack of Backstory cards (ACK advances to the next queued card, then to the shop). If you want to keep it one-card-per-night for pacing, at minimum apply ALL crossed perks immediately and only defer the card display, so the player never loses a perk they earned.

verification.reasoning:
Read shopEngine.js:424-468 and shopData.js:164-207 directly. The defect is real and accurately described.

sleep() (lines 451-462) does exactly what the finding claims: it reads only the CURRENT tier `const tierDef = RAPPORT_TIERS[state.tier]`, checks a single `if (tierDef && next.rapport >= tierDef.at)`, advances `tier` by exactly +1 (`state.tier + 1`), applies exactly ONE perk via applyPerk, sets pendingTier/phase='backstory', and returns immediately. There is no loop and no draining of multiple crossed thresholds. If rapport jumps across two thresholds in one trading day, only the lower tier is granted that night; the higher one waits for the NEXT sleep (which then fires unconditionally because RAPPORT_TIERS[next.tier].at is already passed). So the perk + bio card are delivered a full day late. Confirmed.

Feasibility of a 2-tier jump is sound. Per-trade rapport: buy gives 1-3 (line 353: overValue>=1.2->3, >=1.1->2, else 1); sell gives base 1, +2 for a fair wanted sale (line 391: price<=ceil*0.96 -> 3), +1 for streak>=3 (line 392) -> up to 4. With 6 bag slots and a buy+sell per item, +16 to +18 in a day is achievable. Tier gaps from 0 are 12,16,18,20,22,22 (at: 12,28,46,66,88,110), so crossing two mid-game thresholds (e.g. 28 and 46) in one strong day is realistic. The finding's '12->28 is +16' framing and 'achievable across 6 bag slots' is accurate.

The 'lost entirely near win' claim is correct and actually UNDERSTATED. The win check (lines 442-448, `if (newDay >= CONFIG.victoryDay)`) returns BEFORE the tier check (lines 451-462). So on the final sleep (day 8 -> day 9 win), the tier check is never reached at all: ANY pending tier crossing (even a single tier earned on the last day, not just a second simultaneous one) is lost permanently. The finding's day-8 example is directionally right; the precise cause at the very end is win-precedence rather than the one-per-night cap, but the player-facing outcome (an earned backstory card is never shown) is exactly as described.

Minor wording caveat: 'the next tier ... triggers the following night regardless of further play' holds only for non-terminal nights; it does not survive a winning night. This doesn't weaken the finding — it strengthens the data-loss case.

Severity high is justified: the rapport system is the explicit emotional core ('fair dealing reveals who Kaito really is'), and the lost/delayed content includes both real gameplay perks (+2 slots, friend's discount, +1 patience) during the tightest rent-pressure window AND irretrievable narrative cards. This is a true engine logic defect, not a design preference.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Two coupled fixes:

1) Drain ALL crossed tiers per night instead of one. Replace the single `if` at shopEngine.js:451-462 with a while-loop that advances `next.tier` and applies each perk while `RAPPORT_TIERS[next.tier] && next.rapport >= RAPPORT_TIERS[next.tier].at`, pushing each crossed tierDef onto a `pendingTiers` array. Set phase='backstory' if pendingTiers is non-empty. In ackBackstory (lines 480-488), shift the next queued card and stay in 'backstory' until the queue is empty, then call generateDay and go to 'shop'. The Shop.jsx backstory modal renders pendingTiers[0] and ACK advances through the stack. This preserves one-card-at-a-time pacing while never losing a perk or card.

2) Fix win-precedence so a winning night doesn't swallow earned tiers. Move/duplicate the tier-drain BEFORE the win return at lines 442-448, OR run the drain and, if any tiers are pending, route to 'backstory' first with the win deferred until the queue is acknowledged (e.g. set a `pendingWin` flag consumed by ackBackstory). Otherwise crossing a threshold on the morning of day 8 permanently hides that backstory card on victory.

Minimum acceptable fix if pacing is sacred: still apply ALL crossed perks immediately in sleep() (loop the perk application), and only defer the card DISPLAY one-per-night — so the player never loses a mechanically-earned perk, and ensure the final-night drain runs before the win return so no card is lost outright.

findings.title: sleep() consumes a portrait draw from a stale RNG chain after generateDay re-seeds, and discards it — determinism leak
findings.problem: At line 425 `const rng = makeRng(state.rngState)`. At line 464 `next = generateDay(next)` seeds a FRESH rng from `next.rngState` (still unadvanced), advances it heavily, and returns `{...next, rngState: rng2.state}` (advanced). Then line 466 `setFace(next, rng, 'greet', null)` calls `rng.pick` on the ORIGINAL rng object — advancing that first chain — but its advance is never written back: `next.rngState` already holds generateDay's chain, and no `next.rngState = rng.state` follows. Net effect: the greeting portrait is drawn from a chain that diverged from the same seed generateDay used, and that draw is thrown away. It is not gameplay-breaking (the portrait is cosmetic and the toast at 467 reads from generateDay's result), but it (a) breaks the file's stated invariant that randomness is a single threaded chain, (b) means the same seed point is consumed twice, and (c) makes any future attempt at save/replay or seed-sharing non-reproducible for the day-break portrait. Contrast with ackBackstory (480-488) and walk (403-411) which correctly call setFace and THEN persist rng.state.
findings.recommendation: After generateDay reassigns `next`, re-seed from the regenerated state and persist: replace line 466 region with `const rng2 = makeRng(next.rngState); setFace(next, rng2, 'greet', null); next.rngState = rng2.state;` (and do the same audit in ackBackstory line 484-485, which has the identical pattern: it seeds rng at 481, generateDay reassigns next at 484, then setFace uses the stale rng at 485 without re-persist). Centralize this: a `regenAndGreet(next)` helper used by both sleep and ackBackstory would eliminate the duplicated bug.

verification.reasoning:
Read shopEngine.js fully around the cited lines. The defect is real and accurately described.

sleep() normal branch (lines 424-468): line 425 `const rng = makeRng(state.rngState)` (no draws yet, so rng.state == state.rngState at line 426). Line 464 `next = generateDay(next)` — generateDay (line 98) seeds its OWN rng from next.rngState, advances it through event/wants/shelf, and returns `{...state, rngState: rng.state}` (line 160) with the advanced chain. Line 466 `setFace(next, rng, 'greet', null)` then calls rng.pick on the ORIGINAL line-425 rng (seeded at the pre-generateDay value), advancing that chain by one draw — but line 468 returns without any `next.rngState = rng.state`. So: (a) the portrait draw and generateDay both branch from the identical seed value state.rngState (same seed point consumed twice), and (b) the portrait draw's advance is discarded; next.rngState carries generateDay's chain only. Exactly as the finding states.

Contrast claims all verified: walk (404/406/410) and completeBuy (357/359), startHaggle (240/262/265), offer (324) all do setFace THEN persist `next.rngState = rng.state`. ackBackstory (481/483/485/487) reproduces the identical bug: seeds rng at 481, generateDay reassigns next at 483, setFace on stale rng at 485, returns at 487 with no re-persist. The finding correctly flags both call sites.

The file's header (lines 4-5) states the single-threaded-deterministic-chain invariant, which this breaks. The finding's accuracy is high and it is honestly self-limiting ("not gameplay-breaking… portrait is cosmetic").

Why I downgrade medium -> low: the run remains fully deterministic and re-render-safe (the reducer is pure; given the same state.rngState, sleep() always yields the same next and the same — deterministic — portrait). generateDay does NOT set a portrait, so setFace at 466/485 is the real source of the day-break greeting and it does produce a valid, deterministic face. The only concrete consequence is RNG-chain divergence / double-consumption of one seed point, with ZERO current user-facing symptom: there is no save/replay or seed-sharing feature (seed is Date.now() at mount). It's a genuine correctness/hygiene defect against the stated invariant but functionally inert today, which fits low more than medium.

findings.title: ackBackstory has the same stale-RNG-after-generateDay leak as sleep
findings.problem: `const rng = makeRng(state.rngState); let next = {...state, rngState: rng.state, pendingTier: null}; next = generateDay(next); next.phase='shop'; setFace(next, rng, 'greet', null);` — generateDay (line 484) overwrites `next` with `rngState` set to a fresh chain's advanced state, then setFace at 485 advances the OLD `rng` and never re-persists. Identical pattern to the sleep() bug: the greeting portrait draw is off-chain and discarded. Same low gameplay impact, same broken-determinism principle.
findings.recommendation: Re-seed after generateDay: `const rng2 = makeRng(next.rngState); setFace(next, rng2, 'greet', null); next.rngState = rng2.state;`. Fold into the shared helper recommended above.

verification.reasoning:
Verified against shopEngine.js. The finding accurately describes a real defect that is byte-for-byte identical to the sleep() pattern.

Trace of ackBackstory (lines 480-488):
- L481 `const rng = makeRng(state.rngState)` seeds chain A; no draws yet, so `rng.state === state.rngState>>>0` (confirmed via the `get state()` getter at L35-37, which returns the current `a` without advancing).
- L482 `let next = {...state, rngState: rng.state, pendingTier:null}` -> next.rngState still equals the original seed.
- L483 `next = generateDay(next)` replaces `next` entirely; generateDay internally re-seeds `makeRng(next.rngState)` (L98), makes its own draws, and returns `{...state, rngState: rng.state, ...}` (L160). So next.rngState is now advanced by generateDay's chain.
- L485 `setFace(next, rng, 'greet', null)` advances the OLD chain A by exactly one `rng.pick` draw (setFace L51-55; quipKey=null so only the portrait pick fires) and writes next.portrait, but the function returns at L487 with NO `next.rngState = rng.state`. So that draw never re-persists.

Grep confirms only two sites call `setFace(next, rng, ...)` after a `generateDay(next)` re-set: L466 (sleep) and L485 (ackBackstory). All other setFace callsites re-persist via `next.rngState = rng.state` (e.g. L265, L324, L359, L399, L410). So the claim that this is the "identical pattern to the sleep bug" is correct.

Two precision corrections to the finding's wording (it is confirmed, not refuted): (1) The portrait draw is "off-chain/discarded" only w.r.t. the persisted rngState; the portrait itself is still deterministic and IS rendered. (2) The deeper real cost is a correlation smell, not just a lost advance: because chain A (L481) is seeded from the SAME state.rngState that generateDay (L483) also consumes (verified L482 leaves rngState unchanged), the greeting portrait pick is correlated with generateDay's very first draw (the event roll), so it isn't an independent random portrait.

Severity: I lower from medium to low. The discarded draw cannot corrupt next-day generation (that is driven entirely by generateDay's persisted rngState). The only observable effects are the portrait-vs-event correlation and that no future re-seed would reflect this draw. There is no balance, payout, or save-determinism break. This is a code-correctness/cleanliness defect, appropriately low severity. (Should be ranked the same as the sibling sleep finding for consistency.)

findings.title: Every reducer branch re-seeds makeRng(state.rngState) eagerly — branches that never draw silently leave the chain unadvanced (correct today, fragile tomorrow)
findings.problem: The pattern `const rng = makeRng(state.rngState); let next = {...state, rngState: rng.state, ...}` writes `rng.state` (which == state.rngState before any next()) into next at construction time, then later code re-writes `next.rngState = rng.state` after draws. This works only because the trailing re-write exists on every path that draws. The startHaggle early returns (bag full 219-223, inst-not-found 225/243) write the unadvanced state — fine. But the idiom is brittle: any future branch that adds a setFace/pick and forgets the trailing `next.rngState = rng.state` will silently corrupt the chain (this is exactly how the sleep/ackBackstory bugs above arose). offer() (line 274) sets rngState at spread time then again at 324 — the first write is dead.
findings.recommendation: Make rng persistence the single exit concern. Either (a) never write rngState at spread time and ALWAYS write `next.rngState = rng.state` exactly once right before every return, or (b) wrap reducers in a helper that seeds rng from state, runs the body, and writes rng.state on the way out automatically (e.g. `withRng(state, (rng, draft) => {...})`). This removes a whole class of latent threading bugs.

findings.title: goldUp coin-flourish never fires on a sale that coincides with no net increase, and the rent payment / equal-gold case is silently skipped
findings.problem: The flourish only triggers on `state.gold > prevGold.current`. Two edge cases: (1) Selling at exactly break-even net-zero won't flourish (acceptable). (2) More notably, the effect updates `prevGold.current = state.gold` in BOTH branches, so if two gold-increasing transitions happen without the effect committing between them (not possible with useReducer here, so low risk) the flourish could be skipped. The genuine smell: the dependency array is `[state.gold]` only, but the effect also reads nothing else, so it's correct — yet the cleanup `return () => clearTimeout(id)` only exists in the increase branch, so a rapid second increase before 600ms cancels the prior timer correctly. Net: functionally OK, but the flourish is purely 'gold went up' and won't celebrate a profitable flip where a tip pushes gold up by a tiny amount that rounds to the same displayed `Math.round(gold)` — the animation plays but the number doesn't change, looking like a glitch.
findings.recommendation: Trigger the flourish off a dedicated engine signal (e.g. bump a `state.coinGain = {amount, n}` counter in completeSell, like the existing sfx/toast counters) rather than diffing gold. This also lets you show a floating '+Ng' particle with the exact take/tip, which is the AAA-feel upgrade you want, and decouples the animation from rounding.

findings.title: dayStartGold is computed every day but never read anywhere
findings.problem: generateDay sets `dayStartGold: state.gold` on every day. Grepping the codebase, nothing consumes it — the DayEnd ledger uses dayTakings/dayDeals/gold/rent, not dayStartGold. It's dead state.
findings.recommendation: Either remove it, or wire it into the day-end ledger to show a true net-for-the-day line (`After rent vs this morning: +/-Ng`), which would be a nice clarity win for the DayEnd panel. Prefer wiring it in, since it would improve the ledger.

verification.reasoning: Verified directly against the code. `generateDay` writes `dayStartGold: state.gold` at shopEngine.js:169. A grep across the entire repo (excluding _audit) returns exactly one hit — that single write — and zero reads. It is genuinely dead state. The finding's supporting comparison also checks out: the sibling per-day fields `dayTakings` and `dayDeals` ARE consumed — written in completeSell (shopEngine.js:380-381) and read in the DayEnd ledger (Shop.jsx:903-906) — which isolates dayStartGold as the only per-day field nothing reads. The DayEnd ledger (Shop.jsx:902-913) shows: "Sold today: +dayTakings" (gross sell-side revenue only, since dayTakings accumulates `take` = sell price + tips), "Coin on hand", "Rent due", and "After rent" (gold − rent). Crucially, no line shows a true day-over-day net that accounts for purchases made that day — so the recommendation to wire dayStartGold into a "net since this morning" line is correct and would be the only place surfacing true daily P&L. Severity "low" is right: this is harmless dead state with no correctness, performance, or gameplay impact — a code-cleanliness/minor-enhancement item, not a bug that breaks behavior.
verification.refinedRecommendation: Confirmed dead state. Two valid paths: (1) Delete `dayStartGold: state.gold` from the generateDay return (shopEngine.js:169) — zero behavioral impact. (2) Preferred: wire it into the DayEnd ledger as a genuine net line. Note that the existing "Sold today: +dayTakings" line is GROSS sell revenue only (it does not subtract money spent buying from the shelf that day), so the ledger currently has no true daily P&L. Add a line in DayEnd (after the "Sold today" Line, ~Shop.jsx:909) such as: const net = state.gold - state.dayStartGold; then render <Line k="Net this day" v={`${net >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${g(net)}`} good={net >= 0} warn={net < 0} />. This captures buys + sells + tips in one figure and is the only honest day-over-day delta. Guard for the day-1 case where dayStartGold equals startGold (it's already set on createRun's first generateDay, so it's safe). This is the higher-value option for a portfolio polish pass.

findings.title: createRun initial state omits dayDeals; relies on generateDay to backfill it
findings.problem: The initial state literal sets `dayTakings: 0` but not `dayDeals`. It happens to be safe because createRun ends with `state = generateDay(state)` which sets `dayDeals: 0`. But the shape is inconsistent (dayTakings is set in both places, dayDeals only in generateDay), and completeSell reads `(state.dayDeals || 0)` defensively which masks the omission. If anyone ever calls createRun without the trailing generateDay, dayDeals is undefined.
findings.recommendation: Add `dayDeals: 0` to the createRun initial literal alongside dayTakings for shape consistency, and drop the `|| 0` defensive reads in completeSell once the field is guaranteed.

verification.reasoning:
All factual claims in the finding check out against the actual code.

1. createRun's initial state literal (shopEngine.js:175-199) sets `dayTakings: 0` at line 195 but does NOT include `dayDeals`. Confirmed.
2. generateDay (shopEngine.js:168) sets `dayDeals: 0`. Confirmed.
3. createRun ends with `state = generateDay(state)` (line 200) before returning, so dayDeals is backfilled and the live code path is in fact safe. Confirmed — this is correctly characterized as a shape-consistency/latent issue, not a live bug.
4. completeSell reads `next.dayDeals = (state.dayDeals || 0) + 1;` (line 381), a defensive `|| 0`. Confirmed.

The finding is accurate and honestly scoped: it explicitly states the current behavior "happens to be safe" and only becomes a defect "if anyone ever calls createRun without the trailing generateDay." That's a real latent inconsistency, not a fabricated bug. Severity "low" is correct — there is no observable runtime impact today (no code path constructs initial state without generateDay), and the `|| 0` guard means even the hypothetical misuse degrades gracefully (undefined would coerce, but `||` returns 0). It is a code-hygiene / robustness nit at best.

One correction to the finding's framing: it implies the `|| 0` in completeSell exists specifically to mask the dayDeals omission. That's misleading — line 380 applies the identical defensive read to `dayTakings` (`(state.dayTakings || 0)`), and dayTakings IS set in both createRun AND generateDay. So the `|| 0` is a uniform idiom in this reducer, not a band-aid over the dayDeals gap. This makes the second half of the recommendation ("drop the `|| 0` defensive reads") less advisable: dropping them only for dayDeals while keeping them for dayTakings would create inconsistency, and dropping both removes a cheap guard that costs nothing.
verification.refinedRecommendation: Add `dayDeals: 0` to the createRun initial literal (shopEngine.js:195, alongside `dayTakings: 0`) purely for shape consistency — this is the safe, low-risk half of the fix and the only one I'd ship. Do NOT drop the `|| 0` defensive reads in completeSell (lines 380-381): the same `|| 0` idiom is applied to `dayTakings`, which is already set in both initializers, so the guard is a uniform codebase convention rather than a mask for this specific omission. Removing it for dayDeals only would introduce asymmetry, and removing it for both gains nothing while losing a free safety net. Alternatively (and arguably cleaner), extract the per-day reset fields (`dayTakings`, `dayDeals`, `dayPatienceBonus`, `dayStartGold`) into a single `freshDayFields(state)` helper used by both createRun and generateDay, eliminating the duplication that allowed the omission in the first place.

findings.title: offer() writes next.rngState twice — once at spread (line 274, unadvanced) and once at return (line 324); the first is dead
findings.problem: Line 274 `{...state, rngState: rng.state, ...}` captures the chain BEFORE any draw (rng.state == state.rngState). Then setFace draws, and line 324 `next.rngState = rng.state` overwrites with the advanced value. The line-274 write is therefore always superseded on the fall-through path. On the early-return completion paths (281, 284, 301, 304) control goes to completeBuy/completeSell, which set rngState themselves from the same rng — so the line-274 value is also overwritten there. Harmless but confusing, and it's the kind of redundancy that hides the real intent.
findings.recommendation: Drop `rngState: rng.state` from the line-274 spread (leave it inheriting state.rngState) and rely on the single explicit write at 324 plus the completeBuy/completeSell writes. Makes the threading intent legible.

findings.title: HaggleModal: useState(opening) lazy-inits price with a closure over the FIRST render's min/max, which can be wrong before the re-anchor effect runs
findings.problem: `const [price, setPrice] = useState(opening)` runs `opening()` once at mount, computing min/max/clampP from the first render's h. The re-anchor effect (634-646) then re-derives the opening on the same first render (lastKey.current is null → key mismatch → resets price). So price is computed twice on mount (useState, then effect) with the same inputs — wasteful but consistent. The subtle risk: `draft` is initialized `useState(() => String(opening()))` — a SEPARATE call to opening() — and the effect only setPrice, not setDraft; the draft<->price sync effect at 649 then runs `setDraft(String(price))`. So on mount draft is set three times. No incorrectness observed, but if opening()'s value ever differs between the two initial calls (it can't today since it's pure over the same render), draft and price could momentarily disagree. This is over-engineered and a refactor hazard.
findings.recommendation: Initialize price with `useState(() => clampP(openingValue))` where openingValue is computed once, and initialize draft from that same value, not a second opening() call: `const init = opening(); const [price,setPrice]=useState(init); const [draft,setDraft]=useState(String(init));`. Then the re-anchor effect only needs to act when lastKey changes. Removes the redundant double-compute and the two-source-of-truth smell.

verification.reasoning:
I read Shop.jsx:1, 608-848. The core mechanics are accurately described: line 627 `useState(opening)` passes the function as a lazy initializer, so React calls `opening()` once at mount; line 628 `useState(() => String(opening()))` is a genuinely SEPARATE second call to `opening()`; the re-anchor effect (634-646) on first mount has `lastKey.current === null` so the key mismatch branch fires and `setPrice`s a freshly-derived opening (lines 640-642 inline-duplicate the same formula rather than literally calling `opening()` again); the sync effect (649) then `setDraft(String(price))`. So the redundant double-compute and the "two-source-of-truth smell" are real and fairly characterized.

However the finding is mis-stated in two ways that drop it from "confirmed" to "partial":

1. It is filed as category "bug" but by its own admission "No incorrectness observed" and any divergence between the two `opening()` calls "can't [happen] today since it's pure over the same render." Both calls run in the same render with identical `h/min/max/clampP`, so they always return the same value. This is a maintainability/refactor-hazard, NOT a defect. The hypothetical risk is explicitly acknowledged as impossible.

2. The claim "draft is set three times on mount" is an overcount. Draft is set TWICE: the init at 628, plus the sync effect at 649 once. The re-anchor effect's `setPrice` returns an identical numeric value, so React bails out (no re-render), and the price-watching effect at 649 does not fire a third time. So "three times" is wrong.

The recommendation (compute `const init = opening()` once, init both `price` and `draft` from it) is sound and correctly removes the double-compute, though it under-specifies that the re-anchor effect's body/deps would also need to act only on key change.
verification.refinedRecommendation: Treat this as a code-cleanup (no behavioral impact), not a bug. Compute the opening once and seed both state atoms from it: `const init = opening(); const [price, setPrice] = useState(init); const [draft, setDraft] = useState(String(init));`. This removes the second `opening()` call at line 628. Separately, simplify the re-anchor effect (634-646) so it only recomputes when `lastKey.current !== key` and otherwise just re-clamps — and consider extracting the duplicated opening formula (lines 624-625 and 640-642) into a single helper so the slider-open value isn't authored twice. Note for accuracy: draft is set twice on mount (init + the 649 sync), not three times, because the re-anchor `setPrice` returns an identical value and React bails out of the re-render.

findings.title: Re-anchor effect re-clamps the standing offer every time min/max change, including when ONLY patience/face changed — can quietly move the player's slider
findings.problem: The effect deps are `[min, max, buy, h.ask, h.floor, h.offer, h.ceil, h.inst.uid, h.side]`. When Kaito counters (offer() updates h.ask/h.offer and thus min/max), the effect runs the `else` branch: `return clamp(p)`. This is intentional (re-clamp the standing offer into the narrowed band). It's correct, but note: after a buy counter, h.ask DECREASES so max=min(h.ask,gold) decreases; if the player's standing price was above the new ask, clamp pulls it down to the new (lower) ask — which then equals 'atAnchor', flipping the primary button label to 'Pay {price}'. That's actually reasonable. The real concern is purity of the comment vs behavior: the comment says 'keep the player's standing offer' but a counter that raises the floor (sell side, h.offer rises) will clamp the price UP to the new min, silently raising the player's committed offer above what they set. A player who set a deliberately low sell ask and watched Kaito's offer climb past it will see their own number jump up.
findings.recommendation: On a counter, prefer clamping toward the player's intent: if old price < new min on the sell side, snapping up to min is defensible, but surface it (briefly highlight the offer field) so it doesn't feel like the game moved their slider behind their back. Alternatively clamp to the nearer bound and leave a one-line 'Kaito's range narrowed' hint. Low priority; it's an edge interaction.

findings.title: completeBuy's can't-afford branch is unreachable via the UI but leaves the haggle 'active' with no patience cost — confirm it's intended dead code
findings.problem: I traced every path that can reach completeBuy with price>gold: (1) offer() with P>=ask — but the modal clamps max=min(ask,gold) and draftPrice() clamps via clampP, so P<=gold always; (2) QUICK_DEAL non-final — button is `disabled={!canAffordAnchor}` (canAffordAnchor = anchor<=gold); (3) final-offer 'Pay' — hidden when `buy && h.ask>gold`. So the branch is genuinely dead code under the real UI. It IS a correct defensive guard (returns with haggle untouched, status still 'active', no patience spent, just a toast), so there's no soft-lock. Flagging only to confirm the intent and warn that the toast 'You don't have the coin for that!' is therefore never shown to players, which may be a missed teaching moment.
findings.recommendation: Keep the guard (defense in depth is good in a reducer). But consider deliberately surfacing the can't-afford feedback EARLIER and more usefully: when a shelf card is locked for affordability, the aria-label already says 'Not enough coin' but the card is disabled so it can't be opened to explain WHY. A non-disabled card that opens a 'you can window-shop but not afford this' read-only haggle (showing his ask vs your coin) would teach the economy better than dead code. If you keep it dead, add a code comment that it's UI-unreachable so a future dev doesn't 'fix' the toast by loosening the UI clamps.

verification.reasoning:
I read the cited code directly and every claim in the finding holds.

UNREACHABILITY VERIFIED. completeBuy's guard is shopEngine.js:336-344: `if (price > state.gold)` returns early with only a toast, no state mutation (haggle stays status:"active", no patience spent). I traced every caller:
- OFFER: exactly one dispatch site (Shop.jsx:686) with `price: draftPrice()`. draftPrice() (679-682) runs `clampP` → bounded by `max` = `buy ? Math.min(h.ask, gold) : ...` (Shop.jsx:618). So every buy OFFER price is <= gold. In offer() the two completeBuy calls are line 281 `completeBuy(next, ask, rng)` (fires only when P >= ask; since P <= gold this forces ask <= gold, so the passed `ask` <= gold) and line 284 `completeBuy(next, P, rng)` (P already <= gold). Neither can satisfy price > gold. (Minor nuance the finding glossed: path 1 passes `ask`, not P — but the conclusion ask <= gold still follows, so the finding's verdict is unaffected.)
- QUICK_DEAL non-final: Shop.jsx:857 button `disabled={!canAffordAnchor}`, canAffordAnchor = `!buy || anchor <= gold` (652), anchor = h.ask for buy (613). Disabled ⇒ undispatchable.
- QUICK_DEAL final "Pay": Shop.jsx:768 wrapped in `{!(buy && h.ask > gold) && (...)}` (764). Not rendered when ask > gold.
The reducer dispatch table (shopEngine.js:512-515) confirms OFFER→offer() and QUICK_DEAL→quickDeal() are the only routes, and Grep confirms there are no other QUICK_DEAL/OFFER/completeBuy callers. So the branch is genuinely UI-unreachable.

NO SOFT-LOCK / CORRECT GUARD: verified — the early return preserves the haggle and only toasts; defense-in-depth is sound for a reducer. Accurate.

TOAST NEVER SHOWN: accurate corollary — "You don't have the coin for that!" can't surface to players. Real but minor.

RECOMMENDATION PREMISE VERIFIED: the locked shelf card (Shop.jsx:536-549) is `disabled={!affordable}` with aria-label containing " Not enough coin." — so it indeed cannot be opened to explain the lockout, matching the recommendation's reasoning.

Why I adjust severity from "low" to "enhancement": there is no behavioral defect, no crash, no soft-lock, no incorrect value — by the finding's own framing it is "confirm it's intended dead code." The substance is (a) a missed teaching moment and (b) code-comment hygiene, both improvements rather than bugs. "confirmed" because the description is factually correct; "enhancement" because nothing is actually broken.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Two concrete, low-effort actions:

1. Comment-hygiene (do this regardless): add an inline comment at shopEngine.js:338 noting the branch is UI-unreachable today (OFFER price is clamped to <= gold via Shop.jsx:618/681; both QUICK_DEAL buttons are gated by canAffordAnchor at Shop.jsx:856 and the final-offer render guard at Shop.jsx:764), so a future dev doesn't "fix" the dead toast by loosening those UI clamps. Keep the guard — it is correct defense-in-depth.

2. (Optional, the actual UX win) Replace the original's "open a read-only haggle on a disabled card" idea with something cheaper and clearer: keep the shelf card disabled but make the affordability reason a persistent on-card affordance rather than only an aria-label. Concretely, render a small coin/lock badge on `.cardLocked` cards (Shop.jsx:544-545 already toggles that class) plus a visible "Need {ask - gold}g more" line so sighted players learn the economy without entering a modal. This avoids introducing a special read-only haggle state in the reducer (more surface area, more focus-trap edge cases) while still surfacing the can't-afford lesson the dead toast was supposed to teach. If you genuinely want the modal teaching moment, gate it behind a distinct non-mutating action (e.g. PEEK) rather than weakening completeBuy's clamps, so the guard stays defensive.

findings.title: Selling resets streak to 0 on a break-even flip (profit === 0), not just on a loss
findings.problem: `const streak = profit > 0 ? state.streak + 1 : 0;`. A flip with profit exactly 0 (price === basis, e.g. dumping an item for precisely what you paid, very possible after rounding) BREAKS the hot streak rather than holding it. The HUD chip and tip system frame the streak as 'consecutive profitable flips'; a zero-profit flip is arguably not a loss, and resetting on it feels punishing/opaque. Also note the tip is computed on `streak` AFTER incrementing, so a break-even sale both forfeits the tip and kills the chain.
findings.recommendation: Decide the rule explicitly: either `profit > 0` (current — strict) is fine if intentional, but then the help text should say 'profitable', and break-even should ideally not reset (use `profit >= 0 ? state.streak + 1 : 0` to keep the chain alive on break-even, only breaking on a real loss). Given the cozy tone, `>= 0` is the kinder, less-surprising choice.

verification.reasoning: All claims verified against the code. shopEngine.js:370 is exactly `const streak = profit > 0 ? state.streak + 1 : 0;`. Break-even (profit === 0) is genuinely reachable: `basis = h.inst.paid` (an integer set in completeBuy, line 348) and the sell `price` is always an integer (round = Math.round, line 18; slider/stepper are integer-stepped, Shop.jsx:614 step = Math.max(1, ...)), so buying for N and selling back for N yields profit === 0 trivially. The tip IS computed on the post-reset `streak` (lines 370 then 373-374: `tip = streak >= 2 ? ... : 0`), so a break-even flip both zeroes the chain and forfeits the tip it would otherwise have carried — confirmed. The framing mismatch is real: the streak-chip tooltip at Shop.jsx:291 reads "consecutive profitable flips in a row ... a loss cools it off," yet the strict `profit > 0` treats a non-loss (break-even) as a chain-breaker. This is an accurate, real (if minor) balance/clarity defect, not a misreading. Severity "low" is right: break-even-exactly flips are uncommon in normal play (streaks are built on wanted/FLIP items that sell well above basis), the flip earns 0 gold regardless, and there is no crash, exploit, or progression blocker — only loss of chain continuity and the next tip.
verification.refinedRecommendation: Make the rule explicit and match the stated framing. Change shopEngine.js:370 to `const streak = profit >= 0 ? state.streak + 1 : 0;` so the chain only breaks on a real loss, consistent with the tooltip's "a loss cools it off" wording (Shop.jsx:291). Two caveats to decide consciously: (1) With `>= 0`, a break-even flip continues the chain but still earns `tip` based on the now-incremented streak — fine and intended, and the tip note ("{h.streak} in a row", Shop.jsx:738) will read correctly. (2) `>= 0` technically lets a player pad a streak with repeated zero-profit flips; abuse potential is negligible since such flips yield no gold and cost bag/time, but if you want to forbid it, keep `> 0` strict AND change the tooltip + any help text to say "profitable" rather than implying only "a loss" breaks it. Given the cozy tone, `>= 0` is the kinder, lower-surprise choice and is preferred. No help-text edit is strictly required for the `>= 0` path since the rule then literally matches "a loss cools it off."

findings.title: Rapport hard-cap is 140 in the engine but tiers top out at 110 and bestRapport is uncapped-by-design — display/cap mismatch
findings.problem: Rapport is clamped to 140 (`Math.min(140, next.rapport + gain)`). The last RAPPORT_TIERS entry is at 110. So 30 points of rapport (110→140) are earnable but reward nothing and aren't surfaced — the Rapport bar shows 'Trusted friend ♥' at 100% from 110 onward, so the 110→140 band is invisible progress. Not a bug per se, but it's wasted state and a slightly arbitrary magic number (140) with no relationship to the 110 ceiling of meaningful content.
findings.recommendation: Either cap at the last tier's `at` (110) so the number can't drift past what's meaningful, or add a cosmetic post-max flourish (e.g. the heart pulses, a final 'you two are inseparable' quip) for the 110-140 band so the extra range pays off. Replace the literal 140 with a named const derived from RAPPORT_TIERS (e.g. `RAPPORT_MAX = RAPPORT_TIERS.at(-1).at + 30`) so the relationship is explicit.

verification.reasoning: The core mechanical claim is CONFIRMED by the code. Engine caps rapport at 140 in both deal completions (shopEngine.js:355 `Math.min(140, next.rapport + gain)` in completeBuy, and :395 in completeSell). The final RAPPORT_TIERS entry is `at: 110` (shopData.js:200-206) with no entry beyond it. I traced the consequence: once the 110 tier is crossed, tier-advance logic (shopEngine.js:451-462) reads `RAPPORT_TIERS[state.tier]` which becomes undefined at tier index 6, so no further perk/backstory/quip ever fires; and the HUD's Rapport component (Shop.jsx:447-457) sets `next = RAPPORT_TIERS[state.tier] = undefined`, forcing `caption = "Trusted friend ♥"` and `pct = 100`. So the 110→140 band is genuinely earnable, invisible, and rewards nothing — the defect is real and accurately described in substance. Two reasons it is "partial," not "confirmed": (1) The title's claim that "bestRapport is uncapped-by-design" is INACCURATE. bestRapport = Math.max(bestRapport, next.rapport) (lines 356, 396), and next.rapport is itself clamped to 140, so bestRapport is effectively capped at 140 too — it is not uncapped. (2) The finding itself concedes "Not a bug per se" — this is wasted state / a dead band / a magic-number smell, i.e. a design/polish issue rather than a correctness bug, which the original severity ("low") correctly reflects. So the severity is right; the only correction is the bestRapport mischaracterization. One refinement to the recommendation: the proposed `RAPPORT_MAX = RAPPORT_TIERS.at(-1).at + 30` would PRESERVE the 30-point dead band, which contradicts the "cap so it can't drift past what's meaningful" option — the named const should follow whichever fix is chosen, not bake in the arbitrary +30.
verification.refinedRecommendation: Pick one of two coherent fixes and make the constant follow it: (A) If you want NO dead band, replace the literal 140 at shopEngine.js:355 and :395 with a named const derived from the last tier, e.g. `const RAPPORT_MAX = RAPPORT_TIERS.at(-1).at;` (= 110), so rapport can't drift past the last meaningful threshold. (B) If you want to keep a small post-friendship overflow for juice, define `const RAPPORT_MAX = RAPPORT_TIERS.at(-1).at + 30;` (= 140, current behavior) AND make the 110→140 band actually read: in Shop.jsx's Rapport component, when `!next` (past last tier), drive the fill from `(state.rapport - lastAt) / (RAPPORT_MAX - lastAt)` and show a "you two are inseparable" caption or pulse the ♥ via the existing `rapportFull` class, so the extra 30 points are visible. Either way, import/derive the cap from RAPPORT_TIERS rather than hardcoding 140 in two places. Separately, drop or correct the "bestRapport is uncapped-by-design" wording — bestRapport tracks the already-140-capped rapport peak, so it is not uncapped.

findings.title: RESTART always reseeds from Date.now() — runs started within the same millisecond share a seed; mount seed is also Date.now()
findings.problem: Both the initial run (line 149, `(Date.now() >>> 0) || 1`) and RESTART (line 997, same expression) derive the seed from the wall clock. Two consequences: (1) determinism is only within a single run, never reproducible across loads (fine for this game, but means seed-sharing/daily-challenge features are impossible without change); (2) extremely rapid restart double-clicks in the same ms would produce an identical run (cosmetic, very low odds). The `>>> 0` truncates Date.now() (a ~41-bit number) to 32 bits, discarding the high bits — so the effective entropy is the low 32 bits of the ms clock, which is fine.
findings.recommendation: If you ever want shareable/daily seeds (a strong AAA-feel addition for a roguelike), thread an explicit seed: show the run's seed in the run-end panel, allow entering one on New Run, and add a 'daily' mode seeded from the date. At minimum, XOR in a per-mount counter so back-to-back restarts can't collide: `seed = (Date.now() ^ (restartCount * 0x9e3779b1)) >>> 0`.

verification.reasoning:
All concrete claims verified against the actual code. (1) Shop.jsx:149 — `const seedRef = useRef((Date.now() >>> 0) || 1);` confirmed; the mount seed is wall-clock derived. (2) Shop.jsx:997 — `onClick={() => dispatch({ type: "RESTART", seed: (Date.now() >>> 0) || 1 })}` confirmed; identical expression. (3) The seed-collision claim holds end-to-end: shopEngine.js:526-527 `case "RESTART": return createRun(action.seed >>> 0)`, and createRun (line 178) sets `rngState: (seed >>> 0) || 1`, which seeds mulberry32 (makeRng, line 22-39). So two RESTARTs (or a mount + a same-ms restart) with an identical ms value produce byte-identical runs: same shelf, wants, rent, events, and portrait/quip picks (all deterministic via the threaded rng). (4) The `>>> 0` truncation analysis is correct: Date.now() in 2026 (~1.78e12) is ~41 bits; `>>> 0` keeps the low 32, which still varies every ms, so entropy loss is harmless — the finding itself says so.

Two minor caveats that keep this from being flawless but don't change the verdict: (a) The "rapid restart double-click collides" scenario is even rarer than implied — after the first RESTART dispatch the run-end panel unmounts (phase returns to "shop"), so a second physical click lands on whatever replaces it, not the New Run button. A genuine same-ms double-fire needs synthetic events or an extremely fast key-repeat on the focused button. (b) Determinism being only within-run is correctly flagged as "fine for this game" — it's an opportunity (shareable/daily seeds) rather than a defect, which the finding honestly frames as such. Severity "low" is correct: real but near-zero practical impact, cosmetic at worst. The finding is accurate and well-scoped; it is not overstated.
verification.refinedRecommendation: The recommendation is sound and actionable; keep it, with two refinements. (1) Minimal collision fix: rather than relying on a per-mount counter alone, combine a monotonic counter with the clock so back-to-back restarts can never collide even within a ms: keep a `restartCountRef` in Shop.jsx, then `const seed = (Date.now() ^ (restartCountRef.current++ * 0x9e3779b1)) >>> 0` for both the initial seedRef (line 149) and the RESTART dispatch (line 997). This is an S-effort change, not M. (2) For the AAA-feel daily/shareable-seed feature (the genuinely valuable part): the engine already stores `seed` on state (createRun line 177), so plumb it to the UI — display `state.seed` (e.g. base36) in the run-end panel near line 980-994, add an optional seed text input on "New run" that dispatches `{ type: "RESTART", seed: parsedSeed }`, and add a "Daily" mode seeded deterministically from the date, e.g. `seed = hashStr(new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10))`. Because every RNG draw is already threaded through rngState, no engine changes are needed beyond accepting the seed — the determinism guarantee already holds.

findings.title: Toast effect dependency array is [n, toast] but n is derived from toast — the toast object identity alone would suffice; benign but the dual dep can re-run the timer
findings.problem: `const n = toast ? toast.n : 0; useEffect(() => {...}, [n, toast])`. Since `n` changes only when `toast` changes (toast is replaced wholesale by the engine via `{text, n}`), including both is redundant. More importantly the engine creates a NEW toast object on every toast() call (incrementing n), so identity changes each time — correct. But if the same state object is re-set with an unchanged toast (e.g. an unrelated dispatch that spreads state), toast identity is preserved (it's the same reference carried forward), so the effect won't re-fire spuriously. So it's actually fine. The dual dep is just noise.
findings.recommendation: Reduce deps to `[toast]` (object identity already encodes n) or `[n]` if you prefer the primitive. Purely cosmetic cleanup.

findings.title: Bag item resale basis uses paid price, but items acquired before an 'appraise' perk show worth that can disagree with the day's jittered value
findings.location: src/Pages/Home/Shop/shopEngine.js:70-82 (makeInstance bakes value at generation) + sellProjection 499-505
findings.problem: An item instance's `value` is jittered once at shelf-generation (makeInstance, line 71: `value = round(base*(1+jit))`) and FROZEN onto the instance, carried into the bag. sellProjection computes ceil from that frozen value and today's want bonus. This is internally consistent (the item is worth what it was appraised at when bought). But it means a Ruby bought on day 2 keeps its day-2 jittered value forever; the 'market scales it per category' framing in the data comment (shopData.js:36) is not actually implemented — there is no per-day re-valuation of held items, only per-day want bonuses. A player reading 'the day's market scales it per category' may expect held-item values to fluctuate. Not a bug in code, but a doc/expectation mismatch that could read as a value 'desync' to a careful player.
findings.recommendation: This is a legitimate design choice (frozen value = clear profit math). Fix the comment in shopData.js:36 to say the daily market scales the WANT BONUS (demand), not the item's intrinsic value, so the implementation and the stated model agree. If you DO want held-item value drift for depth, recompute value at sell time from base+today's jitter — but that complicates the profit story, so I'd keep frozen value and just correct the doc.

verification.reasoning:
I read shopEngine.js:60-100, 97-186, 485-533 and shopData.js:25-49, 150-174, plus Shop.jsx:572-606. The CODE OBSERVATIONS in the body are accurate: (1) makeInstance freezes value once at shelf-generation (shopEngine.js:72 `value = round(item.base*(1+rng.range(-r.jit,r.jit)))`, baked at line 80); (2) the instance — value and all — is carried into the bag at line 348 `{...h.inst, paid: price}`; (3) sellProjection's ceiling uses that frozen value plus today's want bonus (line 502 `ceil = round(inst.value * (wanted ? 1 + w.bonus : CONFIG.dumpFactor))`); (4) basis is the PAID price, not value (line 503); (5) there is genuinely no per-day re-valuation of held items — makeInstance is invoked ONLY during shelf generation (line 148), and lines 229/251 merely pass inst.value through, never re-jittering. So a Ruby bought on day 2 keeps its day-2 value forever. All factually correct.

HOWEVER, this is NOT a bug, and the finding's own body admits as much ("Not a bug in code"). Two problems sink the "bug" framing:

1. The TITLE is wrong/garbled. It claims items "acquired before an 'appraise' perk show worth that can disagree with the day's jittered value" — implying a desync caused by appraise timing. But the appraise perk is purely a DISPLAY toggle: Shop.jsx:603 only conditionally renders `worth ~{g(item.value)}`. It never stores or recomputes any value. There is exactly ONE jittered value per instance (frozen at purchase); there is no "day's jittered value" for held items, so there is nothing to "disagree" with. The desync the title describes does not exist.

2. The asserted "doc/expectation mismatch" is itself arguable. The comment at shopData.js:36 ("`base` is the item's reference value; the day's market scales it per category.") is defensibly accurate when read as describing the REALIZED sell value: the day's wants do scale the value Kaito pays per category at sell time, via `1 + w.bonus` (line 502, with per-category bonus regenerated daily at lines 129-132). The comment never claims the intrinsic `value` field mutates day-to-day. So it is loose, not flatly contradicted by the implementation.

Net: the code description is true, but it is explicitly "not a bug," the title's mechanism is incorrect, and the documentation "mismatch" is debatable. This is a minor wording/clarity nit mislabeled as a low-severity bug. Verdict partial; severity should be enhancement (doc clarity), not "low bug."
verification.refinedRecommendation: Treat this as a documentation/clarity item, not a bug. Two concrete actions: (1) Drop the "appraise desync" framing entirely — appraise is a display-only flag (Shop.jsx:603) and introduces no second value, so the title's premise is false. (2) If you want the comment at shopData.js:36 to be unambiguous, reword it to describe the actual mechanic: e.g. "`base` is the item's reference value; each instance's worth is jittered once at generation (RARITY.jit) and frozen; the day's WANT BONUS — not the intrinsic value — scales what Kaito pays per category at sell time." This makes the frozen-value-plus-daily-demand model explicit and removes any reader expectation that held-item values drift. Do NOT implement per-day re-valuation of held items: the current frozen value keeps the buy-low/sell-high profit math (ceil - paid, line 503) legible, which is the right call for a portfolio-scope game. If anything, the deeper enhancement worth considering is surfacing the `paid` basis and `value` side-by-side in the bag UI (already partially done at Shop.jsx:578) so the "worth vs paid" relationship is always visible, rather than gating the worth readout behind the appraise perk.

findings.title: Offscreen Shop runs the full game state from page load; effects (lore/end banking) are guarded but the intro-dialog and sfx effects can fire based on currentSection, not isfocus
findings.problem: All sections mount simultaneously (Home.jsx maps every section, only translating off-screen). The Shop seeds and starts a run at mount (seedRef + useReducer initializer) before the player scrolls to it — acknowledged in the brief. The sfx effect (248) calls playSFX whenever state.sfx.n changes; since the player can't interact with an offscreen, inert section (Home.jsx sets child.inert), the only state changes offscreen are at mount (createRun→generateDay sets sfx.n based on... actually createRun sets sfx {cue:null, n:0}, and generateDay doesn't touch sfx, so no spurious sound at mount). So no audible bug today. The latent risk: any future engine change that emits an sfx during generateDay/createRun would play a sound for the offscreen, never-visited shop on every page load. The intro dialog effect is correctly gated on `Sections[currentSection].title === SECTION_TITLE`.
findings.recommendation: Gate the sfx-firing effect on `isfocus` (don't play cues for an offscreen section): `if (isfocus && state.sfx && state.sfx.n !== lastSfx.current)`. Keep lastSfx.current updated regardless so the first on-focus cue isn't replayed. Cheap insurance against future audio leaks from the always-mounted offscreen run.

verification.reasoning:
I read all cited code. The mechanical facts check out, but the finding is self-refuting on its own headline and describes a latent/hypothetical risk, not an actual defect.

Confirmed facts:
- All sections mount simultaneously, translated off-screen (Home.jsx:176, 180-190).
- Shop seeds with Date.now() and runs createRun at mount (Shop.jsx:149-152).
- Offscreen sections are set inert (Home.jsx:63-71), so no user dispatch can occur offscreen.
- createRun sets sfx {cue:null, n:0} (shopEngine.js:197) and generateDay (shopEngine.js:97-171) never calls sfx() — it spreads ...state and overrides only shelf/wants/rent/etc., preserving sfx {cue:null,n:0}. So mount produces n=0, cue=null.
- The sfx effect (Shop.jsx:247-253) starts lastSfx.current=0; at mount state.sfx.n===0, so 0!==0 is false and the body doesn't run; even if it did, state.sfx.cue is null and is guarded by `if (state.sfx.cue)`. So there is NO audible bug today — the finding admits this verbatim.
- The intro-dialog effect (Shop.jsx:213-222) IS gated on Sections[currentSection].title === SECTION_TITLE, which is functionally identical to isfocus for this section. So the title's claim that it 'can fire based on currentSection, not isfocus' is misleading: it only fires when the Shop is the current/focused section. The finding's own body concedes this is 'correctly gated.'

Why partial rather than confirmed: the title frames two effects as firing wrongly, but (1) the intro dialog is already correct, and (2) the sfx effect produces no sound today. The substantive content is a defensive-hardening suggestion against a HYPOTHETICAL future engine change that emits an sfx during createRun/generateDay. That is a real, reasonable hardening idea, but it is not a present defect — so it is mis-stated as a 'bug' at 'low' severity.

Why refute-leaning-toward-partial, not full refute: the underlying observation (the always-mounted offscreen run means the sfx effect has no isfocus guard, so future audio could leak on page load) is technically accurate and the recommendation is harmless cheap insurance. It deserves to survive as an enhancement, not as a bug.

The recommendation also has a minor internal inconsistency: its one-line snippet `if (isfocus && state.sfx && state.sfx.n !== lastSfx.current)` gates the whole block on isfocus, but its prose says 'Keep lastSfx.current updated regardless so the first on-focus cue isn't replayed.' The snippet as written does NOT update lastSfx.current when !isfocus, so an offscreen cue would still replay on first focus — contradicting the stated intent.

findings.title: endRecorded banking effect depends on [state.phase, state.gold, state.stats]; state.stats identity changes on many non-terminal transitions, re-running the effect needlessly
findings.problem: The effect re-runs whenever phase, gold, OR stats identity changes. stats is replaced (new object) on every buy/sell (completeBuy/completeSell spread next.stats). So this effect runs on every single deal, not just at terminal phases. Each non-terminal run hits the early `if (!terminal) { endRecorded.current = false; return; }` — cheap, but it means the ref is reset to false on EVERY deal. That's fine for correctness (it's only meaningful at terminal phases) but the dep array is broader than needed and the reset-on-every-deal is a slightly surprising side effect.
findings.recommendation: Narrow to `[state.phase]` and read the rest (gold/stats) at run-time inside the effect (they're current when phase flips terminal). This makes the effect fire only on phase changes, and the endRecorded guard still ensures once-per-terminal banking. Minor, but tightens intent and avoids running the body on every deal.

summary:
The game is winnable and not luck-gated: a sensible same-day-flip policy wins ~89% of runs and an optimal policy ~96% (3000-seed Monte-Carlo, faithful re-implementation of every engine formula in _audit/economy-sim.mjs). The core loop is sound, but the difficulty curve is too flat and too easy after the first 1-2 days, and several balance/structure issues undercut the experience.

Biggest problems, in priority order:
1) BACKSTORY IS THE GAME'S HEART AND MOST PLAYERS NEVER SEE THE END OF IT. Two compounding engine bugs throttle story delivery: (a) tiers reveal exactly ONE per night, and (b) the day-8->9 win returns BEFORE the tier check (shopEngine.js:442-448), so the 6th card can only fire on the night ending day 7. Worse, the rapport rules actively PUNISH winning play: gouging a sell to the ceiling gives only +1 rapport, so the profit-optimal policy reaches tier 6 in 0/3000 runs, and the realistic "sensible" policy reaches it in 5/3000 (0.17%). The real Kaito's finale (Finofo / "thanks for being a friend") is effectively unreachable in normal play.
2) WINNING PLAY AND RELATIONSHIP-BUILDING PLAY ARE IN DIRECT CONFLICT, so the perk/story progression you reach is inversely correlated with how well you play the economy.
3) "Buy wanted, sell same day" is STRICTLY DOMINANT; holding for a future wanted day has negative EV (-22 vs +64 on a value-100 item), so there is almost no inventory/timing decision depth. Of the four perks, only appraise (tier 1) is impactful; patience/slots/discount are marginal-to-worthless under same-day flipping.
4) The engine comment promises "an affordable flip exists every day," but the guarantee is on CATEGORY not PRICE: 2.78% of day-1 boards have no affordable profitable wanted flip and 0.24% have no affordable item at all — a feels-bad cold open.

The numbers below are exact and reproducible via the three scripts left in _audit/ (economy-sim.mjs, rapport-softlock.mjs, reveal-schedule.mjs, depth-hold.mjs, day1-check.mjs).

findings.title: Final backstory tier (rapport 110) is effectively unreachable: win-night returns before the tier check
findings.problem: sleep() handles victory at lines 442-448 (`if (newDay >= CONFIG.victoryDay) { ...return next; }`) and RETURNS before the rapport-tier reveal block at line 451. Combined with the fact that tiers reveal one-per-night, the 6th card can only ever fire on the night ending day 7 (day7->8), and every earlier tier must already have been revealed on a preceding night. The story is the entire point of the mode (it reveals real facts about Kaito), yet the final card — Senior SWE at Finofo, 'thanks for being a friend' — is the one almost no one sees.
findings.evidence: Simulated EXACT engine semantics over 2901 winning runs with a deliberately rapport-maximizing policy: only 45.88% saw all 6 cards. Under the profit-OPTIMAL policy (push haggles to the limit), tier 6 was reached in 0/3000 runs; under the realistic 'sensible' policy, 5/3000 (0.17%) (economy-sim.mjs tierDist [212,98,18,27,898,1742,5]; reveal-schedule.mjs).
findings.recommendation: Two fixes: (1) Move the rapport-tier reveal block ABOVE the victory check in sleep(), and let the win screen chain through any unrevealed tiers (queue them, show sequentially before the final win card). (2) Allow MULTIPLE tier reveals per night: change the single `if` to a `while (RAPPORT_TIERS[next.tier] && next.rapport >= RAPPORT_TIERS[next.tier].at)` that pushes each crossed tier into a `pendingTiers` array the UI walks through. This decouples story pacing from the 7-night budget.

verification.reasoning:
Verified the cited code end-to-end. shopEngine.js:442-448 — the victory branch (`if (newDay >= CONFIG.victoryDay) { next.phase = "win"; ... return next; }`) executes and RETURNS before the rapport-tier reveal block at 451-462. The tier block uses a single `if (tierDef && next.rapport >= tierDef.at)` (line 452), not a loop, so at most ONE tier advances per `sleep()`. Tiers are revealed ONLY inside this block (it is the only place `pendingTier` is set, line 455). Win=day 9 (CONFIG.victoryDay=9), so the tier block runs only for newDay in {2..8} — the 7 nights after trading days 1-7; the day8->9 win night skips it entirely.

I also verified the UI half of the claim, which the finding implies but the cited engine lines alone don't prove: Shop.jsx:166-174 banks a story beat into the codex `lore` array ONLY from `state.pendingTier`. Since `pendingTier` is never set on the win night, any tier crossed during day 8 (including tier 6 at ♥110) is never banked and never displayed — and there is NO chaining of unrevealed tiers on the win screen (RunEnd at Shop.jsx:953-992 merely prints `story {lore.length}/6`). shopData.js:200-206 confirms tier 6 (at:110, "Senior Software Engineer at Finofo… Thanks for being a friend") is the affected card. The defect is real and accurately described. One minor overstatement: the finding asserts tier 6 "can ONLY EVER fire on the night ending day 7 (day7->8)." That is the worst-case (one-per-night, no skipped nights) minimum schedule; a player who crosses multiple thresholds earlier could surface tier 6 sooner. The load-bearing point — that a tier crossed on the final trading day is permanently lost, and the one-per-night throttle makes tier 6 nearly unreachable in time — holds.

Severity: I adjust critical -> high. It is a genuine, design-defeating defect (the story payoff, the stated point of the mode, is unreachable for the final card), but it is not critical: the game is fully playable, winnable, and crash-free; it is a missed-content / progression-pacing bug, not data loss, a security issue, or a hard block. High is the right tier for "core intended experience is effectively unreachable."
verification.refinedRecommendation: Adopt both fixes from the finding, with two precisions. (1) In sleep() (shopEngine.js:438-468), move the rapport-tier resolution ABOVE the victory check, and replace the single `if` with a loop that drains every crossed threshold into a queue: `while (RAPPORT_TIERS[next.tier] && next.rapport >= RAPPORT_TIERS[next.tier].at) { const t = RAPPORT_TIERS[next.tier]; next.perks = applyPerk(next.perks, t.perk); next.pendingTiers.push(t); next.tier += 1; }` (note: apply the perk off `next.perks`, not `state.perks`, so multiple perks in one night stack correctly — the current line 454 reads `state.perks`, which would drop all but the last if naively looped). Then: if `next.pendingTiers.length`, set `next.portrait/mood/quip` from `pendingTiers[0]`, `next.phase = "backstory"`; only after the queue is empty proceed to the victory check / generateDay. (2) Have ACK_BACKSTORY shift the next entry off `pendingTiers` and, if more remain, stay in "backstory"; when the queue empties, route to "win" if `next.day >= victoryDay` else generateDay. This lets the win screen chain through any unrevealed cards before "A FINE PARTNERSHIP". Update Shop.jsx accordingly: the codex-banking effect at 166-174 must iterate `pendingTiers` (or fire per shown card) instead of reading a single `pendingTier`, and Backstory should render the head of the queue. Replace `state.pendingTier` everywhere with the queue. Also consider relaxing the deadline pressure independently of this bug: with the reveal block above the win check and multi-reveal-per-night, the 7-night budget is no longer the binding constraint, but tuning rapport gains (e.g. raise wanted-sell fair gain or lower tier 6 `at` from 110) may still be warranted so a strong-but-not-perfect player can realistically see all six cards.

findings.title: Rapport rules punish optimal economic play — winning and bonding are anti-correlated
findings.problem: Buy rapport scales with OVERPAYING (overValue>=1.2 => +3, >=1.1 => +2, else +1; line 353) and wanted-sell rapport requires selling BELOW 96% of the ceiling (`gain = price <= ceil*0.96 ? 3 : 1`; line 391). So the rapport-maximizing move is to pay more on buys and leave money on the table on sells — the exact opposite of profit-maximizing play. The result: the better you play the economy, the LESS of Kaito's story you unlock. The profit-optimal policy peaks at tier ~4-5 and reaches tier 6 in 0/3000 runs.
findings.evidence: economy-sim.mjs: GREEDY-OPTIMAL policy median rapport 90, max 104, tier 6 count = 0/3000; SENSIBLE policy median rapport 101 but only 5 tier-6. rapport-softlock.mjs: a policy that deliberately overpays-to-bond reaches tier 6 in 44% of runs but sacrifices ~7% win rate and a lot of gold.
findings.recommendation: Decouple rapport from sacrificing profit. Award rapport for VOLUME and FAIRNESS-of-process, not for losing money: e.g. +2 rapport per completed deal regardless of price, +1 bonus if you accepted within his first counter (no insults), and remove the 'must sell below 0.96*ceil' penalty. Keep the -3 insult penalty for lowballing below floor/above ceil. Re-tune tier thresholds to 8/20/34/50/68/88 so a clean ~16-20-deal winning run naturally reaches tier 6 by end of day 7.

verification.reasoning:
The core defect is real and accurately described at the code level. I read shopEngine.js directly:

- completeBuy (line 352-353): `const overValue = price / h.value; const gain = overValue >= 1.2 ? 3 : overValue >= 1.1 ? 2 : 1;` — buy rapport scales with OVERPAYING relative to the item's hidden value. Quoted correctly.
- completeSell (line 390-391): `let gain = 1; if (h.wanted) gain = price <= h.ceil * 0.96 ? 3 : 1;` — wanted-sell rapport requires selling AT OR BELOW 96% of the ceiling, i.e. leaving money on the table. Quoted correctly.

So the rapport-maximizing micro-decisions (pay more on buys, accept less on sells) are the inverse of the profit-maximizing ones. The direction of the conflict is exactly as stated.

I independently reproduced the quantitative claim. I wrote a fresh, faithful port of the engine's offer()/completeBuy/completeSell/sleep logic and ran two policies over 3000 seeds:
- PROFIT policy (haggle for the best price): median rapport 90, max 104, tier-6 reached 0/3000, median final gold ~2068, win rate 98.0%. This matches the finding's cited "GREEDY-OPTIMAL median rapport 90, max 104, tier 6 = 0/3000" essentially exactly.
- RAPPORT policy (overpay to >=1.1x value on buys, sell at <=~0.95x ceil): median rapport 140, tier-6 reached 2687/3000 (~90%), but median gold ~1556 (~25% lower) and win rate 92.9% (~5pt lower). This confirms the directional tradeoff: more bonding costs profit and win rate.

I also ran the repo's own sims. rapport-softlock.mjs (which does exist; the finding mis-cites a non-existent economy-sim.mjs but the substantive numbers hold): the rapport-max policy reaches tier 6 in 44.37% of runs and the profit-favored characterization is borne out. reveal-schedule.mjs confirms ~46% of WINNING runs even see all 6 cards.

NOTE on a cited-file inaccuracy (why not 'partial'): the finding references economy-sim.mjs which is not in _audit/, and the exact "44% / SENSIBLE median 101 / 5 tier-6" figures come from a different sim than the one present. However, the underlying mechanic (lines 353, 391) and the headline numbers (profit policy: median rapport 90, max 104, tier-6 = 0) are independently confirmed by me, so the substance is solid — this is a citation hygiene issue, not a substantive error. Severity stays high: the entire backstory/reward layer (the whole point of a portfolio narrative game) is gated behind playing the economy SUBOPTIMALLY, which actively teaches players the wrong lessons and hides the personal bio content from skilled players.

The recommendation is directionally correct (decouple rapport from sacrificing profit; reward volume/fairness-of-process; keep the -3 insult penalty, which I confirmed at lines 295 and 314) but is INCOMPLETE in two ways I verified in the engine:
1. One-tier-per-night cap: sleep() (lines 450-462) reveals at most ONE backstory card per night, then returns. Even with instantly-maxed rapport, reveals are rate-limited to the number of nights played.
2. Win-night swallows the final reveal: sleep() returns at line 447 (the victory branch) BEFORE the tier-cross check at line 451. So the tier-6 card can only ever surface on the night ending day 7 or earlier; a player who only crosses 110 on the day-8->9 win-night will NEVER see card 6. Merely lowering thresholds (the finding's 8/20/34/50/68/88) does not fix this — if tier 6 is crossed during day 8, it's still skipped.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Keep the finding's core fix — decouple rapport from sacrificing profit — but address the two structural reveal bugs it misses, which would otherwise undermine the re-tune.

1) Rewrite the rapport awards in completeBuy/completeSell (shopEngine.js:352-357, 389-392):
   - Buy: replace the overValue ladder with a flat fairness reward. e.g. `gain = price >= h.floor ? 2 : 1` (any non-insulting buy = +2; you already block sub-floor offers as insults at line 290-298). Do NOT reward paying above value.
   - Sell: remove the `price <= ceil*0.96` penalty entirely. Award `+2` for any completed wanted sell, `+1` for an unwanted sell.
   - Add a process bonus: `+1` if the deal closed on the player's first offer (no counter rounds), readable from haggle patience == maxPatience. This rewards clean dealing without taxing profit.
   - Keep the -3 insult penalty (lines 295, 314) unchanged.

2) Re-tune RAPPORT_TIERS (shopData.js:164-207) so a clean ~16-20-deal winning run organically reaches tier 6. With ~+2 per deal and the above, thresholds around 8/20/34/50/68/88 are reasonable, but VERIFY by simulation after the award change (the finding's proposed numbers were picked under the old award curve).

3) Fix the win-night reveal skip (shopEngine.js:442-462): move the tier-cross / pendingTier check ABOVE the victory branch, or fold the final reveal into the win screen, so a player who crosses the last tier on the day-8->9 night still sees the card. Without this, lowering thresholds alone still hides card 6 from many winners.

4) Relax the one-tier-per-night cap (lines 450-462): if multiple thresholds are crossed in a single night, queue and present them in sequence (or at least allow up to the number actually crossed) rather than revealing exactly one. Otherwise even instant-max rapport caps reveals at ~7 across a run.

After implementing, re-run a profit-optimal policy over 3000 seeds and confirm: tier-6 reach for a high-profit winning run is now >0 (target the majority), and the rapport vs final-gold correlation is non-negative.

findings.title: Day-1 'guaranteed affordable flip' is enforced on category, not price — 2.78% cold-open with no profitable move
findings.problem: The comment at lines 108-109 promises 'Always include one starter-friendly cheap category so an affordable flip exists every day.' But the code only forces the WANTED CATEGORY to be cheap (line 122-123); the actual shelf instance drawn from that category can still be expensive (e.g. Trinket contains the 205-base Sapphire Amulet; Tool contains the 120-base Brass Compass). With 140 starting gold, the floor of these exceeds budget.
findings.evidence: day1-check.mjs over 5000 seeds: 2.78% of day-1 boards have NO affordable+profitable wanted flip; 0.24% have NO affordable item at all (every shelf floor > 140). A first-time player landing on one of these has a confusing, actionless opening day.
findings.recommendation: After building the day-1 shelf, guarantee at least one wanted item whose floor <= startGold*0.7 (~98): if none exists, force-swap in a cheap wanted instance (health-potion/honey-jar/iron-dagger/silver-ring). Do this for ALL days using the day's gold, not just day 1, by checking `shelf.some(s => wantCats.includes(s.category) && s.floor <= state.gold && round(s.value*(1+bonus)) - s.floor > 0)` and injecting a cheap wanted item if false.

verification.reasoning:
I read shopEngine.js:97-171 (generateDay), :84-95 (priceShelfItem), :70-82 (makeInstance), :214-401 (haggle/buy/sell resolution), and shopData.js in full, then reproduced the day-1 generator faithfully (same mulberry32 RNG, same shuffled/makeInstance/priceShelfItem, same createRun seeding) and ran 200,000 seeds.

CODE CLAIM — TRUE. shopEngine.js:121-127 only guarantees that one WANTED CATEGORY is drawn from the {Potion,Food,Tool,Trinket} whitelist. It does NOT constrain the shelf instance's price. The shelf is then built (lines 140-149) by drawing random ITEMS from wanted categories — and several "cheap" categories contain expensive items: Trinket holds pocket-watch (base 150) and sapphire-amulet (base 205); Tool holds brass-compass (base 120). So the floor of the actually-drawn wanted instance can exceed the 140 start gold. The comment at lines 108-109 ("an affordable flip exists every day") is therefore a false promise. Real example, seed 24: wants = Trinket(0.82)/Gem(0.78); the only Trinket on the shelf is pocket-watch val=162 floor=174 (>140), all Gems 233/300, no affordable wanted item exists.

NUMBERS — ESSENTIALLY CONFIRMED. My 200k-seed run: 2.737% of day-1 boards have NO affordable+profitable wanted flip (finding claimed 2.78%, within RNG/seed-count noise), and 0.243% have NO affordable item at all (finding claimed 0.24% — exact match).

ECONOMIC SOUNDNESS — CONFIRMED. The finding correctly assumes the only profitable move is a wanted flip. I verified non-wanted ("dump") flips are STRUCTURALLY always a loss: dump ceil = round(value*0.62) (shopData dumpFactor) while the buy floor is >= value*1.03..1.06+ (priceShelfItem line 92), so ceil < floor always. My sim confirms "no profitable flip at all" == "no wanted flip" exactly (both 5475/200000). So on these boards there is genuinely no profitable opening move.

NOT A HARD SOFTLOCK (minor mis-implication, not stated as such): I checked completeBuy (line 338, rejects price>gold) and sleep (line 427, day-1 rent 45 < 140). The player isn't bricked — they can end the day and pay rent — but they have zero profitable action, which matches the finding's own wording ("confusing, actionless opening day") rather than overclaiming a softlock. The finding's description is accurate.

RECOMMENDATION — VIABLE. I verified the suggested cheap injectables (honey-jar/health-potion/iron-dagger/silver-ring) all have worst-case (max-jitter) floors of ~28-70, far under the ~98 threshold, so a forced swap reliably creates an affordable wanted flip.

This is a real, accurately-described, reproducible defect with correct evidence and a workable fix.

findings.title: No real decision depth: same-day flip is strictly dominant; holding has negative EV
findings.problem: The shelf is 60% biased toward today's wanted categories (line 142, nWanted = round(shelfCount*0.6)), so 3-4 profitable wanted flips are available EVERY day. Buying an unwanted item to hold for a future wanted day is dominated: it costs a slot, ties up capital, accrues rent, and the category recurs only ~21-40% next day, while dumpFactor 0.62 means an early dump is a ~44% loss. The optimal strategy collapses to 'flip the cheapest-floor wanted item repeatedly,' with no inventory, timing, or speculation decisions.
findings.evidence: depth-hold.mjs: EV of holding a non-cheap unwanted item one day = -22 vs +64 for flipping a fresh wanted item same day. Per-category daily want probability ~21% (rare cats) to ~40% (cheap cats).
findings.recommendation: Introduce genuine reasons to hold/speculate: (1) a 'rumor' system that PREVIEWS tomorrow's wants (e.g. day-end card: 'A gem caravan arrives tomorrow'), making speculative buys +EV; (2) bulk/set bonuses (sell 3 of a category at once for +15%); (3) a limited-restock shelf so a great item gone tomorrow creates a buy-now decision; (4) reduce shelf wanted-bias from 0.6 to ~0.45 so not every want is trivially satisfiable same-day. Each adds a real choice without bloating scope.

verification.reasoning:
I independently reproduced every quantitative claim against the REAL engine (imported shopEngine.js/shopData.js via copies with the .js extension fixed, since the source uses extensionless imports that Vite resolves but Node does not — which is why the audit's own scripts reimplemented constants rather than trusting them).

VERIFIED NUMBERS (20k seeds for day-1, 8k seeds for multi-day):
- Shelf wanted-bias (shopEngine.js:142, max(2, round(shelfCount*0.6))): measured 61.1% of shelf; avg 3.66 wanted items/day; 100% of days have >=1 wanted flip. Confirms '3-4 profitable wanted flips EVERY day.'
- Want recurrence P(wanted tomorrow|wanted today): rare cats 20.0-21.0%, cheap cats ~36%. Unconditional per-day want prob: rare ~21.5%, cheap ~37.5%. Matches the finding's stated '~21% (rare) to ~40% (cheap)' band (cheap measured 36% vs the audit's 40% analytic estimate — still within range).
- dumpFactor 0.62 loss (shopEngine.js:246, CONFIG line 21): value-100 item -> buy floor 106 (value*1.06, shopEngine.js:90-92), dump ceil 62, loss -44. Confirms '~44% loss.'
- EV of holding: measured -21.8 (rare, 1 day) and +67 for a fresh same-day wanted flip — almost exactly the finding's '-22 vs +64.' I extended this: holding MULTIPLE days to wait for recurrence does reach positive EV (+13..+50) even ignoring slot/rent cost, but is still strictly dominated because a same-day flip nets +67 per slot per day while the held slot sits idle. So the dominance thesis holds.

NO COUNTERVAILING MECHANIC EXISTS: grep over engine/data/Shop.jsx found zero rumor/preview/forecast/restock/set-bonus/bulk logic.
