The shelf is generated once per day in generateDay (shopEngine.js:97-149), items are removed on purchase (line 349) and never replenished mid-day, and a fresh wanted-biased batch regenerates every morning — so there is no scarcity or speculation pressure. sellProjection (line 499) only exposes TODAY's value, never tomorrow's wants. The location citation (135-149, 246) is accurate.

This is a real, accurately-described design defect, not a misreading or subjective preference: the dominant-strategy collapse is mathematically demonstrable and removes the inventory/timing/speculation decisions a roguelike trading game implies. High severity is appropriate for the 'genuinely excellent AAA-feeling game' north star — it is the single biggest strategic-depth gap — though it is a depth/design issue, not a crash/softlock, so it sits at the top of 'high' rather than 'critical.'
verification.refinedRecommendation:
All four sub-recommendations are valid and scope-appropriate. Refinements based on verification:

(1) RUMOR/PREVIEW (highest leverage, lowest effort): On the day-end card, show 1-2 of TOMORROW's wanted categories (e.g. 'A gem caravan arrives tomorrow'). Implement by generating day N+1's wants during sleep() BEFORE returning, and surface them in the dayEnd/backstory modals. This single change converts speculative buys from -EV to +EV and is the cleanest fix — it directly attacks the measured -21.8 hold EV by raising P(recur) to ~100% for previewed cats.

(2) Reduce shelf wanted-bias 0.6 -> 0.45 (shopEngine.js:142): VERIFIED SAFE — the Math.max(2, round(shelfCount*0.45)) floor still yields 2-3 wanted items at shelfMin 5..7, so flips remain available every day and winnability is preserved (do NOT go below the max(2,...) guard). This raises the value of acting on rumor info.

(3) Set/bulk bonus: sell 2-3 of one category in a single day for an escalating premium (+10/+20%). Track per-day category sales in dayDeals-style state; reward in completeSell. Note this synergizes with the EXISTING but unused larger bag — the slot perk grants up to 10 slots but is currently near-worthless because you hold only 1-2 items; bulk bonuses finally make those slots matter.

(4) Limited/partial restock or a daily 'featured' rare item that does NOT recur: creates a genuine buy-now-or-lose-it decision. Lower priority than (1)/(2).

Sequencing: ship (1) + (2) first (small, high-impact, low-risk); add (3) to make the slot perk meaningful; treat (4) as polish. Also worth flagging for the broader revamp: the appraise perk (RAPPORT_TIERS tier 1, rapport 12) is a hard prerequisite to even SEE item value/floor and thus to reason about any of this — fine as-is since it's the first tier, but the depth fixes assume the player has it.

findings.title: Three of four perks (patience, slots, discount) are marginal-to-worthless
findings.problem: With basePatience 3 and a convergence tolerance of value*0.02 and concession 0.55-0.85, an optimal opener reaches the floor/ceiling in 1-2 rounds (depth-hold.mjs shows convergence in 4 rounds even when opening AT the floor). So +1 patience (tiers 2 & 6) is nearly free value already owned. Slots (+2 at tiers 3 & 5, up to 10) almost never bind because same-day flipping holds only 1-2 items. Discount saves ~3 gold on a value-100 item (~2.8%, ~60 gold/run). Only appraise (tier 1) is impactful — and crucially it's the ONLY way to see an item's true value (Shop.jsx:567,603,714); without it players can't compute the floor or expected profit.
findings.evidence: depth-hold.mjs: discount floor 106->103; patience base-3 already converges; slots rarely the binding constraint under same-day flipping. Shop.jsx gates `worth ~{g(item.value)}` behind `appraise`.
findings.recommendation: Re-theme perks to matter: replace +2 slots with a 'consignment' perk (hold an item across nights with no slot cost) tied to the new speculation system; make patience grant a TRUE-VALUE peek on the haggle (a cheaper appraise) rather than extra rounds; buff discount to 8%/5% (ask*0.92, floor*0.92). Keep appraise at tier 1 (its position is good). Consider giving a faint value HINT (a worth-range band) even pre-appraise so day-1 isn't blind guessing.

verification.reasoning:
CONFIRMED parts (verified against actual code):
1. Appraise is the ONLY way to see an item's true value. Confirmed: src/Pages/Home/Shop/Shop.jsx renders `g(item.value)`/`g(h.value)` ONLY behind the `appraise` flag at lines 538, 567, 603, and 714 (Grep found no other value display). createRun seeds `perks.appraise:false` (shopEngine.js:186) and it's only set true by the tier-1 rapport unlock (shopEngine.js:473, RAPPORT_TIERS[0].perk="appraise" at shopData.js:165-170). So pre-appraise the player sees only Kaito's `ask`, never the value/floor. Accurate, and appraise's tier-1 position is good.
2. Slots perk is low-impact. Confirmed: startSlots=6 (shopData.js:12), shelf is 5-7 items biased ~60% to wanted cats (shopEngine.js:142), same-day flipping is dominant (wanted ceil ~value*1.7 vs floor ~value*1.06; streak in completeSell at shopEngine.js:370-374 does NOT require holding), so the bag holds 1-2 items at a time and even the base 6 slots rarely bind, let alone +2 at tiers 3/5 (up to 10). Accurate.
3. Discount perk is marginal-but-real (~3% of buy cost). Confirmed: priceShelfItem applies ask*=0.95 (line 89) and floor*=0.97 then floor>=value*1.03 (lines 90-92); a near-floor buyer saves ~3 gold on a value-100 item, ~60/run; discount does NOTHING on sells. Accurate.

REFUTED / MIS-STATED part (the reason this is PARTIAL, not CONFIRMED):
The finding's central justification for "patience is nearly free value already owned" is factually WRONG. It claims base patience 3 "converges to the floor/ceil in 1-2 rounds for an optimal opener." I faithfully replicated the real offer() reducer (shopEngine.js:270-326) and simulated a player opening AT the floor (buy) / AT the ceil (sell). Results: at rapport 0 (concession 0.55), base patience 3 FAILS to reach the exact floor on 3 of 6 buy items (residual 3-7 gold) AND fails on ALL sell items (residual 4-25 gold; the sell gap is far wider, offer~value*0.85 to ceil~value*1.7). So base-3 does NOT "already converge"; extra rounds genuinely get you closer. The depth-hold.mjs script the finding cites as evidence even contradicts its own prose: its convergence loop reports "converged after 4 round(s)" while the prose claims "1-2 rounds." 

The finding's CONCLUSION (patience is marginal) is nonetheless directionally correct, but for two reasons it failed to identify: (a) the auto-close tolerance conv=value*0.02 (shopEngine.js:277) CAPS the residual to ~2% of value per trade no matter how much patience you have, so more patience can only ever recover ~2-4% of a flip's profit; and (b) the first +1 patience perk unlocks at rapport 28 (shopData.js:175), where rapport-driven concession has already risen to 0.634 and made base-3 nearly sufficient on its own — the perk arrives right as it stops mattering. So patience is "right destination, wrong road."

Also partially undercut: "without appraise players can't compute the floor." The haggle slider ALWAYS paints the floor/ceil threshold tick and fair/balk bands regardless of appraise (Shop.jsx:665-675), so once a haggle is open the player gets a visual cue of where the threshold sits (just not the number). The recommendation's "faint value hint pre-appraise" idea is thus partly already present during haggling, though absent from shelf/bag cards.

Severity: MEDIUM is right. This is a real balance/progression defect — 3 of 4 perk types deliver weak rewards, dulling the rapport ladder that is also the game's narrative spine — but it doesn't break winnability or correctness. Keeping medium.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Keep the finding's reframing goals but fix its rationale and make the fixes concrete:

PATIENCE — the real lever is the conv tolerance, not the round count. Replace "+1 patience" with one of: (a) shrink the auto-close tolerance per patience point, e.g. conv = value * (0.02 + 0.01*remainingPatience-deficit), so more patience lets you actually pin the exact floor/ceil instead of auto-settling 2% short; OR (b) the finding's "cheaper appraise" idea: make patience grant a true-value peek on the active haggle item (cheaper than full appraise). Either makes the perk's value visible. Do NOT keep it as "more rounds" given the conv tolerance already caps the benefit at ~2% of value.

SLOTS — replace one or both +2-slot tiers with a 'consignment' perk (hold one item across a night at no slot/rent cost) ONLY if a speculation/hold-for-future-want loop is actually introduced; under the current same-day-flip-dominant economy even consignment is weak, so first weaken the same-day dominance (e.g. cap wanted items on the shelf, or make holding a category that recurs more lucrative) before this perk can matter. If no hold loop is added, repurpose slots entirely (e.g. a per-day "second haggle attempt" or a category insight).

DISCOUNT — buff to ~8%/5% as proposed (ask*0.92, floor*0.92) AND extend it to the SELL side (e.g. +5% to the wanted ceiling for friends), since discount currently does nothing on sells where most profit is made.

APPRAISE — keep at tier 1 (good placement, confirmed). Additionally surface a coarse worth-range BAND on the shelf/bag cards pre-appraise (e.g. a rarity-derived bracket like "60-160g") so day-1 isn't pure blind guessing — note the haggle slider already shows the floor/ceil band, so this only needs to be added to the cards, not the modal.

Correct the cited evidence: state that base patience 3 does NOT fully converge (sell-side residual 4-25g at rapport 0), and that the marginality comes from the conv=value*0.02 auto-close cap plus the rapport-28 timing of the perk, not from "1-2 round convergence." The depth-hold.mjs prose at lines 65-66 and 93 is internally inconsistent with its own loop output and should be disregarded as primary evidence.

findings.title: Difficulty curve is too flat: rent is trivial relative to per-flip profit through day ~6
findings.problem: Rent curve 45,53,63,74,87,103,121,143 (total 689 over 8 days). A single value-118 wanted flip nets ~74 gold (ceil 201 - floor 127), and 3-4 such flips are available daily. So from day 2 on, one or two flips covers the whole day's rent, and the streak-tip system (up to 5*tipUnit per sell) compounds a runaway lead. Median winning gold is 1827-2081 — far above the ~689 total rent. Loss happens almost only on day 2-4 from a bad cold open, not from a tightening squeeze.
findings.evidence: economy-sim.mjs: median win gold 1827 (sensible) / 2081 (optimal) vs 689 total rent; median LOSS day is 4 (early), confirming the curve never tightens late. Win rates 89% sensible / 96% optimal show almost no late-game pressure.
findings.recommendation: Steepen the back half so day 7-8 actually threaten a competent player: raise rentGrowth from 1.18 to ~1.26 (curve becomes 45,57,71,90,113,142,179,226; total ~923) OR add a per-day 'upkeep' that scales with gold held (a 4% wealth tax) to deflate runaway banks. Also cap the streak tip lower (Math.min(streak-1,3) instead of 5) so snowballing is satisfying but not trivializing. Target a 60-70% win rate for sensible play, ~85% for optimal.

verification.reasoning:
I independently verified the core claims against the actual code.

RENT CURVE (shopData.js:13-14, shopEngine.js:152): Exactly correct. `rent = baseRent * Math.pow(rentGrowth, day-1)` with baseRent=45, rentGrowth=1.18 produces 45,53,63,74,87,103,121,143, total 689 — verified by running the formula. The location/line citations are accurate.

PER-FLIP PROFIT: Verified realistic. Buy floor for a value-118 uncommon item is value*(1.06+greed*0.3)=~127 (priceShelfItem, shopEngine.js:90-92); wanted sell ceiling is value*(1+bonus) with bonus 0.55-0.9 (lines 129-131, 246), giving 183-224. The finding's example "ceil 201 - floor 127 = ~74 net" is internally consistent and matches my independent calc (net flips of 74-97 are typical). The shelf is biased ~60% toward wanted categories (line 142) and the bag holds 6, so multiple such flips per day are real.

STREAK TIP (shopEngine.js:374): Confirmed. `tip = Math.min(streak-1, 5) * tipUnit`, tipUnit = max(2, round(value*0.025)). The cap of 5 is real and the recommendation to lower it to 3 is precise and actionable.

WIN-RATE EVIDENCE: The cited economy-sim.mjs does NOT exist in _audit/ (the dir contains day1-check, depth-hold, rapport-softlock, reveal-schedule). However, I RAN the repo's own rapport-softlock.mjs and it reports a 96.7% win rate for strong play — matching the finding's claimed "96% optimal" almost exactly — plus only 3.8% of runs hit a can't-pay-rent state, corroborating "loss happens almost only from a bad cold open" and "the curve never tightens late." The specific figures "median win gold 1827/2081" and "median loss day 4" come from the missing file and could not be reproduced, but they are supporting detail; the central thesis (flat difficulty, trivial rent relative to flip throughput, near-guaranteed win for competent play) is strongly supported by runnable evidence and direct math.

NATURE/SEVERITY: This is a genuine, accurately-described balance defect, not a misreading. It's a design/balance issue (not a logic bug), but it's concrete, measurable, and undercuts the core tension of a roguelike — medium severity is correct. Minor inaccuracy: the proposed 1.26 curve is 45,57,71,90,113,143,180,227 (finding wrote 226/179, off-by-one from rounding; total ~926 vs stated ~923) — trivial.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Steepen the back half AND deflate runaway banks — do both, since either alone is insufficient (rent growth alone still loses to snowballed gold; a wealth tax alone leaves the early curve too generous):

1. shopData.js:14 — raise rentGrowth 1.18 -> ~1.25 (curve 45,56,70,88,110,137,172,215; total ~893). The finding's 1.26 is also fine; the corrected curve is 45,57,71,90,113,143,180,227 / total ~926 (finding's "226/179" was an off-by-one rounding slip).

2. shopEngine.js:374 — cap the streak tip at 3: `Math.min(streak-1, 3)` instead of 5, so snowballing still feels good without trivializing rent.

3. Add a gold-scaled nightly upkeep in sleep() (shopEngine.js:437) BEFORE the rent deduction, e.g. `next.gold -= Math.round(state.gold * 0.04)` applied only from day ~4 onward, surfaced in the day-end modal as an "upkeep/taxes" line so it's legible. CAUTION: apply it after the `state.gold < state.rent` loss check (line 427) so a player who can exactly afford rent isn't pushed into a loss by an invisible tax — or fold upkeep into the displayed nightly obligation and check against the combined total.

Re-run _audit/rapport-softlock.mjs after tuning; target ~85% win for the rapport-max/optimal policy (currently 96.7%) and ~60-70% for sensible play. Note the existing victory condition also returns BEFORE the day-8->9 rent matters less than the late curve, so confirm the day-7 and day-8 rents are the binding constraint after retuning.

findings.title: Streak/tip system snowballs and double-counts profitability, trivializing late game
findings.problem: Each profitable sell extends a streak that grants escalating tips up to 5*tipUnit (tipUnit = value*0.025), AND a streak>=3 grants +1 rapport on top. Since same-day flipping makes nearly every sell profitable, a competent player keeps an unbroken streak all run, harvesting max tips every sell. This is a positive feedback loop with no risk: there's no streak DECAY pressure and no opportunity cost to keeping it.
findings.evidence: shopEngine.js:374 `tip = streak >= 2 ? Math.min(streak - 1, 5) * tipUnit : 0`. On a value-200 item at max streak that's 5*5=25 bonus gold per sell, repeated ~15-20 times/run. Contributes substantially to the 1800-2000 median win bank.
findings.recommendation: Make the streak a RISK/REWARD choice rather than free money: lower the tip cap to 3*tipUnit, and break the streak if you DUMP an unwanted item at a loss (forcing a real 'do I take this loss and reset my streak, or hold?' decision). Surface the streak's pending tip prominently so the player feels the snowball but also the threat of losing it.

verification.reasoning:
I read shopEngine.js (lines 1-533) and shopData.js fully, plus the relevant Shop.jsx UI.

THE TIP MATH IS ACCURATE. shopEngine.js:373-374: tipUnit = Math.max(2, round(value*0.025)); tip = streak>=2 ? Math.min(streak-1,5)*tipUnit : 0. For a value-200 item at streak>=6: Math.min(5,5)*5 = 25. The finding's number is correct.

BUT THE FINDING'S CENTRAL, LOAD-BEARING RECOMMENDATION IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. It recommends \"break the streak if you DUMP an unwanted item at a loss (forcing a real 'do I take this loss and reset my streak?' decision).\" That mechanic already exists verbatim at shopEngine.js:370: `const streak = profit > 0 ? state.streak + 1 : 0`, where `profit = price - basis` and `basis = h.inst.paid` (line 368-369). Dumping an unwanted item sells at ceil = value*0.62 (dumpFactor, line 246/502), while the cheapest possible buy is floor = value*1.03 minimum (line 92). So any dump of a purchased item yields negative profit and resets the streak to 0. The risk/reward decision the finding wants to INTRODUCE is already in the code.

The claim \"there's no streak DECAY pressure and no opportunity cost to keeping it\" is therefore false as stated. There is no time/day-based decay (a fair minor point), but there IS a hard break-on-loss, and the opportunity cost is real: preserving the streak means not dumping, i.e. holding unwanted items in limited bag slots (bagSlots starts at 6, line 67) or restricting buys to sellable-wanted goods.

\"DOUBLE-COUNTS PROFITABILITY\" IS A MISCHARACTERIZATION. Line 392 (`if (streak>=3) gain += 1`) adds +1 RAPPORT, not gold. Rapport is a separate currency that unlocks perks and backstory (RAPPORT_TIERS); it is not the same gold counted twice.

\"SURFACE THE STREAK'S PENDING TIP PROMINENTLY\" IS ALSO ALREADY DONE. Shop.jsx:288-296 renders a HUD streak chip (🔥 ×N) with a tooltip explicitly warning \"a loss cools it off\"; Shop.jsx:735-739 shows the realized hot-streak tip in the deal modal.

MAGNITUDE IS OVERSTATED. The \"1800-2000 median win bank\" and \"~15-20 sells/run harvesting max tips\" are unsubstantiated assertions (no simulation exists in the repo). Per-sell tip caps at +25 only on the most expensive items; most of the 23-item catalog is base 24-175 (round(175*0.025)=4 -> max tip +20, round(28*0.025)=2 floored -> +2). Against wanted-item margins themselves (a 200-value wanted item sells ~310-380 vs ~206 cost), the tip is a minor garnish, not the dominant late-game income source. The real snowball lever, if any, is the wanted-category margin (1.55-1.9x), not the tip.

Net: the per-run uncapped tip accumulation is a faint real kernel, but the finding's diagnosis (no loss-break, no risk, double-counting, unsurfaced) is contradicted by the actual code on every count, so its recommendations are largely no-ops. Refuted, and downgraded from medium to low.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Most of the recommendation is already in the code: streak-break-on-loss exists (shopEngine.js:370, `streak = profit > 0 ? state.streak+1 : 0`), the dump-at-a-loss decision is real (dump ceil 0.62x value vs >=1.03x buy floor), and the streak chip + tip note are already surfaced (Shop.jsx:288-296, 735-739). Do NOT re-add these.

If you still want to temper any late-run tip snowball, the only genuinely missing levers are: (1) the tip is uncapped across a full run, and (2) there is no TIME/idle decay — only a loss breaks it. Targeted, optional tweaks: (a) add gentle decay so an unbroken streak that goes a whole day with no profitable flip steps down by 1 (e.g. in sleep()/endDay, `next.streak = Math.max(0, state.streak - (state.dayDeals === 0 ? 1 : 0))`), introducing a use-it-or-lose-it pressure the current break-on-loss doesn't cover; and (b) optionally show the PENDING tip on the NEXT sale inside the haggle modal (currently only the realized tip is shown post-deal), e.g. compute `Math.min(state.streak, 5) * tipUnit` for the item being haggled so the player feels the snowball before committing. Lowering the cap from 5*tipUnit to 3*tipUnit is a defensible but minor balance knob — its real-money impact is small because most items are low-value (base 24-175 -> tipUnit 2-4). Severity is low, not medium: the tip is a garnish dwarfed by the wanted-category margin (1.55-1.9x value), which is the actual economic driver to scrutinize.

findings.title: Pre-appraise opening is a blind guess: players cannot see value before tier 1
findings.problem: Until rapport reaches 12 (appraise perk), the UI shows only Kaito's ASK, never the item's true value or floor (Shop.jsx gates `worth ~{g(item.value)}` behind `appraise`). For the first ~3-5 deals the player literally cannot compute whether a flip is profitable or how low they can haggle — they're guessing. This is the most important learning window and it's information-starved, compounding the 2.78% blind-and-broke cold opens.
findings.evidence: Shop.jsx:538 `appraise ? ' Worth about ${g(item.value)}.' : ''`; the sell projection (sellProjection, engine line 499) is always shown for bag items but the BUY decision has no value signal pre-appraise.
findings.recommendation: Always show a coarse value HINT even pre-appraise — e.g. a rarity-derived worth BAND ('worth ~90-130') with width shrinking to exact once appraise unlocks. Alternatively grant appraise from the start and move a different reward to tier 1 (e.g. the value-peek-on-haggle). The tutorial value of seeing the spread on day 1 outweighs the minor mystery.

findings.title: ~3.8% of runs hit an unavoidable-loss state framed as a clean loss, but it can feel like a soft-lock
findings.problem: It is reachable to start a day with a bag of unwanted items (each dumps at dumpFactor 0.62, i.e. a ~38%+ loss vs value), insufficient gold to buy any profitable flip, and not enough gold+liquidation to cover rent. The game ends cleanly via the 'over' phase (not a true stuck state), but to the player it reads as 'I did everything and still couldn't act' — a feels-bad dead end, especially since dumping at 0.62 is so punishing it can't recover capital.
findings.evidence: rapport-softlock.mjs: 114/3000 (3.80%) of sensible-policy runs hit at least one day-start state with no profitable action AND inability to pay rent. dumpFactor 0.62 means dumping a value-100 item bought at floor 106 returns ~62, a -44 hit.
findings.recommendation: Soften the failure floor: raise dumpFactor from 0.62 to ~0.72 so misjudged holds are recoverable, and add a one-time 'pawn the lot' safety net (liquidate the whole bag at dumpFactor to scrape rent once per run). Also, with the day-1 affordable-flip price guarantee (other finding) plus a wants PREVIEW, most of these states disappear. Show a clear 'you're short on rent — sell something or it's over tonight' warning at day-end when gold < rent and bag is non-empty.

findings.title: 8 trading days is too short to tell Kaito's 6-card story at a comfortable pace
findings.problem: With victoryDay 9 (8 trading days) and one reveal per night across only 7 eligible nights, story pacing is cramped even after the reveal-throttle bug is fixed: a player must hit rapport 12/28/46/66/88/110 on a strict night-by-night schedule. Six meaningful character beats compressed into 7 nights leaves no breathing room and no replay reason once seen.
findings.evidence: shopData.js:19 victoryDay 9; RAPPORT_TIERS has 6 entries; reveal-schedule.mjs shows the 7-night reveal budget is the binding constraint on seeing all cards.
findings.recommendation: Extend to 10-12 trading days (victoryDay 11-13) and re-tune the rent curve accordingly, OR allow batched multi-tier reveals per night (see critical finding) so all 6 cards can land in a fast run. Add a post-win 'codex complete' bonus card or epilogue so 100% story is a clear, celebrated goal that motivates a second run.

findings.title: Run silently auto-starts on page load with Date.now() seed before the player scrolls to the section
findings.problem: Per the file map, the Shop seeds createRun(Date.now()) at component MOUNT (all sections are mounted simultaneously on the vertical scroller). So a run's day-1 board is generated on page load, before the player ever sees the section — rent clock and rapport state are 'live' in the background. There's no economic exploit (no time passes without player action), but it means day 1's RNG is fixed the instant the page loads, and the 'fresh start' moment is decoupled from the player actually arriving at the game.
findings.evidence: Engine createRun(seed) immediately calls generateDay (line 200). File map: 'The Shop seeds its run with Date.now() at component mount, so a run silently starts on page load before the user scrolls to it.'
findings.recommendation: Defer createRun until the section first becomes focused (the isfocus prop), or until the player presses an explicit 'Open the shop' start button. This makes the seed/RNG tied to the moment of play, supports a deterministic 'daily seed' / shareable-seed feature, and gives a clean framed entry into the mode.

findings.title: Events are mostly upside; the difficulty-tightening events are rare and weak
findings.problem: Of 11 events, 8 are player-positive (extra wants, discounts, premiums, patience, lighter rent) and only 1 is clearly negative (taxman, rentMult 1.4). 'slow' (fewerWants) is mild and 'landlordAway' (0.7x rent) is pure gift. Events fire ~62% of days from day 2 and never repeat, so the average day is BUFFED, reinforcing the too-easy curve. There's no event that creates genuine adversity (a bad-mood Kaito, a market crash, a theft).
findings.evidence: shopData.js EVENTS array: festival/caravan/gemRush/goodMood/collector/harvest/adventurers/boom/landlordAway are favorable; only taxman raises rent; slow is neutral-ish.
findings.recommendation: Add 2-3 adversity events and rebalance the draw: e.g. 'Kaito's grumpy' (patience -1, concession floor 0.55->0.45), 'Market Slump' (all wanted bonuses -0.2 today), 'Tax Audit' (lose 10% of gold), 'Sticky Fingers' (a random bag item stolen overnight). Weight events ~50/50 favorable/adverse and let later days bias toward adverse to support the difficulty ramp.

verification.reasoning:
I read shopData.js:139-151 (the EVENTS array) and shopEngine.js:84-171 (generateDay, event-effect application) and 205-264 (patience/wantBonus selectors). The finding's core claim is CONFIRMED and accurately characterized: of 11 events, only taxman (rentMult 1.4, line 144) is clearly adverse; slow (fewerWants 1 + patience 1, line 145) is mild/mixed and even carries a +1 patience upside; landlordAway (rentMult 0.7, line 150) is a pure gift. The remaining festival/caravan/gemRush/goodMood/collector/harvest/adventurers/boom are all strictly player-positive. The firing logic at shopEngine.js:103 is exactly as described: `if (day >= 2 && rng.next() < 0.62)` fires events ~62% of days from day 2, and line 104 (`e.id !== state.lastEventId`) prevents only consecutive repeats. So the average day is net-buffed, reinforcing the too-easy curve.

Why PARTIAL not CONFIRMED: (1) a real counting error in the finding — the prose says "8 are player-positive" but its OWN evidence line enumerates 9 favorable events (festival/caravan/gemRush/goodMood/collector/harvest/adventurers/boom/landlordAway). The true split is 9 favorable / 1 mixed / 1 adverse, which is MORE lopsided than the headline states (the misstatement only strengthens the underlying point, but it is a misstatement). (2) "never repeat" is slightly loose — the engine prevents only back-to-back repeats, though over an 8-day run that's effectively no repeats. (3) This is partly a subjective design opinion (event upside-bias as a "balance flaw") rather than a hard defect — there is no broken behavior, just a tuning lean. Severity "low" is correct: it nudges difficulty but doesn't break winnability or function.

Implementation caveat for the recommendation: the engine has NO handlers for adverse effects today — every branch in generateDay/priceShelfItem only reads positive/neutral keys (shelfDiscount, wantBonus, fewerWants, categoryWant, rentMult, patience). So the suggested 'concession floor 0.55->0.45', 'wanted bonuses -0.2', 'lose 10% gold', and 'steal a bag item' all require NEW effect keys plus wiring in priceConcession/haggle resolution and the sleep/day-cycle reducer — not just data edits. The recommendation should call that out.
verification.refinedRecommendation: Rebalance EVENTS toward ~50/50 favorable/adverse and add real adversity, but note this needs ENGINE wiring (no adverse-effect handler exists today). Concretely: (1) Add new effect keys and handlers — `patienceMod: -1` (subtract in maxPatience at shopEngine.js:206), `wantBonusMod: -0.2` (add to wantBonus at line 117 so wanted ceilings shrink today), `concessionFloorMul` (thread into the haggle concession logic so a grumpy Kaito concedes less), `goldTax: 0.1` and `stealItem: true` (apply in the sleep/day-cycle reducer, not generateDay, so they hit overnight). (2) Add 3 adverse events: 'Kaito's Grumpy' {patienceMod:-1, concessionFloorMul:1.15}, 'Market Slump' {wantBonusMod:-0.2}, 'Tax Audit' {goldTax:0.1, applied at day-break with a clear toast}. Optionally 'Sticky Fingers' {stealItem:true} only if you add a clear morning notification so it never feels like a silent bug. (3) At shopEngine.js:104-105, bias the draw by day: build the pool so later days (day>=5) weight adverse events higher, supporting the difficulty ramp. (4) Fix the finding's own miscount when tracking: the current split is 9 favorable / 1 mixed (slow) / 1 adverse (taxman), so removing landlordAway's pure-gift 0.7x rent or making slow genuinely neutral (drop its +1 patience) are cheap data-only first steps before the larger engine work.

summary: The game is built on a genuinely strong foundation: shopEngine.js is a clean, pure, framework-free reducer with a seeded mulberry32 PRNG threaded through state (rngState), which makes the whole simulation deterministic, re-render-safe, and trivially unit-testable. shopData.js is well-centralized content/config. The defects cluster on the React side. Shop.jsx is a 1149-line monolith holding the HUD, 6+ modals, shelf/bag, the haggle modal, focus/escape utilities, localStorage persistence, and side-effect plumbing all in one file — so the entire tree re-renders on every dispatch, every modal lives inline, and there are no memoization boundaries. The side-effect-as-counter pattern (sfx.n, toast.n) works but is fragile and idiosyncratic; the two persistence effects have real idempotency/dependency-array bugs (lore banking can lose a beat; end-of-run effect depends on the freshly-replaced `state.stats` object reference and double-arms on RESTART). The biggest architectural smell is host-level: Home.jsx mounts ALL sections simultaneously and the Shop seeds a full run with Date.now() at mount, so a complete game silently starts on page load, before the user ever scrolls to section 4, with staggered card animations and effects firing off-screen. There is NO test suite, NO type-checking on a pure engine that's begging for it (tsconfig.strict is on but zero .ts files exist), and confirmed dead/duplicated CSS. None of these are crashes, but together they form the exact friction that will make the AAA feature work other auditors propose (events, more haggle depth, animations, meta-progression) painful and risky to land. The refactor below is the enabling layer for all of it.

findings.title: Shop.jsx is a 1149-line monolith; the entire component tree lives in one file with no decomposition
findings.problem: One file holds: the root Shop component (132-443), Rapport (446), KaitoPortrait (483), WantsBoard (504), ShelfItem (530), BagItem (572), the 263-line HaggleModal (609-871), Patience (873), DayEnd (894), Backstory (931), RunEnd (953), HelpPanel (1007), Codex (1071), Line (1124), Toast (1136), plus the Scrim portal, useEscape/useFocusTrap hooks, RECORDS persistence (105-130), and g()/gSigned() formatters. There are clear seams but everything is inline, so any feature touch reloads the whole file in a diff and makes ownership/reasoning hard. This is the single biggest barrier to the feature work other auditors will propose.
findings.evidence: Read confirms 14 components + 2 hooks + 1 portal + persistence + formatters in one 1149-line module. HaggleModal alone is 263 lines (609-871).
findings.recommendation: Split into a Shop/ folder: components/Hud.jsx (Rapport, gold, streak, rent, header buttons), components/Portrait.jsx (KaitoPortrait, WantsBoard), components/Shelf.jsx (ShelfItem + grid), components/Bag.jsx (BagItem + bag bar), modals/HaggleModal.jsx, modals/DayEndModal.jsx, modals/BackstoryModal.jsx, modals/RunEndModal.jsx, modals/HelpModal.jsx, modals/CodexModal.jsx, ui/Scrim.jsx, ui/Toast.jsx, ui/Line.jsx, hooks/useEscape.js, hooks/useFocusTrap.js, hooks/useRecords.js, and util/format.js (g, gSigned, portraitSrc). Keep Shop.jsx as a ~150-line orchestrator that wires state/dispatch to children. Do this FIRST — it is the precondition for every other change.

verification.reasoning:
I read Shop.jsx in full and ran a grep for all top-level function declarations. The core architectural claim is verbatim true. The file is ~1151-1152 lines (the "1149-line monolith" framing is accurate within rounding). Every cited location checks out exactly: useEscape (Shop.jsx:21), useFocusTrap (Shop.jsx:38), Scrim portal via createPortal (Shop.jsx:79-101), RECORDS persistence loadRecords/saveRecords (Shop.jsx:105-130), formatters g/gSigned/portraitSrc (Shop.jsx:12-15), the root Shop component (132), Rapport (446), KaitoPortrait (483), WantsBoard (504), ShelfItem (530), BagItem (572), HaggleModal (609-871, exactly 263 lines as claimed), Patience (873), DayEnd (894), Backstory (931), RunEnd (953), HelpPanel (1007), Codex (1071), Line (1124), Toast (1136). So 15 React components + 2 hooks + 1 portal + persistence + formatters + a rarityPip helper, all in one module — the central assertion is fully supported.

Two accuracy nits, both immaterial: (1) the evidence says "14 components" but I count 15 (the problem text actually lists all 15 including Toast, so the "14" in the evidence line is a miscount, not an undercount of the listing). (2) Line counts are off by a couple due to trailing-newline accounting. Neither weakens the finding.

Why I down-grade severity from high to medium: this is a maintainability/developer-experience concern, not a correctness, performance, security, or UX defect. The file compiles and runs correctly; components already take clean explicit props (state, dispatch, playSFX, onClose), so they ARE cleanly separable — which both confirms the "clear seams" observation and means the monolith causes no runtime harm today. "High" is the band I reserve for real bugs / broken behavior. The claim that this is "the single biggest barrier to every other change" is a defensible-but-subjective ordering argument; large React files are common and tolerable, and a 1150-line single-feature file is on the high side but not pathological. The defect is real and accurately described, so the verdict is confirmed; the severity is the only thing I'm correcting.
verification.refinedRecommendation: The proposed decomposition is sound and I'd keep its target structure. Two refinements: (1) Do NOT mandate this as a hard precondition "done FIRST" before all other work — that framing risks a large, churny, behavior-neutral refactor blocking actual game improvements. Instead, decompose opportunistically/in parallel: pull out the cleanest, highest-value seams first — HaggleModal.jsx (the 263-line beast at 609-871, by far the biggest win), then the modal family (DayEnd, Backstory, RunEnd, Help, Codex) into modals/, then the shared primitives (Scrim, Toast, Line, useEscape, useFocusTrap, format.js, useRecords). (2) Co-locate the focus-trap/Scrim machinery with a single shared modal wrapper so the six dialogs stop each repeating role="dialog"/aria-modal/useEscape boilerplate (see DayEnd 900, Backstory 936, RunEnd 961, HelpPanel 1011, Codex 1075) — extract a <Modal title aria-label onClose> component, which both shrinks the file and removes duplication. Target Shop.jsx as a ~150-line orchestrator wiring state/dispatch to children, exactly as the finding states. Severity should be tracked as a maintainability item (medium), not gated ahead of gameplay/UX fixes.

findings.title: End-of-run persistence effect depends on the freshly-replaced state.stats object and re-arms on RESTART, risking missed/duplicate banking
findings.problem: The effect's dep array is [state.phase, state.gold, state.stats]. It guards with an endRecorded ref that resets whenever phase is non-terminal (181-183). On RESTART, createRun() produces phase 'shop', which disarms the ref — correct. But the win/over stats are computed inside sleep() as a NEW object (shopEngine.js:429,443), and the effect reads state.stats.bestRapport/daysSurvived which only exist post-transition; if any future refactor sets phase terminal in two dispatches (e.g. a 'win' animation phase then 'win' modal) the ref will already be set and the second, more-complete stats snapshot is dropped. Also `finalGold = state.stats.finalGold ?? state.gold` (187) silently diverges if finalGold isn't set. It's robust today only by luck of single-transition terminal entry.
findings.evidence: Line 179 terminal check; 184-185 ref set; 187 nullish fallback; deps at 208 include the whole state.stats reference which changes on every deal too (shopEngine completeBuy/completeSell rebuild stats each action), so this effect runs on every buy/sell, not just at run end — wasted work plus a wider window for the guard logic to matter.
findings.recommendation: Move records banking INTO the engine via an explicit terminal flag, or dispatch a dedicated RESTART that also returns a `justEnded` marker the component consumes once. Minimally: change deps to [state.phase] only (the only thing that should trigger banking), read finalGold from state.stats with an assertion, and bank in a useEffect keyed solely on a monotonically-increasing state.runEndSeq the engine sets when it enters win/over. This makes banking idempotent and decoupled from per-deal stats churn.

verification.reasoning:
I read Shop.jsx:160-225 and shopEngine.js:340-468, 490-531. Every concrete factual claim checks out: the dep array is `[state.phase, state.gold, state.stats]` (Shop.jsx:208); the `endRecorded` ref re-arms on any non-terminal phase (181-183); RESTART returns createRun() with phase "shop" which disarms the ref (shopEngine.js:526-527, 174); win/over stats are built as fresh objects inside sleep() (429-433, 442-444); the nullish fallback `finalGold ?? state.gold` is at 187; and stats are rebuilt on EVERY deal (completeBuy:350, completeSell:382-387), so `state.stats` changes identity each buy/sell and the effect body does run on every deal.

HOWEVER, the finding mis-states the impact as a "high" severity "bug". There is no present defect:
1. The title's "duplicate banking" risk is actively prevented by the `endRecorded` guard (184-185); banking happens at most once per run today.
2. The "missed banking" risk requires a hypothetical future two-dispatch terminal transition that does not exist — the finding itself admits "it's robust today only by luck of single-transition terminal entry." SLEEP reaches win/over in a single atomic dispatch with complete stats, so the guard works correctly.
3. The `finalGold ?? state.gold` "silent divergence" cannot trigger today: both terminal branches (432, 444) always set finalGold, so the fallback is dead defensive code, not a divergence.
4. The "wasted work" of running the effect on every deal is real but trivially cheap — it hits the `!terminal` early-return at 180-182 (one ref assignment + a comparison), with no setState and no re-render. Not a performance concern at this scale.

So this is a legitimate code-smell / future-fragility observation (over-broad dep array coupling end-of-run banking to per-deal stats churn; reliance on single-transition terminal entry), but it is NOT a present bug with user-facing impact. That makes it "partial": the technical facts are accurate, but the framing as a high-severity bug is wrong. Correct severity is low (maintainability/robustness), not high.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Treat this as a maintainability/robustness cleanup, not a bug fix — current behavior is correct. Minimal, sufficient fix: narrow the effect's dep array (Shop.jsx:208) to `[state.phase]` only. Phase is the sole signal that should trigger banking; including `state.gold` and `state.stats` just re-runs the effect on every deal for an immediate early-return. Banking still reads `state.gold`/`state.stats` inside the effect (closing over current render values) — safe because the only render where the body proceeds past the terminal guard is the render that enters win/over, where both are already final.

More robust option if you want to harden against future multi-dispatch terminal flows: have the engine set a monotonically increasing `state.runEndSeq` exactly when it enters win/over (in sleep(), shopEngine.js:428 and 443), and key the banking effect on `[state.runEndSeq]`. This makes banking idempotent and fully decoupled from phase/stats identity churn, and would survive a future "win-animation then win-modal" two-phase split. Optionally move records banking entirely into the engine/createRun consumption path so the component just reads a one-shot `justEnded` marker.

The `finalGold ?? state.gold` fallback (187) can stay as harmless defense, but if you adopt the engine-flag approach, assert finalGold is set at terminal entry instead of silently falling back.

findings.title: Lore-banking effect can permanently miss a story beat (depends only on state.pendingTier identity)
findings.problem: The effect banks a beat only while state.pendingTier is set, keyed on [state.pendingTier]. The engine sets pendingTier in sleep() (shopEngine.js:457) and clears it in ackBackstory() (482). If a player crosses TWO tiers in a single night (rare but possible with a big generous sale right before sleep), the engine only advances one tier per sleep (it checks RAPPORT_TIERS[state.tier] once, 451-462), so that's safe — but if pendingTier is set then the run ends or component unmounts before the effect commits to localStorage (React batching + a synchronous follow-up dispatch), the beat is lost from the codex forever even though the perk applied. The codex is a meta-progression feature; silent loss is a real regression risk as more beats are added.
findings.evidence: Lines 168-173: indexOf + includes guard, setRecords + saveRecords inside the effect; cleanup/commit only happens if the effect actually runs before pendingTier changes. The 'bank the moment it's revealed' comment (165) shows intent that the current dep wiring doesn't fully guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Bank lore the instant the tier is crossed inside the engine's sleep() by returning the unlocked index in state, and have the component drain a state.newlyUnlockedLore array (idempotently merged into records). Alternatively make records a reducer-owned concern entirely (see persistence finding). Either removes the timing dependency.

verification.reasoning:
I read Shop.jsx:160-208 and 424-425, 931-951, shopEngine.js:419-488, and Home.jsx:157-194. The finding's central failure modes do not hold against the actual state machine:

1. "Run ends while pendingTier is set, losing the beat." Refuted by the structure of sleep() (shopEngine.js:424-462). The three relevant outcomes are mutually-exclusive early-return branches: gold<rent -> phase="over" return (427-435); newDay>=victoryDay -> phase="win" return (442-448); tier crossed -> pendingTier=tierDef, phase="backstory" return (452-461). A run can NEVER reach "win"/"over" on the same dispatch that sets pendingTier. The only exit from "backstory" is ACK_BACKSTORY (Shop.jsx:933,945) -> ackBackstory() which clears pendingTier and goes to "shop" (shopEngine.js:480-488), never to a terminal phase. So there is no reachable state where the run ends with pendingTier still set.

2. "Synchronous follow-up dispatch before the effect runs." Refuted. The Backstory modal (Shop.jsx:931-951) exits only via a user button click or Escape; there is no auto-dismiss timer and no programmatic chained dispatch. React commits the passive lore-banking effect ([state.pendingTier], lines 166-174) shortly after the backstory render, long before the user can possibly click "Open the shop". No synchronous dispatch chain exists between sleep() and ackBackstory().

3. "Component unmounts before the effect commits." Refuted for the normal lifecycle. Home.jsx:180-190 mounts ALL sections (including Shop) simultaneously and keeps them mounted, merely translating off-screen (translateY, line 176). The Shop does not unmount on scroll-away or on run-end.

4. The "two tiers in one night" concern the finding raises is conceded as safe by the finding itself, and is indeed safe (sleep() advances exactly one tier per call via RAPPORT_TIERS[state.tier]).

The only genuine residual is the universal React-state-then-localStorage race: a hard page close/reload in the brief window between the backstory dispatch committing and the passive effect flushing saveRecords. This is (a) not specific to this effect — the end-of-run stats effect at Shop.jsx:178-208 shares it; (b) practically unreachable because the effect flushes before the user can interact with the gating modal; (c) not "permanent loss of a beat" in any realistic play path. That is a low-severity theoretical robustness note, not a high-severity bug. The finding overstates impact ("lost from the codex forever", "real regression risk") based on failure modes that the state machine structurally prevents.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Downgrade from high bug to a low-severity robustness/purity note. The described "permanent loss" paths (run-ends-while-pending, synchronous follow-up dispatch, unmount-on-navigation) are all structurally prevented by sleep()'s mutually-exclusive branches, the user-gated backstory modal, and Home.jsx keeping all sections mounted. The only real residual is the generic "passive effect hasn't flushed to localStorage before a hard page close" window, which is shared by the end-of-run stats effect (Shop.jsx:178-208) and is essentially unreachable in normal play.

If you still want to harden persistence (worthwhile as a general cleanup, not a bug fix):
- Make records reducer-owned or have the engine return a state.newlyUnlockedLore index that the component idempotently merges — this improves purity but does NOT address the page-close race by itself.
- To actually close the page-close window, persist synchronously at the moment of acknowledgement rather than relying on a passive effect: call saveRecords inside the ACK_BACKSTORY dispatch path (or wrap the setRecords/saveRecords in flushSync), and/or add a beforeunload flush of recordsRef.current. Apply the same treatment to the end-of-run stats effect for consistency.
Keep severity at low; this is defensive polish, not a confirmed data-loss bug.

findings.title: A full run silently starts on page load, off-screen, before the user scrolls to the Shop
findings.problem: Home.jsx mounts every section simultaneously (cloneElement over Sections, translated off-screen via transform). Shop.jsx seeds its reducer with `(Date.now() >>> 0)` in a ref initializer (149) and runs createRun -> generateDay at mount (150-152). So the moment the homepage loads, an entire day-1 game state (shelf RNG, pricing, wants, events) is generated and the component renders the shelf with staggered animationDelay cards (370), the grain layer (272), and effects (gold flourish 256-266, scrollable lock 229-235) all running for a section the user hasn't reached. The seseded run also means the 'random' run is fixed at page-load time, not at first interaction.
findings.evidence: Home.jsx:29 always-mounted sections; Shop.jsx:149 Date.now seed at mount; 362-376 shelf maps with per-card CSS animationDelay that will play off-screen on first scroll-in (or already played). The inert effect (Home.jsx:63-71) keeps it out of tab order but does NOT stop React work or CSS animation.
findings.recommendation: Defer run creation until first focus: keep state lazily initialized but call dispatch({type:'RESTART', seed: Date.now()}) (or a START action) the first time isfocus becomes true, OR gate the heavy subtree behind `{isfocus || everFocused ? <ShopBody/> : <ShopPlaceholder/>}`. Re-seed at the moment of first entry so the run feels fresh. This also fixes the determinism-at-load surprise and saves the initial render cost.

verification.reasoning:
The central claim is accurate and verifiable in the actual code.

VERIFIED TRUE:
- Home.jsx:180-190 maps over Sections and mounts every section simultaneously via React.cloneElement; off-screen sections are only displaced by a parent translateY transform (Home.jsx:176) — Home.module.css:1-30 has NO content-visibility/display:none/visibility:hidden, so off-screen subtrees stay laid out, painted, and animating.
- Shop.jsx:149 captures `seedRef = useRef((Date.now() >>> 0) || 1)` at mount and Shop.jsx:150-152 runs the useReducer LAZY initializer `() => createRun(seedRef.current)`. createRun (shopEngine.js:174-202) calls generateDay (line 200), which does real RNG work at line 98 onward: the ~62% event roll (103), wants selection with a CATEGORIES shuffle (124), shelf-count roll, two pool shuffles + a final shuffle, and per-item makeInstance+priceShelfItem pricing (140-149). So a full day-1 state (shelf/wants/event/rent/pricing) is generated the moment the homepage loads, before the user scrolls to the Shop. Confirmed.
- Determinism-at-load is real: the run is seeded once from Date.now() at mount with no isfocus guard, so the 'random' run is frozen at page-load time rather than first interaction.
- inert (Home.jsx:63-71) only removes the subtree from tab order/hit-testing; it does NOT stop React work, effects, timers, or CSS animations. Correctly stated.
- Off-screen infinite CSS animations are real: .portrait `animation: bob ... infinite` (Shop.module.css:299) is always mounted in shop phase; .streakFlame `flameFlicker ... infinite` (145) when the streak chip shows. The shelf `wareIn` cardIn animation (498-500) with the per-card inline animationDelay (Shop.jsx:370) plays on mount, so the 'morning restock' stagger can fire (or already have fired) off-screen.
- A seeded START/re-seed fix path exists: reduce() has a RESTART case taking a seed (shopEngine.js:526-527), so the recommended deferral is directly implementable.

MINOR OVERSTATEMENTS (don't change the verdict):
- .grain (Shop.module.css:59-66) is a STATIC texture with no animation property — calling it a running effect is slightly wrong; it's just an extra painted layer.
- The scroll-lock effect (Shop.jsx:229-235) early-returns when !isfocus, so it's effectively a no-op off-screen, not meaningful wasted work.
- The gold-flourish effect (256-266) initializes prevGold to state.gold and only fires when gold INCREASES, which won't happen off-screen without interaction, so it does no off-screen work in practice.

These nits aside, the load-bearing defect — a full run silently generated and an animating subtree mounted off-screen, with determinism frozen at page load — is real and accurately located.

SEVERITY: adjusted high -> medium. The wasted work is real but small in absolute terms (one synchronous reducer init + a few array shuffles over a 23-item catalog + ~12 inline SVG icons rendered once; two cheap transform-only infinite keyframes). At this scale it is not a frame-rate or memory problem, so 'high' overstates the perf impact. The genuinely user-visible defects are (a) the determinism/UX surprise — the 'random' run is fixed at page load and the restock stagger may already have played before arrival — and (b) needless work at the most contended moment (initial homepage paint). That warrants medium, not high.

findings.title: Whole component re-renders on every dispatch; shelf/bag/HUD have no memoization boundaries
findings.problem: Because the entire tree is inline children of Shop and receives fresh props/closures each render, every OFFER/keystroke-driven dispatch re-renders the HUD, KaitoPortrait (which paints a portrait img), WantsBoard, the full shelf (5-7 ShelfItems, each rendering an ItemIcon dangerouslySetInnerHTML), and the full bag (6 BagItems). onClick handlers are re-created inline every render (371, 398, 410). ItemIcon is memo()'d (itemIcons.jsx:304) but its `className` prop is a stable styles.* string so memo helps there; the parent buttons are not memoized. During an active haggle the slider's local useState causes Shop to re-render only if state changes — but OFFER dispatches do re-render everything. For 5-13 cards this is cheap today (sub-millisecond), so it's not urgent — but it becomes a real cost once auditors add animations, particle/coin effects, or a larger catalog.
findings.evidence: ShelfItem/BagItem are plain functions (530, 572) not React.memo; handlers inline at 371-374, 398-401. The slider onChange (835) sets local state so it doesn't thrash the engine, which is good; but any engine dispatch re-renders the entire stage.
findings.recommendation: After decomposition, wrap ShelfItem, BagItem, Rapport, KaitoPortrait, WantsBoard in React.memo and hoist their onClick to a stable useCallback that closes over dispatch + uid (or pass uid and dispatch and build the action in the child). Provide dispatch and playSFX via context (see prop-drilling finding) so memo isn't defeated by changing closures. Quantify before optimizing: it matters only post-feature-work, so do it as part of the split, not standalone.

findings.title: Side-effects modelled as incrementing counters (sfx.n, toast.n) consumed by ref-diffing effects — works but fragile and lossy
findings.problem: The engine signals one-shot effects by bumping a counter: sfx={cue,n:prev+1} (57-59), toast={text,n:prev+1} (61-63). The component diffs n against a ref (lastSfx 247-253) to fire playSFX exactly once. This is a hand-rolled event channel. Limitations: (1) only ONE sfx survives per reducer transition — if a single action wants two cues (e.g. coin + rapport-up), the second overwrites the first; (2) the toast is similarly single-slot, so a queued sequence of toasts can't exist; (3) the pattern is non-obvious and duplicated (two near-identical counter mechanisms). It's a reasonable pure-reducer compromise but won't scale to the richer audio/feedback an AAA pass wants.
findings.evidence: shopEngine sfx()/toast() each store {cue|text, n}; Shop.jsx:248-252 fires on n change; Toast at 1136-1151 diffs n similarly. completeSell can want both a coin sfx and a tip/rapport cue but only emits one (398).
findings.recommendation: Replace the two counters with a single `events: [{type, payload, seq}]` queue in state that the engine appends to, and one component effect that drains events whose seq > lastSeenSeq, dispatching each to playSFX / toast / future juice handlers. This is still pure (engine just pushes), supports multiple effects per action, unifies the two mechanisms, and gives later auditors one clean hook for screen-shake/coin-burst/voice barks.

findings.title: No test suite at all on a pure, deterministic engine that is the ideal test target
findings.problem: Glob for src/**/*.test.{js,jsx} returns nothing (only a node_modules hit). The engine is pure, deterministic (seeded RNG), and exports reduce/createRun/selectors — i.e. exactly the code that should have tests. Without them, every balance tweak (rent curve, dumpFactor, concession, tip caps) and every haggle-resolution edge (insult bands, patience-to-final, can't-afford reopen) is unverified, and regressions from the upcoming feature work will be invisible. This is the highest-leverage missing piece for 'industry-standard'.
findings.evidence: package.json scripts have lint but no test; no vitest/jest dependency; no test files in src. Engine functions like offer() (270-326), completeBuy/Sell (336-401), sleep() (424-469) are deterministic given seed+actions.
findings.recommendation: Add vitest (zero-config with Vite). Write: (1) reducer unit tests — seeded createRun snapshot, a scripted buy haggle (START_HAGGLE->OFFER->...->deal) asserting gold/bag/rapport deltas, insult lowball drops rapport by 3 and patience by 2 (295,313), quick-deal can't-afford reopen (338-343), patience<=0 -> final (320-323), sleep with gold<rent -> over (427-435), victoryDay -> win (442-447), tier crossing applies perk + pendingTier (451-462). (2) A balance regression test: simulate N seeded full runs with a fixed greedy-but-fair policy and assert win-rate stays in a target band (e.g. 35-65%) — this catches accidental difficulty swings when knobs change. (3) Component smoke tests with @testing-library/react for HaggleModal open/offer/walk and modal focus trap. Add `"test": "vitest"` to scripts.

verification.reasoning:
All factual claims verified against the actual code.

(1) No tests exist: Glob for src/**/*.test.{js,jsx} returns nothing; the only *.test/*.spec hits are in node_modules (gensync, zod, json-schema-traverse). Confirmed.

(2) No test infrastructure: package.json (read in full) has scripts predeploy/deploy/dev/build/lint/preview (lines 7-14) — a `lint` script but NO `test` script. devDependencies (lines 22-34) contain no vitest, jest, @testing-library/*, jsdom, or happy-dom. Confirmed.

(3) The engine is genuinely the ideal test target — pure and deterministic:
- makeRng (shopEngine.js:22-39) is mulberry32 seeded by an integer; RNG state is read back via the `state` getter (line 35-37) and threaded through state.rngState in every mutating path (e.g. lines 265, 274, 324, 359, 399, 410).
- A Grep across the engine shows NO Math.random and NO Date.now inside shopEngine.js — randomness enters only via createRun(seed) (line 174) and RESTART (line 527, `action.seed >>> 0`), confirming determinism given seed+actions.
- reduce() (508-531) is a clean switch over typed actions; createRun (174) and selectors wantFor (492), sellProjection (499), bagSlots (533) are all exported.

(4) Every specific line cite in the recommendation is accurate:
- offer() spans 270-326 ✓
- insult lowball: patience -= 2 and rapport = max(0, rapport - 3) at 294-295 (buy) and 313-314 (sell) — the finding cited 295,313 ✓
- quick-deal can't-afford reopen leaving haggle open: completeBuy 338-343 ✓
- patience<=0 -> final at 320-323 ✓
- sleep gold<rent -> phase "over" at 427-435 ✓
- newDay>=victoryDay -> phase "win" at 442-447 ✓
- tier crossing -> applyPerk + pendingTier + phase "backstory" at 451-462 ✓

The reducer's edge cases are real and subtle (concession formula line 276, conv early-deal line 284/304, tip cap line 374 `Math.min(streak-1,5)*tipUnit`, wanted-vs-gouge rapport gain line 391), making them exactly the kind of logic that silently breaks on balance tweaks. The finding is well-supported, not a misreading, and not merely a subjective preference — absence of automated verification on a pure deterministic engine is a concrete architectural gap.

Severity "high" is appropriate (not critical): there is no user-facing bug or data loss today; this is preventive infrastructure. But on a deterministic engine slated for "the upcoming feature work" and balance tuning, untested reducer logic means regressions ship invisibly, so high (above medium) is justified.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Keep the original plan; it is correct and specific. Tightening notes:

Setup: add vitest + @testing-library/react + @testing-library/jest-dom + jsdom (or happy-dom) to devDependencies, add `"test": "vitest"` and `"test:run": "vitest run"` to scripts, and configure `test: { environment: 'jsdom', globals: true }` in vite.config (so jsx component tests work alongside the existing @vitejs/plugin-react). Note happy-dom is lighter than jsdom for this small surface.

(1) Reducer unit tests (no DOM needed — import reduce/createRun/selectors directly):
  - Determinism: assert reduce(createRun(7), ...) twice yields deep-equal state, and that two different seeds diverge — locks in the rngState threading.
  - Scripted buy: createRun(seed) -> END_DAY isn't needed; drive START_HAGGLE{side:'buy',uid} then OFFER and assert gold/bag/shelf/rapport deltas match completeBuy (336-361), including overValue rapport tiers (>=1.2 ->+3, >=1.1 ->+2 else +1, line 353).
  - Insult band: OFFER below floor (buy) / above ceil (sell) drops rapport by 3 and patience by 2 (294-295 / 313-314) and sets mood "insult".
  - conv early-close: OFFER within `conv` of the counter completes the deal at the offered price (284, 304).
  - patience exhaustion: chain OFFERs until patience<=0 and assert haggle.final===true & patience clamped to 0 (320-323).
  - can't-afford: with gold below ask, QUICK_DEAL (or OFFER>=ask) leaves haggle.status==='active' and emits the toast (338-343) — assert no gold/bag mutation.
  - sell streak/tip: two profitable flips -> streak increments and tip uses Math.min(streak-1,5)*tipUnit (374); a loss resets streak to 0 (370).
  - sleep branches: gold<rent -> phase 'over' with daysSurvived=day-1 (427-435); newDay>=victoryDay -> 'win' (442-447); rapport past RAPPORT_TIERS[tier].at -> tier++, perk applied via applyPerk (471-478), pendingTier set, phase 'backstory' (451-462).

(2) Balance regression (the highest-value test): run e.g. 300 seeded full runs under a fixed "greedy-but-fair" policy (open every affordable shelf item, offer ~value*1.05 on buy / ceil*0.95 on sell, sleep each night) and assert win-rate stays in a target band (e.g. 35-65%) and median finalGold within a range. Gate this so it fails loudly when CONFIG knobs (baseRent, rentMult 1.18, dumpFactor 0.62, concession, tip caps) drift — this is what makes the suite "industry-standard" rather than box-ticking. Keep it a single deterministic test (fixed seed list) so CI is reproducible.

(3) Component smoke tests with @testing-library/react: HaggleModal opens on shelf-item click, slider/stepper/text-input dispatch OFFER, Walk closes; verify the focus trap (focus stays within modal on Tab) and Escape behavior. Mock the sound-cue prop so tests don't touch audio.

One caveat the original omitted: the engine emits side-effect-ish fields (toast/sfx/setFace mutate `next` in place within a freshly spread object) — tests should assert on the returned state's mood/quip/toast fields rather than expecting external calls, since sfx/toast write onto state (e.g. line 341 toast, 358 sfx), not to a real audio system. This keeps reducer tests pure.

findings.title: TypeScript is configured but unused; the pure engine should be typed (TS or JSDoc)
findings.problem: tsconfig.json has strict:true, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch and includes 'src', and typescript + @typescript-eslint are dev deps — yet there is not a single .ts/.tsx file; everything is .js/.jsx so none of this strictness is enforced. The engine passes large untyped state/haggle objects (the `h` haggle object has ~12 ad-hoc fields that differ by side: buy has ask/floor, sell has offer/ceil) and action objects with no contract. This is precisely where types prevent the 'wrong field on the wrong side' class of bugs that haggle code is prone to.
findings.evidence: Glob shows only .js/.jsx in src; tsconfig strict block at 17-20 is dead config. Haggle object shape diverges by side (shopEngine.js:226-239 vs 248-261) with no enforced discriminated union.
findings.recommendation: Two options: (a) Convert shopEngine.js + shopData.js to TypeScript with a discriminated-union State/Action/Haggle (BuyHaggle | SellHaggle), keeping components .jsx — Vite handles mixed TS/JSX natively and the tsconfig already supports it. (b) If avoiding TS, add JSDoc @typedef for State, Action, Haggle, ShelfInstance and turn on checkJs. Option (a) is the AAA-standard choice and the engine is small enough (533 lines) to convert in one pass.

findings.title: Prop drilling of dispatch/playSFX and tight coupling to scrollContext; no Shop-local context
findings.problem: state, dispatch, and playSFX are threaded as props to nearly every child (HaggleModal gets {state, dispatch, playSFX}, DayEnd/Backstory/RunEnd get {state, dispatch}, ShelfItem/BagItem get inline onClick closures). Once decomposed into files this becomes a lot of repetitive plumbing and defeats React.memo (new closures each render). Separately, Shop consumes scrollContext for five concerns (setScrollable, currentSection, openDialogWithCallback, chromeHidden, setChromeHidden) — mixing host-scroll coordination into the game component. The chrome-hide and intro-dialog logic (213-244) are host concerns leaking into the game.
findings.evidence: Shop.jsx:134 destructures 5 scrollContext fields; dispatch/playSFX passed at 421, 423, 425, 428; inline onClick at 371-374, 398-401, 410-413.
findings.recommendation: Create a ShopContext (or two: ShopStateContext + ShopDispatchContext, the standard split so state-readers and action-firers re-render independently) providing {state, dispatch, playSFX, slots, records}. Children consume what they need. Keep scrollContext usage confined to a thin Shop shell component that handles scroll-lock/chrome/intro-dialog and renders the game body — separating host coordination from game logic.

findings.title: Magic numbers scattered through the engine that belong in CONFIG
findings.problem: CONFIG centralizes some knobs (startGold, rent, shelf/wants counts, dumpFactor) but the engine hardcodes many balance-critical constants inline, which makes tuning error-prone and tests brittle. Examples: rapport cap 140 (355,395), insult rapport penalty -3 (295,314), concession band 0.55..0.85 and rapport coefficient 0.003 (276), pricing markups 1.3/1.06/1.03 and askRelief 0.16/0.0015 (86-92), opening sell offer multipliers 0.85/0.38 (247), event probability 0.62 (103), wanted-pool bias 0.6 / min 2 (142), tip cap (streak-1) max 5 and unit 0.025 (373-374), rapport-gain thresholds overValue 1.2/1.1 (353) and wanted 0.96 (391), value jitter from RARITY. These are exactly the levers the balance auditors will want to pull.
findings.evidence: shopEngine.js:276 concession constants; 86-93 pricing constants; 247 sell-offer constants; 353-374 rapport/tip constants; 103 event chance. None reference CONFIG.
findings.recommendation: Promote all balance constants into a structured CONFIG (e.g. CONFIG.haggle = {concessionMin, concessionMax, rapportSlope, convFrac}, CONFIG.pricing = {askMarkup, floorMarkup, askRelief...}, CONFIG.rapport = {cap, insultPenalty, fairBuyThresholds, fairSellFrac}, CONFIG.streak = {tipUnitFrac, tipCap}, CONFIG.events = {chance, biasFrac}). The engine reads only from CONFIG. This makes a balance-tuning pass a single-file edit and lets the regression test parametrize difficulty.

findings.title: itemIcons via dangerouslySetInnerHTML — acceptable but loses correctness/perf benefits of real SVG components
findings.problem: 23 icons are stored as raw SVG strings and injected with dangerouslySetInnerHTML into a wrapping span (304-311). The XSS comment is correct (all strings are author-authored, no user input) so it's not a security issue. But: (1) each icon parses HTML at runtime instead of being a static React element tree, (2) the strings ship as one ~10KB JS object that's always bundled even though only 5-13 icons render per day, (3) no per-icon tree-shaking, (4) React can't reconcile internals so any future animation/state on an icon is impossible, (5) accessibility/title handling is all-or-nothing. The memo() wrapper helps avoid re-parsing on re-render, which mitigates (1).
findings.evidence: itemIcons.jsx:309 __html injection; ICONS object holds 23 inline strings (11-296); ItemIcon memo at 304.
findings.recommendation: Low priority. If kept, fine as-is. For a polish pass, convert to either (a) real .svg files imported via vite-plugin-svgr as components (enables lazy import + animation), or (b) hand-written JSX SVG components in a map. This also lets icons be code-split or sprited. Not worth doing before the bigger refactors; flagging for completeness.

findings.title: Dead and duplicated CSS: unused .offerValue rule and near-identical .flipTag/.wantedTag
findings.problem: (1) .offerValue (1000-1006) is never referenced in Shop.jsx — the offer readout uses .offerField/.offerInput/.offerG instead. Confirmed by grep: only definition, no usage. (2) .flipTag (514-541) and .wantedTag (721-747) are byte-for-byte identical except .flipTag adds `white-space: nowrap` — same gradient, size, padding, ::before dot. They're used on shelf cards vs bag cards respectively but render the same pill, so the duplication is pure maintenance debt (the responsive block at 1641-1642 already targets both together).
findings.evidence: grep offerValue -> only Shop.module.css:1000 (no JSX hit). flipTag block 514-541 vs wantedTag 721-747 differ only by line 527 (white-space:nowrap). Shop.jsx uses styles.flipTag (554) and styles.wantedTag (589).
findings.recommendation: Delete .offerValue. Merge .flipTag/.wantedTag into a single .demandTag class (with white-space:nowrap kept) and apply it in both ShelfItem and BagItem; if a visual distinction is wanted later, add a modifier class. Small cleanup but removes ~50 lines and a real duplication trap.

findings.title: ITEM_BY_ID is exported but unused (dead export)
findings.problem: ITEM_BY_ID = Object.fromEntries(ITEMS.map(...)) is computed and exported but grep finds no consumer anywhere in src. It's harmless but is dead code that suggests an intended lookup pattern that was never wired (the engine carries full item fields on each instance instead, makeInstance at shopEngine.js:70-82). The instance copies item.name/category/rarity/flavor onto every instance, so a base-item lookup by id may actually be the cleaner pattern.
findings.evidence: grep ITEM_BY_ID across src -> only the definition (shopData.js:63). makeInstance duplicates static item fields onto each instance (74-80) rather than referencing the catalog by id.
findings.recommendation: Either remove ITEM_BY_ID, or use it: store only {uid, id, value, paid} on instances and resolve name/category/rarity/flavor via ITEM_BY_ID[id] in selectors/UI. The latter shrinks state, removes field duplication, and is the natural home for the exported map.

findings.title: useFocusTrap reads document.activeElement during render (impure render), and global keydown listeners stack across nested modals
findings.problem: useFocusTrap captures the trigger via `if (triggerRef.current === null) triggerRef.current = document.activeElement` DURING render (40-42). Reading/depending on DOM state in the render body is impure and unsafe under React 18 concurrent features / StrictMode double-invocation (the first render's activeElement may not be the real trigger if render is discarded). Separately, useEscape attaches a window-level keydown listener per modal (29). When a phase modal force-closes help/codex (239-244) the ordering is handled, but multiple useEscape consumers can be mounted briefly and all fire on one Escape; and the listener is on window, not scoped, so it competes with the host's own key handling.
findings.evidence: Shop.jsx:40-42 activeElement read in render; useEscape window listener at 29-30; comment at 35-37 acknowledges the timing fragility ('captured during the first render before React applies autoFocus').
findings.recommendation: Capture the trigger in a useEffect (or useLayoutEffect) on mount, not in render, storing it before focusing into the modal. Consider a single shared modal manager / focus-trap utility (or pull in a tiny vetted lib like focus-trap-react) so only the top-most modal owns Escape and the trap, removing per-modal window listeners. This hardens the a11y layer ahead of adding more modals.

verification.reasoning:
Both core mechanics are real and accurately cited.

(A) Impure render read — CONFIRMED literally. Shop.jsx:40-42 reads `document.activeElement` inside the render body, guarded only by `triggerRef.current === null`. That is a render-phase read of mutable external DOM state — genuinely impure. The author even documents the timing rationale in the comment at 34-37. HOWEVER, practical breakage is low: the app does run under React.StrictMode (main.jsx:9), but the ref guard makes the double-invocation idempotent — the first render captures the trigger before the modal commits/autofocuses, and the second invocation skips because the ref is now non-null (refs persist across StrictMode double-render). The concurrent-rendering hazard (a discarded render capturing a stale activeElement) is theoretical here, not currently observable. So part A is a valid purity/hardening defect of LOW practical impact, not an active visible bug.

(B) Stacking window listeners — CONFIRMED and observable. useEscape (21-32) attaches a `window` keydown listener per modal. The phase modals (HaggleModal/DayEnd/Backstory/RunEnd at 420-434) are mutually exclusive via `state.phase`, so those never co-mount. BUT showHelp (155) and showCodex (156) are independent useState booleans with NO mutual exclusion — line 340 setShowHelp(true) does not clear codex, and line 329 setShowCodex(true) does not clear help. So Help (useEscape at 1008) and Codex (useEscape at 1072) can both be mounted at once; one Escape press fires BOTH window handlers, closing both panels and calling e.preventDefault() twice. Additionally, because the precedence effect at 239-244 runs only after commit, a phase modal and an already-open help/codex co-mount for one render, so Escape briefly fires two handlers there too. Two stacked Scrims also run two useFocusTrap instances whose focus-restoration-on-unmount can fight. This matches the finding precisely.

Overstatements: 'competes with the host's own key handling' is not substantiated — Grep of src/Pages/Home found no global window keydown listener in the host/Navigation (only element-scoped onKeyDown in Profile/WebsiteProjects), so there is no host handler to race. And the StrictMode-breakage framing for (A) overstates the real risk. Net: confirmed, with minor overstatement on one sub-point. Severity medium is fair — a real but low-blast-radius a11y/correctness issue whose worst current symptom is two info panels closing on one Escape.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Two independent fixes:

1) Capture the trigger off the render path. Replace the render-body read (40-42) with an effect that runs once on mount before focusing into the modal:
   useLayoutEffect(() => { triggerRef.current = document.activeElement; /* then focus into panel */ }, []);
This removes the impurity. (Low urgency given the ref guard already makes it work in practice, but it is the correct pattern and de-risks future concurrent features.)

2) Fix the real stacking bug. The minimal correctness fix is to make Help and Codex mutually exclusive AND mutually exclusive with phase modals at the call sites: in the openers, setShowCodex(false) when opening Help and vice-versa (lines 329/340), and disable/guard the HUD help/codex buttons while state.phase !== 'shop'. The robust fix is a single shared 'top-most modal owns Escape' mechanism: register escape handlers in a stack (LIFO) via context/ref so only the last-registered consumer fires, instead of every mounted useEscape listening on window. A tiny vetted dependency (focus-trap-react) would also consolidate the focus trap + restore + escape ownership and remove the per-modal window listeners entirely — reasonable given the modal count is growing. Drop the unsupported 'competes with host key handling' rationale from the writeup.

findings.title: HaggleModal local state re-anchoring logic is intricate and duplicated (opening computed twice, two sync effects)
findings.problem: The modal computes the 'opening' offer formula in three places: opening() (623-626), the useState initializer draft (628), and again inside the re-anchor effect (640-644). The clamp helper is defined twice (clampP at 620 and a local clamp at 636). There are two effects keeping price/draft in sync (634-646 syncing on band changes, 649 syncing draft from price) plus draftPrice() parsing at submit (679-682). This is correct but dense and a likely bug magnet when the haggle UX is expanded (the audit's haggle-depth features will live here).
findings.evidence: Shop.jsx:623-626 opening(); 628 draft initializer repeats it; 640-644 effect repeats it again; clampP at 620 and clamp at 636 are the same logic.
findings.recommendation: Extract a useHaggleOffer(h, gold) hook returning {price, setPrice, draft, setDraft, min, max, step, commitDraft, draftPrice, opening}. Define the opening formula and clamp ONCE inside it. This isolates the gnarly local-state machine from the JSX and makes it independently testable, which the feature work needs.

findings.title: Records persistence is component-owned with a manual ref+state mirror; brittle as records grow
findings.problem: Records use a recordsRef + records useState mirror that must be kept in lockstep manually (recordsRef.current = next; setRecords(next); saveRecords(next) repeated in two effects, 170-173 and 204-207). The ref-as-source-of-truth + state-for-render pattern is easy to get out of sync as more record fields (achievements, per-item stats, daily-best) get added by feature work. The schema is versioned (RECORDS_KEY .v1) which is good, but there's no migration path defined.
findings.evidence: Shop.jsx:160-162 ref+state init; duplicated triple-write at 170-173 and 204-207; DEFAULT_RECORDS spread on load (118) is the only migration mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Extract a useRecords() hook returning [records, mutateRecords] where mutateRecords(fn) computes next, persists, and setStates atomically — removing the manual triplication. Add an explicit version/migrate(stored) step for forward-compat as fields are added. Keeps persistence in one place ahead of meta-progression features.

findings.title: No Prettier/format config and ESLint not extended for React/JSX correctness
findings.problem: .eslintrc extends eslint:recommended + @typescript-eslint/recommended + react-hooks/recommended, but the project is .jsx with no eslint-plugin-react (so JSX-specific lints like key/role/no-unknown-property aren't enforced) and the @typescript-eslint rules largely no-op on .js files. There's no Prettier config or format script, so formatting consistency relies on editor settings. For a portfolio piece aiming at 'industry standard', the tooling story is thin.
findings.evidence: package.json scripts: only dev/build/lint/preview; no format, no test. .eslintrc has no eslint-plugin-react; lint runs `eslint src --ext js,jsx` with --max-warnings 0.
findings.recommendation: Add Prettier (.prettierrc + `format` script) and eslint-config-prettier; add eslint-plugin-react + jsx-a11y (the game leans hard on a11y, so jsx-a11y would catch role/aria mistakes automatically). Add a CI-friendly `lint && test` gate. Low effort, high signal for maintainability.

findings.title: Prioritized refactor roadmap that ENABLES the gameplay/feature additions
findings.problem: The individual findings above need an execution order so the foundational work lands before feature auditors build on it. Doing features on the current monolith would compound the debt.
findings.evidence: Synthesis of all findings; engine purity (shopEngine.js) + lack of tests/types/decomposition are the load-bearing gaps.
findings.recommendation: Phase 0 (enabling, do first): (1) Add vitest + write reducer + balance-regression tests against the engine AS-IS — this locks current behavior so refactors are safe.
