(2) Convert shopEngine.js/shopData.js to TS (or JSDoc+checkJs) with State/Action/Haggle unions. (3) Centralize all magic numbers into structured CONFIG. Phase 1 (decompose): split Shop.jsx into the folder structure (Hud/Shelf/Bag/Portrait/modals/ui/hooks), introduce ShopState+ShopDispatch context, extract useHaggleOffer/useRecords hooks, replace sfx.n/toast.n with a single events queue. Phase 2 (lifecycle/perf): defer run creation until first focus, memoize ShelfItem/BagItem/HUD. Phase 3 (cleanup): delete .offerValue, merge flipTag/wantedTag, resolve ITEM_BY_ID, add Prettier + jsx-a11y, harden focus trap. After Phase 1 every feature auditor's work (deeper haggle UX, more events/items, animations, meta-progression) drops into a clear seam with test coverage behind it.

summary: KAITO'S CURIOS is a polished, genuinely charming single-screen haggling game with excellent juice (streaks, quips, rapport story beats) and clean systems code. But as a GAME it is shallow and, critically, mislabeled. It is NOT a roguelike: it is a fixed-length (8-day) economic puzzle with one repeated minigame, linear story-gated "perks," and no run-to-run variety, no build choices, no death-with-persistent-unlocks loop, no meta-progression beyond localStorage high scores. The core economic loop is a solved, dominant strategy — "buy wanted items cheap, sell them back the same day" — and the math makes it trivially winnable: a competent player nets ~100g/day against 45g day-1 rent, and because the haggle margin is a fixed ~55% of item value while rent grows only 18%/day, the player's compounding bankroll outpaces rent the moment gold clears ~400 (typically day 2-3). After that there is zero failure pressure; the remaining six days are a formality. The haggle minigame — a slider + offer loop against a single deterministic concession curve — has no item-specific behavior, no bluffing, no mood/event variance, and becomes rote within ~10 plays. Rapport/perks are not player choices; they unlock in a fixed order tied to the (excellent) Kaito-bio story, so there is no build identity. Replayability is near zero after one win: the same 23 items, same 11 events, same 6 story beats, same dominant strategy, and the story — the actual reason to play — is fully consumed in a single successful run. The fix is not more polish (polish is already AAA-tier for a portfolio); it is to (a) make the label honest by either repositioning it as a "cozy trading puzzle" or actually building roguelike bones (death loop + persistent meta-unlocks + per-run build variety), (b) introduce real decision tension (scarcity, opportunity cost, risk), and (c) make the haggle a skill expression with variety. I rank concrete proposals by impact/effort below; the three highest-leverage moves are: fix the broken economy so survival is actually at stake, add per-haggle variety + item/customer personality, and add a meta-progression spine that gives a reason to replay after the story is seen.

findings.title: It is not a roguelike — fixed length, no build variety, no death-loop meta-progression
findings.problem: The game is sold as a 'cozy haggling roguelike' but has none of the genre's defining traits. (1) Fixed length: victoryDay:9 means a hard 8-day run every time — no escalation past a known finish line. (2) No run-to-run build variety: every run starts identical (createRun seeds the same startGold 140, startSlots 6, basePatience 3, empty perks), and perks are not chosen — applyPerk() fires in a FIXED order locked to rapport tiers (appraise→patience→slot→discount→slot→patience). Two runs play mechanically identically. (3) No meta-progression: the only thing that persists (Shop.jsx:105-130 RECORDS_KEY) is high scores + which lore cards were ever seen. Nothing the player earns carries into the next run — no unlocks, no currency, no new content gated by prior runs. (4) No death-and-restart-with-progress loop: losing just resets to an identical run. This is a fixed-length economic puzzle with seeded daily RNG, i.e. closer to a 'cozy management/merchant sim vignette' than a roguelike.
findings.recommendation: Pick one of two honest directions. CHEAP/HONEST: rename it in the intro/help/Home memory to a 'cozy trading puzzle' or 'haggling vignette' and drop the roguelike claim — costs nothing, removes the false promise. AMBITIOUS/CORRECT: build actual roguelike bones — (a) on death/win, award a meta-currency (e.g. 'reputation tokens' = bestStreak + daysSurvived + rapport/10) banked in RECORDS; (b) a between-runs 'caravan upgrade' shop spending that currency on persistent unlocks (start with +1 slot, a starting perk pick, a new item category, a harder/longer mode); (c) make each run offer a CHOICE of perk at each rapport tier (draft 1-of-3) instead of a fixed sequence, so builds diverge (e.g. a 'patience build' vs a 'bag-size build' vs a 'discount/margin build'); (d) add an endless/ascension mode past day 8 where rent keeps climbing for a score chase. This is the single biggest lever for turning a vignette into a replayable game.

verification.reasoning: All four sub-claims verified against the actual code. (1) FIXED LENGTH — confirmed: shopData.js:19 `victoryDay: 9` and shopEngine.js:442 `if (newDay >= CONFIG.victoryDay) { next.phase = "win"; }` hard-terminate at the morning of day 9 (8 trading days). Rent escalates (baseRent 45 × 1.18^(day-1), shopEngine.js:152) but only to a known finish line; there is no endless/ascension branch. (2) NO BUILD VARIETY — confirmed: createRun (shopEngine.js:174-202) always seeds gold:140, the default empty perks `{appraise:false, patience:0, slots:0, discount:false}`, basePatience 3, startSlots 6. Perks are never chosen — sleep()/ackBackstory() call `applyPerk(state.perks, tierDef.perk)` (shopEngine.js:454, 471-478) where tierDef.perk is hard-coded per RAPPORT_TIERS entry in a fixed order: appraise(12)→patience(28)→slot(46)→discount(66)→slot(88)→patience(110) (shopData.js:164-207). The only run-to-run variance is the Date.now() seed (Shop.jsx:149) driving daily RNG for events/wants/shelf/value-jitter — exactly the "seeded daily RNG" the finding itself names. (3) NO META-PROGRESSION — confirmed: RECORDS_KEY persists only bestGold/bestRapport/bestDay/bestStreak/wins/runs and a `lore[]` array of seen story-card indices (Shop.jsx:105-130, 166-208). The lore array is pure codex memory; it gates/unlocks nothing mechanical. Nothing earned carries forward. (4) NO DEATH-LOOP — confirmed: the "New run" button dispatches `RESTART` → `createRun(Date.now())` (Shop.jsx:997, shopEngine.js:526-527), producing a mechanically identical fresh run. NUANCE: two runs are not bit-identical experiences — daily events, wants, shelf composition and value jitter all differ by seed — but the finding's claim is specifically about the *mechanical systems* (starting resources, build path, progression) being identical, which is true, and the finding explicitly concedes the seeded-daily-RNG point. The "not a roguelike" verdict is partly definitional, but the underlying code facts are all correct and the genre critique is evidence-backed, not a misreading. Severity HIGH is appropriate: this is the single largest replayability lever, even though it is a design-scope/honesty issue (not a functional bug) and the finding's own CHEAP fix (rename, drop the roguelike claim) costs essentially nothing.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Keep both honest directions from the original; they are correct. Two refinements for accuracy/actionability:

CHEAP/HONEST (do this regardless, immediately): drop the "roguelike" claim in shopData.js:3 ("A cozy haggling roguelike"), the intro Shop1 dialog, the Help panel, and the Home auto-memory note (MEMORY.md fourth-section). Call it a "cozy haggling trading puzzle" or "merchant-sim vignette." Zero code risk, removes the false promise.

AMBITIOUS/CORRECT (if investing): 
(a) Meta-currency — derive it from the values ALREADY banked at run end (Shop.jsx:195-203) rather than recomputing: e.g. tokens += state.stats.daysSurvived + state.stats.bestStreak + Math.floor(state.stats.bestRapport/10); store a `tokens` and `unlocks{}` field in RECORDS (DEFAULT_RECORDS, Shop.jsx:106-114) and apply purchased unlocks in createRun().
(b) Perk drafting — the blocker is shopEngine.js:454 hard-coding `applyPerk(state.perks, tierDef.perk)`. Refactor RAPPORT_TIERS so each tier offers `choices: [perk, perk, perk]`; have sleep() enter a new `phase:"perkPick"` (don't auto-apply), and add a `PICK_PERK` action that calls applyPerk with the chosen perk then resumes generateDay(). This is the change that actually creates divergent builds (patience vs bag-size vs margin).
(c) Endless/ascension — gate behind a meta-unlock: at shopEngine.js:442, instead of forcing phase:"win", if an `endless` unlock/mode flag is set, keep generating days with continued rentGrowth for a score chase; otherwise win as today.
(d) Between-runs caravan shop — a new modal off RunEnd (Shop.jsx:953) spending tokens on persistent unlocks (+1 start slot, a starting-perk pick, an extra item category, endless mode).

Sequence by ROI: (a)+(b) deliver most of the "roguelite" feel for the least surface area; (c)+(d) are the larger lift. Note the perk catalog is currently only 4 distinct effects (PERK_LABELS, shopData.js:154-159) — drafting needs more perk variety to be meaningful, so expand that catalog as part of (b).

findings.title: The economy is solved and trivially winnable — fixed ~55% margin outpaces rent by day 2-3
findings.problem: I modeled the math. Buy floor is value*1.06; wanted-sell ceil is value*(1+bonus) with bonus 0.55-0.9. A patient player buys near floor and sells near ceil, so per-flip profit is a FIXED ~50-70% of item value regardless of item (verified: value 28→+15 (54%), value 230→+128 (56%), value 320→+180 (56%)). Rent grows only 18%/day from a base of 45 (day1 45 … day8 143; total 689 over the run). A skilled day-1 chain of ~4 cheap wanted flips nets gold 140→240 BEFORE rent — already ~5x day-1 rent. Because margin scales linearly with item value, a bigger bankroll buys pricier items for bigger ABSOLUTE profit, so income compounds while rent grows only 18%. The result: once gold clears ~400 (typically day 2-3) rent can never catch up, and the last 5-6 days have zero failure risk. There is no economic tension and the win is a formality. The shelf is even deliberately biased 60% toward wanted categories (shopEngine.js:142) and always guarantees a cheap-category want (line 122-123), removing the last bit of scarcity.
findings.recommendation: Re-balance so survival is genuinely at stake all 8 days. Concrete: (1) Make rent growth super-linear relative to margin — either raise rentGrowth to ~1.28 OR add a flat per-day rent step, so cumulative rent is ~70-85% of optimal income, not ~25%. (2) Cap same-day re-flips: items Kaito sells should NOT be instantly re-buyable by him at a premium the same day — introduce a hold/cooldown (he won't buy back a category he just sold you for N hours/turns), or make wanted-bonus apply only to items NOT bought from his own shelf today (kill the risk-free instant flip). (3) Make margin shrink as bankroll grows (Kaito's greed/floor scales with the player's gold, or wanted-bonus diminishes on repeat sells of the same category that day). (4) Add a per-day action/energy budget (e.g. 'the shop closes after K haggles') so you can't flip the entire shelf every day. Target: a good player wins ~60-70% of runs, a careless one loses. Right now it's ~100%.

verification.reasoning:
I independently re-derived the economy from the code and every load-bearing claim holds; if anything the finding is conservative.

PER-FLIP MARGIN (shopEngine.js:90-94 floor, :246 ceil): buy floor = value*max(1.06+greed*0.3, 1.03); wanted-sell ceil = value*(1+bonus), bonus = rng.range(0.55,0.9) (shopData line via generateDay:131). My model reproduces the cited examples almost exactly: value 230 -> +146 at mid-bonus (63%); value 320 -> +197 (62%); value 28 -> +18 (64%). Margin is indeed a near-fixed ~46-82% of item value, scaling linearly with value, exactly as claimed.

REALISTIC HAGGLE LANDING: I faithfully re-implemented offer() (shopEngine.js:270-326). At base patience 3 a patient player does NOT quite reach the exact floor/ceil — buy lands ~+2.4% over floor (~257 vs floor 251), sell ~-4.5% under ceil. But the round trip still nets ~53% of value (value 230: buy 257, sell 379, net +122). And when patience hits 0, h.final is set and the UI offers QUICK_DEAL at the current near-floor/near-ceil price (Shop.jsx:753-768), so the player still captures it. The finding's "~50-70%" band is accurate.

RENT CURVE (shopEngine.js:152, CONFIG): day1 45 ... day8 143, cumulative 689 — matches the finding's numbers exactly.

INSTANT RE-FLIP / NO COOLDOWN: Confirmed. Sell ceiling depends only on wantFor(state, inst.category) (sellProjection:499-504, startHaggle:244-246). There is no boughtToday flag, no cooldown, no per-category sell decay — a freshly-bought wanted item gets the full premium on same-day resale. The finding's claim is exactly right.

SHELF BIAS / GUARANTEED CHEAP WANT: Confirmed. shopEngine.js:142 forces ~60% of the shelf into wanted categories; lines 122-123 always seed one cheap wanted category (Potion/Food/Tool/Trinket). So an affordable risk-free flip exists every single day.

NO OTHER PRESSURE: The only loss condition is sleep() rent check (shopEngine.js:427). There is no per-day action budget anywhere (grep confirmed — only bag slots=6 and patience-per-haggle limit you), no inventory spoilage, no overnight gold drain, and bag carries over nights. Income compounds (bigger bankroll buys pricier items for bigger absolute profit) while rent grows only 18%.

UNDERSTATEMENT, not overstatement: My full 8-day greedy simulation with the realistic 140-gold day-1 constraint ends day 1 at ~253-298 gold (already 5-6x the 45 rent), and the streak-tip system (completeSell:373-374, escalating up to 5x value*0.025 per flip) — which the finding doesn't even factor in — accelerates this further. By day 2 gold blows past 400 and rent is permanently irrelevant. The finding's "clears ~400 by day 2-3, win is a formality" is accurate and slightly conservative.

The one minor inaccuracy: the finding's parenthetical "day-1 chain of ~4 cheap wanted flips nets gold 140->240" — you can fit up to 6 flips (bag has 6 slots and you re-flip to free cash), and exact figures vary with the seeded shelf, but the magnitude is right. This is a phrasing imprecision, not a flaw in the thesis. Severity 'critical' is correct: for a game whose core loop is risk/reward survival, a solved economy with ~100% win rate and zero tension across days 4-8 guts the entire design.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
The original recommendation is sound and actionable; I'd tighten and add specifics, grounded in the exact lines verified:

(1) RAISE RENT PRESSURE — multiple levers, not just rentGrowth. Bump CONFIG.rentGrowth (shopData.js:14) from 1.18 to ~1.30 AND add a flat escalating step. Concretely make rent = baseRent*pow(growth, day-1) + 12*(day-1) (edit shopEngine.js:152). Target cumulative rent ~70-85% of an average player's optimal income, not the current ~25%.

(2) KILL THE INSTANT SAME-DAY RE-FLIP (highest-leverage fix). Tag instances bought from the shelf with a boughtDay field in completeBuy (shopEngine.js:348: spread `boughtDay: state.day`), then in startHaggle sell-side (shopEngine.js:244) and sellProjection (:502) suppress the wanted bonus if `inst.boughtDay === state.day` — fall back to dumpFactor (0.62) for same-day resale. This alone removes the risk-free flip: profit then requires holding overnight and predicting tomorrow's wants (real risk, since wants reroll each generateDay).

(3) MAKE MARGIN SHRINK WITH BANKROLL / REPEAT SELLS. Two compounding fixes: (a) scale Kaito's buy floor up with player gold — in priceShelfItem (shopEngine.js:90) add `+ Math.min(0.25, state.gold/4000*0.25)` to the floor multiplier so a rich player faces a higher floor; (b) decay the wanted bonus per same-category sell that day — track a per-day per-category sell counter and multiply ceil by pow(0.85, soldThisCategoryToday) so dumping 6 of one category collapses the premium.

(4) ADD A PER-DAY ACTION BUDGET so you cannot drain the whole shelf daily. Add CONFIG.dailyHaggles (e.g. 5), decrement on each completed deal, and gate startHaggle when exhausted (toast "Kaito's shutting up shop for the day"). This caps daily income independent of bag size.

(5) ADD HOLD RISK so carried inventory isn't free. Either reroll instance.value slightly at day-break (±8% market drift) or add a small "stale stock" penalty so hoarding to chase tomorrow's wants has downside.

Verification target: tune so a skilled player wins ~60-70% and a careless one loses. I'd add a quick Monte-Carlo harness over the seeded RNG (createRun + a scripted greedy policy) to confirm the post-change win rate before shipping — the engine is pure and deterministic, so this is straightforward.

findings.title: One dominant strategy, no opportunity cost — the 'hold for a better day' mechanic is a trap with no upside
findings.location: shopEngine.js:140-149 (shelf bias), shopData.js:21 (dumpFactor 0.62), Shop.jsx:1031-1037 (help: 'Hold the rest')
findings.problem: The intended decision space is 'flip wanted items now vs hold non-wanted items for a future day Kaito wants them.' But holding is strictly dominated and irrational: (a) bag slots (6) are precious and instant same-day flips are always available because the shelf is 60%-biased toward wants AND a cheap want is guaranteed daily, so there's never a reason to tie up a slot speculatively; (b) money held in inventory is money NOT compounding through flips; (c) the future is RNG — there's no guarantee Kaito ever wants a held category before day 8, and no carry-over value at run end (held items are just lost gold). So the 'hold' pillar the help text teaches (Shop.jsx:1034) is actively bad advice. The entire game collapses to one loop: each morning, buy the cheapest wanted items in floor-to-ceiling order, sell them back, repeat. No routing, no portfolio, no risk/reward.
findings.recommendation: Give holding a real, legible upside and create genuine opportunity cost. Options: (1) Show a 3-day demand FORECAST (partial info) so speculative holds become an informed bet — 'Gems wanted in 2 days, +35%.' (2) Item conditions/aging: some items appreciate if held (a fine wine, a 'ripening' curio) creating a buy-and-hold lane; others spoil (food loses value daily) creating a sell-now lane. (3) Non-wanted floor (dumpFactor 0.62) should sometimes beat a future wanted price after accounting for slot lock + rent, so the math is a real choice. (4) Limit how many of a category Kaito will buy per day (he saturates), forcing you to spread sales across days and actually hold. (5) Let unsold inventory carry run-to-run value (sells into the meta-shop) so a hold isn't pure loss. Goal: at least two viable strategies (fast-flip churn vs patient appreciation) that trade off against each other.

verification.reasoning:
Verified every load-bearing claim against the code and it holds up.

SHELF/WANTS BIAS (claim a): shopEngine.js:142 `nWanted = Math.min(wantedPool.length, Math.max(2, Math.round(shelfCount * 0.6)))` — the shelf is hard-biased 60% toward today's wanted categories. shopEngine.js:122-127 reserves the FIRST want for a guaranteed cheap category (`["Potion","Food","Tool","Trinket"]`). So an affordable same-day flip is guaranteed every day. Confirmed.

NO COUNTERVAILING MECHANIC: grep for appreciat|aging|spoil|ripen|saturat|forecast|carry returned nothing in shop files. There is no item appreciation, no spoilage, no per-day buy cap (dayDeals at shopEngine.js:168/381 is a stats counter only — never gates buying), and no demand forecast (UI shows only "TODAY'S DEMAND", Shop.jsx:507). The shelf is fully regenerated each day (shopEngine.js:147-149,162), so a non-bought item is gone tomorrow — speculative holding requires BUYING at the ~1.06–1.1x-value floor (shopEngine.js:90-93) and locking a slot.

NO CARRY-OVER (claim c): at win (shopEngine.js:444) and loss (shopEngine.js:431-432) `finalGold` = `state.gold` only; the bag is never liquidated. Held inventory is forfeited entirely at run end. Confirmed.

OPPORTUNITY-COST MATH: a wanted flip nets ~+0.5x to +0.84x of item value per day (buy near 1.06x floor, sell at wanted ceiling 1+bonus, bonus 0.55–0.90 per shopEngine.js:131 / dumpFactor sell path 246/502). A held non-cheap category has only ~1.5/8 ≈ 19%/day chance of becoming wanted, with the slot idle meanwhile. The guaranteed daily churn dominates the uncertain hold. Holding is net-negative in the overwhelming majority of cases.

BAD-ADVICE CLAIM: confirmed and actually WORSE than stated — the "Hold the rest … stash it and wait" advice appears not only in the help panel (Shop.jsx:1033-1035) but is repeated at the live decision point inside the sell haggle ("You could hold it for a day he wants it.", Shop.jsx:790-791). The tutorial teaches a losing line in two places.

WHY confirmed not partial: the finding's one slight overstatement is "strictly dominated" — holding CAN pay off in narrow late-game edge cases (surplus slots+gold, a high-value item bought cheap whose category swings wanted). It's near-universally inferior rather than mathematically strict domination. But this is a minor wording nit; the substantive defect (a single dominant fast-flip loop, holding being net-negative yet actively taught, and zero designed opportunity cost) is fully real and is a genuine game-design defect, not a subjective preference — so the verdict is confirmed and severity "high" stands for a depth/replayability lens.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Keep the original multi-option recommendation; it is specific and correct. Tighten/prioritize as follows for portfolio scope:

PRIORITY 1 (cheapest, highest impact) — per-day saturation cap. Track sales per category per day in completeSell and decay the wanted bonus on repeated sales of the same category, e.g. effective bonus = baseBonus * 0.7^(salesOfCategoryToday). This single change (a) breaks the unbounded same-day churn, (b) immediately makes spreading sales across days—i.e. holding—mathematically correct for high-value categories, and (c) requires only a `daySales` map in state plus a factor in completeSell (shopEngine.js:391) and sellProjection (shopEngine.js:502). Effort S, not L.

PRIORITY 2 — 3-day demand forecast (partial info). Pre-roll the next 2-3 days' wants at generateDay and expose a "coming soon" strip in the demand board (Shop.jsx:507). Turns blind holding into an informed bet ("Gems wanted in 2 days, +35%"). This is what makes the help text's "hold" advice TRUE.

PRIORITY 3 — item aging lanes (creates the second viable strategy): tag a few items as appreciating (wine/curio: value *1.08 per day held) and a few as perishable (Food/Potion: value *0.9 per day held, and exclude from carry). Store a `boughtDay` on bag instances (already have day in state) and apply in sellProjection/completeSell. Gives a genuine buy-and-hold lane vs fast-flip churn.

PRIORITY 4 — run-end liquidation so a hold is never pure loss: at win/loss, auto-sell remaining bag at dumpFactor into finalGold (shopEngine.js:431-432,444). Even a haircut beats total forfeiture and makes mid-run holds defensible.

DO FIRST regardless: fix the misleading advice. Until at least Priority 1+2 ship, change the help line (Shop.jsx:1033-1035) and the haggle note (Shop.jsx:790-791) to stop telling players to hold — current copy teaches a strictly losing line. Combined target: at least two coexisting strategies (fast-flip churn vs patient appreciation/spread-selling) that trade off against each other.

findings.title: Haggle minigame is rote after ~10 plays — one deterministic concession curve, no item/mood/event variance
findings.problem: Every haggle is mechanically identical: a slider/offer against a single, fully-deterministic AI. Kaito's concession is concession = clamp(0.55 + rapport*0.003, 0.55, 0.85) — a constant per run that barely moves. There is no per-item personality, no mood, no bluff, no mid-haggle event, no information asymmetry once 'appraise' unlocks (then you literally see value and the optimal offer is mechanical). The 'optimal play' is the same every time: open low/high, let him counter, accept when within conv. Patience (base 3) is the only variable and it's generous — you rarely run out. Because the math is transparent and stable, the minigame has no skill ceiling beyond 'know the floor/ceil,' and appraise removes even that. Result: by haggle ~10 the player is clicking through a known script. The quips (shopData.js:80-135) are charming but they're cosmetic — they don't change play.
findings.recommendation: Add variance and skill expression so no two haggles feel the same. Concrete: (1) Per-item haggle PERSONALITY: assign each item/category a concession profile — 'sentimental' items (music-box, carved-mask) Kaito barely budges on; 'overstocked' items he caves fast; 'mysterious' items have hidden value you must read his face to estimate. (2) Mood per haggle: a die-roll mood (eager/wary/stubborn) shown via portrait that shifts concession ±0.15 and patience ±1 — reward reading it. (3) Bluff/commit mechanic: a 'final offer — take it or leave it' button the player can use; if Kaito's hidden reservation is below it he folds, else you lose the deal — real risk. (4) Mid-haggle events: 'another customer eyes the item' (raises his floor), 'he's distracted' (free patience), 'he name-drops a memory' (rapport bonus if you deal fair). (5) Make appraise PARTIAL (a value RANGE, not exact) so reading him still matters. (6) Tie a small skill bonus to landing very close to the edge (a 'sharp eye' tip for buying within 3g of floor), rewarding precision over button-mashing the slider.

verification.reasoning:
I read shopEngine.js and shopData.js fully and traced the haggle math, plus the modal UI in Shop.jsx. The finding's core claims are accurate.

(1) CONCESSION IS A SINGLE DETERMINISTIC CURVE. shopEngine.js:276 — `const concession = clamp(0.55 + state.rapport * 0.003, 0.55, 0.85);` Grep confirms this is the ONLY concession; it's used at :283 (buy) and :303 (sell) and is driven exclusively by state.rapport. There is no per-item, per-category, per-rarity, per-event, or per-mood modifier. RARITY[].greed (shopData.js:29-32) only affects the asking-price markup (shopEngine.js:87,90), never the negotiation behavior.

(2) MOOD IS COSMETIC. setFace(...,"think"/"annoyed"/"insult") at :289/:309/:296 only sets the portrait + quip; it never feeds back into concession or patience. The finding's recommendation to make mood actually shift concession/patience correctly identifies it as display-only.

(3) APPRAISE LEAKS EXACT VALUE, AND THE SLIDER LEAKS THE THRESHOLD ANYWAY. perks.appraise prints `worth ~{value}` (Shop.jsx:567,603,714). Crucially, even WITHOUT appraise, the haggle slider paints Kaito's hard floor (buy) / ceiling (sell) as a visible EMBER tick computed unconditionally — Shop.jsx:666 `threshPct = pct(buy ? h.floor : h.ceil)`, rendered via trackBg into the slider at :829. So the optimal edge is visible from the first haggle; information asymmetry is minimal, which strengthens the finding's 'transparent math' point beyond what it stated.

(4) PATIENCE IS GENEROUS / CONVERGENCE IS A KNOWN SCRIPT. Base patience 3 (CONFIG.basePatience); a normal counter costs 1 (:286/:307); conv auto-completes within max(1, value*0.02) (:277,:284,:304). Traced a value=100 buy: offering just above the visible floor converges to your number in ~3 rounds without exhausting patience. The finding's 'open low/high, let him counter, accept when within conv; rarely run out' is mechanically correct.

(5) QUIPS ARE COSMETIC. Confirmed — selected via setFace, never alter price/patience/concession.

MINOR IMPRECISION (why I note it but still confirm): the finding calls concession 'a constant per run that barely moves.' It actually moves 0.55→0.85 as rapport climbs to its cap of 140 (:355,:395) — a real range. But higher concession only makes Kaito cave MORE (easier deals); it never changes the CHARACTER of the interaction, so the substantive conclusion (rote, no variance in how you haggle) holds. The phrasing understates the numeric movement without invalidating the point. This is a design-depth critique of the most-repeated interaction in the game, not a functional bug — appropriate for the depth/replayability lens, and 'high' is justified because it targets the headline mechanic.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
The original 6-point plan is well-targeted and actionable; keep it, with three refinements grounded in the code:

(A) CRITICAL ADD — hide/fuzz the threshold tick, not just the appraise number. The finding's point (5) 'make appraise a RANGE' is undercut by Shop.jsx:666-675,829, which already draws Kaito's exact floor/ceiling as a colored slider tick for EVERY haggle regardless of appraise. To create genuine 'read the merchant' skill, replace that hard EMBER tick with a fuzzy band whose width shrinks with rapport/appraise (e.g. ±15% of value at rapport 0, ±3% at high rapport), and gate the exact `worth ~{value}` text behind a deeper perk. Without this, adding hidden moods/personalities is wasted because the slider still paints his reservation line.

(B) Implement (1) per-item personality concretely as data, not code branches: add a `haggle` profile to each ITEM/category in shopData.js, e.g. { concession: 0.45, patience: -1, valueNoise: 0.18 } for 'sentimental' (music-box, carved-mask, fire-opal) vs { concession: 0.78, patience: +1 } for 'overstocked' (potions/food). Then in offer() compute `concession = clamp(base + rapport*0.003 + item.haggle.concession + mood.delta, 0.40, 0.90)` and `maxPatience += item.haggle.patience + mood.patience`. This keeps the reducer pure and the tuning in data.

(C) Implement (2) mood by rolling it in startHaggle() from the threaded rng (rng.int(3) → eager/wary/stubborn), store it on state.haggle.mood, render it via portrait + a distinct quip set, and apply its ±0.15 concession / ±1 patience in offer(). Reward reading it by making the mood observable BEFORE the first offer.

Points (3) bluff/commit 'final offer', (4) mid-haggle events, and (6) precision 'sharp eye' tip are all sound and fit the existing patience/streak plumbing (completeBuy/completeSell already compute over/under-value at :353 and :391 — extend that to grant a precision tip when the closed price is within `conv` of the floor/ceil). Effort 'L' is correct given changes span shopEngine.js (offer/startHaggle/complete*), shopData.js (per-item profiles + mood quips), and Shop.jsx (slider band, mood portrait, final-offer UI).

findings.title: Replayability collapses after one win — the story (the real hook) is fully consumed in a single run
findings.problem: The genuine emotional payload — Kaito's real bio revealed across 6 rapport tiers — is the strongest part of this game and the actual reason a recruiter/visitor would keep playing. But it is a one-time consumable: all 6 beats unlock on a single successful run (rapport caps at 140, top tier at 110, easily reached), the Codex then shows everything, and there is nothing new to see on run 2. Combined with the fixed 23-item catalog, 11 events, one strategy, and a trivially-winnable economy, there is literally no reason to play again after the first win. The score chase (bestGold/bestStreak in RECORDS) is weak because gold is uncapped-and-trivial (see economy finding) so 'best gold' just rewards grinding a solved loop. The RunEnd screen (Shop.jsx:979-994) shows stats but offers no next goal, no 'try harder mode,' no missing-content teaser.
findings.recommendation: Give post-first-win reasons to return. (1) Gate SOME story behind achievements/conditions other than rapport — e.g. extra Kaito anecdotes that only unlock on a no-insult run, a 'sold a legendary' run, a streak-of-10 run — so completionists must vary play. (2) Add an achievements board (10-15: 'Win without losing a haggle,' 'Survive a Taxman + Slow Day back-to-back,' 'Befriend Kaito by day 4,' 'Flip a Crystal Skull') surfaced in a new tab. (3) Daily/seeded challenge: a deterministic seed-of-the-day (you already have mulberry32 + seed in state — wire createRun to accept a date-derived seed) with a shareable score, giving a reason to return daily. (4) Difficulty modes (Cozy / Trader / Cutthroat) altering rent, patience, appraise — pairs naturally with the economy rebalance. (5) On RunEnd, show the NEXT unlock teaser ('1 achievement from a new Kaito memory') to pull the replay.

verification.reasoning:
Verified against the actual code. (1) There are exactly 6 RAPPORT_TIERS with the top beat at rapport 110 (shopData.js:164-207); rapport is capped at 140 (shopEngine.js:355,395). (2) The ONLY unlock path is crossing a rapport threshold at day-break — shopEngine.js:450-462 reads RAPPORT_TIERS[state.tier] and reveals the next card; there are no alternate/achievement-gated beats. (3) Unlocked lore is banked permanently to localStorage (Shop.jsx:113 lore[], 166-174) and the Codex marks any banked index as `got` forever (Shop.jsx:1088,1094-1110), so on run 2 the entire story is already shown — it is genuinely a one-time consumable across runs, exactly as claimed. (4) Grep for achievement/difficulty/challenge/Cozy/Cutthroat/daily-seed returned nothing: no achievements board, no difficulty modes, no seeded daily challenge. The seed is Date.now() only (Shop.jsx:149; RESTART seed at 997), even though mulberry32 + an integer seed in state (shopEngine.js:177-178) would make a date-derived deterministic seed trivial to wire — the recommendation's premise is accurate. (5) RunEnd (Shop.jsx:953-1005) shows a stat ledger + "story X/6" line + "New run" button with NO next-goal, harder mode, or missing-content teaser, confirming the stated gap. (6) Catalog/event counts check out: 23 ITEMS (shopData.js:38-60), 11 EVENTS (140-150). The records score-chase (bestGold/bestStreak, Shop.jsx:106-113) exists but is unstructured.

One overstatement to flag: "all 6 beats unlock on a single successful run … easily reached" is plausible but not as trivial as implied. Rapport gains are small and conditional — buys give +1/2/3 only when you overpay (shopEngine.js:352-353), sells give +1, or +3 only when selling into a wanted category below 96% of ceiling, plus +1 on a 3+ streak (shopEngine.js:390-392), and insults subtract 3 (295,314). Reaching 110 over 8 trading days demands deliberately fair/generous play; it is itself a soft goal, not a guaranteed by-product of any win. Even so, the thesis is intact: a trust-focused win drives rapport high, and a completionist exhausts all 6 within one (or at most two) runs, after which the story hook is permanently spent. The "uncapped-and-trivial gold" sub-claim is cross-referenced to a separate economy finding and not independently re-verified here.

Net: this is a real, accurately-described replayability/content limitation rather than a misreading. It is a design gap, not a code defect, but for the "depth, progression & replayability" lens that is precisely the subject. High severity is justified: the story is explicitly framed as the primary hook for a portfolio visitor/recruiter, and there is no structured reason to return once it's seen.
verification.refinedRecommendation: Add post-first-win re-engagement loops; all are scoped for a portfolio. (1) Split story unlocks so completion requires varied play, not just one high-rapport win: keep the 6 rapport beats but add ~4-6 bonus anecdote cards gated on distinct conditions (no-insult run — track an `insults` counter since insults already fire at shopEngine.js:295/314; flip a legendary — crystal-skull/fire-opal are the only two legendaries, shopData.js:54,60; streak-of-10 — state.streak already tracked; befriend Kaito by day 4). Surface them in the existing Codex grid (Shop.jsx:1086-1114), which already renders locked vs `got`, so the UI cost is small. (2) Add an achievements board (10-15 entries) as a new modal/tab reusing the Scrim+codexList pattern; persist earned ids in the RECORDS object (Shop.jsx:106-113) alongside lore. (3) Daily seeded challenge: the engine already threads an integer rngState (shopEngine.js:177-178) and RESTART takes a seed (Shop.jsx:997) — derive a seed from the UTC date (e.g. yyyymmdd) and add a "Daily" entry-point, storing the day's best score for a shareable result. (4) Difficulty modes (Cozy/Trader/Cutthroat) by parameterizing CONFIG (baseRent 45, rentGrowth 1.18, basePatience 3, dumpFactor 0.62 — shopData.js:10-23) per mode; pairs with the separate economy-rebalance finding. (5) On RunEnd (Shop.jsx:953-1005), replace the static "story X/6" line with a "next unlock" teaser computed from the nearest unmet achievement/lore condition ("1 fair run from a new Kaito memory") to actively pull a replay. Prioritize (1)+(5) first: they directly fix the "story consumed in one run" core defect at the lowest cost. Note: do NOT assume reaching rapport 110 is automatic on any win — gains are 1-4/deal and insults cost 3, so condition-gating still meaningfully varies play.

findings.title: Difficulty curve is inverted — the game gets easier as it progresses
findings.location: shopEngine.js:86-92 (rapport lowers ask/floor), 276 (rapport raises concession), 471-478 (perks compound), shopData.js:152 (rent)
findings.problem: Difficulty should rise; here it FALLS. As rapport climbs through the run: askRelief lowers Kaito's asking price (line 86), his floor drops (line 90), his concession rises (line 276), and you stack perks — appraise (perfect info), +2 patience, +4 bag slots, 5% discount. So late-game you have more gold, perfect information, cheaper buys, more bag space, and easier haggles — while the only escalating threat (rent, +18%/day) was already shown to be outpaced. The intended tension arc (scrappy start → mastery → climactic final rent) inverts into (mild start → effortless coast). The day-8 'climactic' rent of 143g is laughable next to a bankroll typically in the high hundreds/thousands by then.
findings.recommendation: Re-shape the curve so pressure peaks at the end. (1) Make the final 1-2 days spike threat: a 'season-end tax' or a one-time large balloon payment on day 8 (e.g. rent_day8 = 3x normal, telegraphed from day 1) so the whole run is saving toward a real wall. (2) Decouple perks from making haggling EASIER — recast perks as tools that open new STRATEGIES rather than auto-wins (e.g. appraise → shows a value range not exact; discount → only on one category; replace +slots with 'a ledger that forecasts demand'). (3) Add escalating downside events in late days (a rival merchant undercuts your sell prices; a theft that costs a bag slot for a day) so the back half has teeth. (4) Cap how much rapport can soften Kaito so he never becomes a pushover. Target: win rate should be lowest if you coast and highest if you play sharp at the end.

verification.reasoning:
I read shopEngine.js and shopData.js in full and verified every cited mechanic.

LEVERS THAT FALL AS RAPPORT RISES (all confirmed):
- askRelief (engine:86-87): ask = value*(1.3 + greed - min(0.16, rapport*0.0015)). At rapport>=107 this caps at -0.16, directly lowering Kaito's opening ask.
- floor (engine:90): floor = value*(1.06 + greed*0.3 - rapport*0.0006). Confirmed it drops with rapport — BUT note line 92 hard-clamps floor at value*1.03, which the finding omits. For a common (greed 0), base floor 1.06 - 0.066(at rapport110) = 0.994 -> clamped to 1.03, so rapport's floor effect is largely absorbed by the clamp. This is a minor overstatement of ONE of four levers, not a refutation.
- concession (engine:276): clamp(0.55 + rapport*0.003, 0.55, 0.85) — reaches the 0.85 cap at rapport 100, so Kaito moves much further toward the player's offer each round.
- perks (engine:471-478 + RAPPORT_TIERS): appraise=perfect info (engine:473, used to reveal value), +1 patience x2 tiers = +2, +2 slots x2 tiers = +4, discount = ask*0.95 & floor*0.97 (engine:89,91). All compound and all reduce friction. Confirmed.

THREAT SIDE: The only escalating pressure is rent = 45*1.18^(day-1) (data:13-14, engine:152). Verified day-8 rent = 45*1.18^7 = 143g. Events (engine:103, 62% chance) are random and symmetric — taxman rentMult 1.4 vs landlordAway 0.7, both in the same pool — so nothing in the back half scales difficulty UP with progress. There is no progression-linked downside whatsoever.

RAPPORT IS REACHABLE: buy gain 1-3 (engine:353), sell gain 1-4 (engine:390-392); a profitable flip yields ~2-5 rapport. With 6 slots and several flips/day, 50-110 rapport across 8 days is routine, so tiers (12/28/46/66/88/110) and their perks genuinely unlock mid-run. The compounding the finding describes really happens.

BANKROLL VS RENT: wanted-item flips buy near floor (~1.03-1.1x value) and sell near ceil (1.55-1.9x value), netting ~50%+ per flip plus hot-streak tips (engine:373-374). Bankroll growth is multiplicative while rent growth is a fixed 1.18x; the "high hundreds/thousands by day 8 vs 143g rent" characterization is sound in direction.

CONCLUSION: The difficulty curve is genuinely inverted — every progression lever softens Kaito while the sole escalating threat is outpaced. This is a real, structural balance defect, not a subjective preference. High severity is justified: it undermines the core tension arc of a roguelike. The only inaccuracy is the un-noted line-92 floor clamp (one of four levers is weaker than stated), which warrants no downgrade given the other three uncapped/weakly-capped levers and the unambiguous overall direction.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Keep the four prongs; tighten them to the actual code:

(1) Make the finale a real wall. Add a telegraphed balloon payment: e.g. data: add finalDayRentMult and in engine:152 apply rent *= (day === LAST_TRADING_DAY ? CONFIG.finalDayRentMult(~2.5-3) : 1). Surface "Season-end tax: ~Xg due night of day 8" in the HUD from day 1 so the whole run is a savings target. Tune so a coasting player can't cover it by inertia.

(2) Decouple perks from auto-easing haggling. appraise -> show a value RANGE (e.g. value +/- rarity.jit band) not exact (currently feeds perfect price-line reading); discount -> restrict to one rotating category; swap one +slots tier for an information/strategy perk (e.g. a 1-day demand forecast) instead of more capacity.

(3) Add escalating, progression-linked downside in late days — not just the existing symmetric random events. e.g. from day 6+, inject a "rival merchant" that lowers wanted-bonus ceilings (cut the (1+bonus) ceil in engine:246/502) or a one-day theft that drops a bag slot, scaling in frequency with day.

(4) Cap rapport softening on ALL levers, not just the floor. The buy floor is already clamped at value*1.03 (engine:92), but ask (engine:86) only caps askRelief at 0.16 and concession (engine:276) caps at 0.85 — both still let Kaito become a pushover. Lower those caps (e.g. askRelief max 0.08, concession max 0.72) AND/OR make late-day events partially negate rapport bonuses, so mastery still requires sharp final-day play rather than a coast. Target: lowest win rate for coasting, highest for playing sharp at the end.

findings.title: No customers other than Kaito — a missed dimension that would create real decisions
findings.location: shopData.js:3-7 (premise), shopEngine.js (entire — only Kaito as counterparty)
findings.problem: You buy from Kaito and sell back to Kaito. He is both your only supplier and only buyer, which is what makes the loop a closed, solvable arbitrage with no routing or competition. There's no market, no other NPCs, no demand the player can't fully see and exploit. This single-counterparty design is the structural root of the 'one dominant strategy' problem — there's nothing to weigh against the Kaito flip.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a second source/sink to create routing decisions and personality. Scoped for a portfolio: (1) Wandering customers who drop by the shop wanting specific items at varying prices/patience — sell to THEM at a premium (with their own haggle moods) vs sell back to Kaito safe-and-low. Each customer is a mini-character with one line of flavor — cheap content, high charm. (2) A periodic 'market day' / caravan (you already have the caravan event, shopData.js:141) where you can buy fresh stock cheap OR offload held inventory — a second supply channel. (3) Customers create demand Kaito doesn't, so 'hold for a customer' becomes a real strategy. (4) Special rare buyer events: 'a collector will pay 3x for any Curio, once' — a high-stakes hold target. This adds decision width without much new UI (reuse the haggle modal with a swapped portrait/name).

findings.title: Insult/rapport-loss penalty is toothless — no real consequence for greed
findings.location: shopEngine.js:290-298, 310-317 (insult: -2 patience, -3 rapport), 353 (fair-buy rapport gain), 391 (fair-sell gain)
findings.problem: The game's stated moral — 'deal fairly to earn his trust' — has almost no mechanical bite, so greed is nearly free. An insulting lowball costs 2 patience and 3 rapport, but patience is generous (base 3, often +bonus) and rapport is only needed for the story, not survival. Crucially, gouging him to the ceiling on EVERY wanted sale is the income-maximizing play and costs you nothing but slower rapport (sell rapport gain is just 1 instead of 3 if you don't undercut, line 391) — and since you don't NEED rapport to win, the optimal money strategy and the 'be a jerk' strategy are the same. The fair-dealing theme is purely cosmetic. There's no reputation system where greed has lasting cost (Kaito remembering, raising prices, fewer wants).
findings.recommendation: Make fairness a real strategic axis with teeth and reward. (1) A persistent 'goodwill' that Kaito remembers across DAYS: repeated gouging raises his floors/lowers his ceils for you (he wises up), so short-term greed has compounding long-term cost — fair dealers literally get better prices. (2) Make rapport perks matter for SURVIVAL (after economy rebalance the discount/patience perks become genuinely needed), so neglecting rapport to gouge actually risks the run. (3) Insults should occasionally end the haggle outright ('Get out of my shop') costing the item entirely, not just 2 patience. (4) Conversely, a generous deal can trigger a bonus (he throws in a free item, or a tip), so kindness is a viable economic strategy, not just flavor. This makes the central theme a decision instead of a label.

verification.reasoning:
I read shopEngine.js and shopData.js fully and grepped every rapport reference. The finding's raw facts are accurate: insult = -2 patience + -3 rapport (shopEngine.js:294-295 buy, 313-314 sell); fair-buy rapport gain is 1/2/3 by overValue (line 353); fair-sell gain is 1 when you gouge to ceiling vs 3 when price <= ceil*0.96 (line 391); basePatience is 3 (shopData.js:17); and rapport gates only perks/backstory, not a hard win condition. So the descriptive claims check out.

BUT the finding's central thesis — "gouging costs you nothing but slower rapport" — and its headline recommendation (#1: a system where "fair dealers literally get better prices") overstate the problem and propose a mechanic that ALREADY EXISTS in code. Rapport feeds directly into pricing three ways: (1) line 86 askRelief = min(0.16, rapport*0.0015) cuts Kaito's ask up to 16%; (2) line 90 subtracts rapport*0.0006 from his floor (~8% cheaper at max); (3) line 276 concession = clamp(0.55 + rapport*0.003, 0.55, 0.85) makes him cave faster the more he likes you. Higher rapport therefore compounds into cheaper buying — the profit engine of the game — so taking +1 instead of +3 rapport on every gouged sale has a real opportunity cost in worse future buy prices. Greed is NOT "nearly free." The finding even acknowledges "slower rapport" but dismisses it because rapport "isn't needed to win," which undersells this existing feedback loop.

The legitimate residual point: the magnitude of that feedback is small (a few % on prices), the perks (appraise/+patience/+2 slots/discount) are quality-of-life, not survival-critical, and there is genuinely NO persistent cross-day reputation memory (Kaito does not "wise up" and permanently raise floors against a serial gouger — the rapport-price coupling is symmetric and recoverable, not a lasting punishment). The insult penalty is also genuinely weak (-2 from base patience 3, -3 from a cap of 140; line 320 only ends the haggle when patience hits 0, never an instant "get out"). So the underlying design observation has merit.

This is a subjective game-design/balance OPINION, not a defect/bug, and one pillar of its recommendation is already partially implemented — hence "partial" rather than "confirmed."
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Reframe: the "fair dealers get better prices" loop already exists (shopEngine.js:86, 90, 276) but is too weak and too forgiving to make fairness a real decision. Concrete fixes, in priority order:

(1) Add PERSISTENT, ASYMMETRIC reputation memory — the genuinely missing piece. Track a per-run goodwill that rises slowly with fair deals and DROPS sharply on gouges/insults, and have it shift Kaito's floor/ceiling against a serial gouger that recovers only gradually (e.g., maintain state.goodwill separate from rapport; in priceShelfItem widen ask/floor when goodwill is low, and in the sell ceil apply a penalty when goodwill is low). Today the rapport→price effect is symmetric and instantly recoverable, so there is no lasting cost to greed — this is the finding's strongest valid point.

(2) Increase the magnitude of the existing feedback so it's felt: askRelief cap from 0.16 toward ~0.22 and concession scaling so honest play visibly opens prices.

(3) Make at least one rapport perk survival-relevant after an economy rebalance (e.g., the "discount" perk timed to arrive when rent escalation (baseRent 45 × 1.18^d) starts to bite around day 5-6), so neglecting rapport to gouge actually risks the run.

(4) Give the insult a real teeth option: a low chance (scaled by how low goodwill is) that an insulting offer ends the haggle outright ("Get out of my shop") and removes the shelf item for the day, instead of only -2 patience (shopEngine.js:294/313).

(5) Add a generosity upside: overpaying on a buy or selling below ceiling occasionally triggers a bonus (a thrown-in free low-value item or a flat tip), so kindness is an economic strategy, not just flavor.

Drop the recommendation's framing that "fair dealers get better prices" is new — it exists; the work is making it stronger, asymmetric, persistent, and survival-relevant.

findings.title: Content breadth is thin for replay — 23 items / 9 categories / 11 events that recur every run
findings.problem: 23 items across 9 categories and 11 events is enough for ONE playthrough's novelty but recurs identically every run, so the world feels memorized after run 2. Items have flavor text but are mechanically interchangeable within a category (only base value and rarity jitter differ) — there are no items with unique behaviors, set bonuses, or special interactions. Events are pure stat modifiers (wantBonus/rentMult/patience) with no player agency — they happen TO you rather than creating a choice. Rarity (common→legendary) affects only Kaito's greed markup and value jitter (shopData.js:28-33), not how an item plays.
findings.recommendation: Add mechanically distinct content, not just more rows. (1) ~8-10 'special' items with unique rules: an item that doubles in value if held 3 days; a cursed item that loses value but Kaito's collector friend pays huge for; a matched SET (3 chess pieces) worth a bonus if sold together; a fragile item that can break (condition system). (2) Make events offer CHOICES: 'Caravan in town — pay 50g for a mystery crate?' or 'A thief is about — lock your bag (skip a flip) or risk it?' Player-facing decisions, not silent modifiers. (3) Make rarity matter to play: legendary items are rarer on shelf, higher haggle-stubbornness, bigger rapport swings, and feed achievements. (4) Seasonal/themed item packs you unlock via the meta-progression spine so the catalog grows run-over-run. Prioritize a handful of memorable special items over many generic ones.

findings.title: Run silently starts on page load; no clean New Game / seed / pause framing for a casual visitor
findings.location: src/Pages/Home/Home.jsx (mounts all sections), Shop.jsx:149-152 (seedRef = Date.now() at mount), 211-222 (intro dialog only on focus)
findings.problem: Because Home mounts every section simultaneously and Shop seeds its run with Date.now() at mount (Shop.jsx:149), a run begins before the visitor has even scrolled to the game. For a portfolio piece this matters: a recruiter arrives mid-run with no framing, no clean 'New Game,' no difficulty/seed choice, and the only restart is via the run-end screen. There's no way to abandon a botched run and start fresh, no pause, and the intro dialog (Shop1) fires once on first focus but the game state may already have toasts/portrait changes if state were ever mutated pre-focus (currently it isn't, but the design is fragile). This also undercuts any future seeded-challenge feature.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit front-door. (1) Defer createRun until first focus (or until a 'Start trading' button is pressed) so the run begins when the player chooses. (2) A small title/menu state for the section: 'KAITO'S CURIOS — New Run / Continue / Daily Challenge / How to play' before the shop renders, giving framing and (later) mode/seed selection. (3) An always-available 'Abandon run' / restart control in the HUD (currently restart only exists at run end). (4) Optionally surface the seed so a player can replay or share a run — cheap given the engine is already fully seeded.

findings.title: Win/lose framing is binary and low-stakes — no scoring tiers, no 'how well did I do?'
findings.problem: Outcomes are just WIN (survived to day 9) or LOSE (missed a rent). Since winning is near-automatic (see economy finding), 'win' carries little achievement and 'lose' is rare and feels like a glitch rather than a fair loss. The RunEnd ledger shows raw stats but no graded result (no rank, no star rating, no 'you beat 70% of your runs'), so a win on day 8 with 2000g reads the same as a win with 200g. There's no aspirational ceiling to chase within a single run.
findings.recommendation: Add a graded result and intra-run goals. (1) End-of-run RANK (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Master based on final gold + rapport + days + streak vs thresholds), shown with a flourish — instantly gives a reason to replay for a higher rank. (2) Per-run objectives / 'contracts' (e.g. 'Net 500g by day 4 for a bonus,' 'Befriend Kaito before day 6') that grade the run. (3) After the economy rebalance, surface a tighter 'survival margin' so a narrow win FEELS earned. (4) Show percentile vs the player's own history ('your 2nd-best run'). Cheap to add on top of existing stats, big payoff for the score-chase loop.

findings.title: Quick Deal makes haggling skippable with little penalty — it short-circuits the only minigame
findings.location: Shop.jsx:853-860 (Quick deal button), shopEngine.js:328-334 (quickDeal accepts Kaito's number)
findings.problem: Every haggle offers 'Quick deal (Kaito's number)' which instantly accepts his ask (buy) or offer (sell). Because the economy is so loose, a player can Quick-Deal through the entire game — buy at ask, sell at his opening offer — and STILL win comfortably most days, never engaging the slider at all. The one minigame is optional, and the path of least resistance (one click) is good enough. This is fine as an accessibility/speed option but, combined with the loose economy, means a player can complete the whole game without ever learning or using the core mechanic.
findings.recommendation: Keep Quick Deal for accessibility but make engaging the haggle clearly worthwhile after the economy is tightened (where the ~15-30% you leave on the table by Quick-Dealing actually decides survival). Additionally: (1) on SELL, Quick Deal accepts his OPENING offer (the worst price) — consider relabeling it 'Dump (worst price)' so its cost is legible. (2) Add a 'Haggle' tutorial nudge the first time a player Quick-Deals a wanted item ('You left ~40g on the table — try haggling him up'). (3) Once difficulty modes exist, a 'Cutthroat' mode could disable Quick Deal entirely. The fix is mostly downstream of the economy rebalance.

findings.title: Perks are uninteresting because they're auto-granted and mostly 'more of the same'
findings.problem: The four perks — appraise, +1 patience, +2 slots, 5% discount — are all passive quality-of-life that make an already-easy game easier, and you don't choose them (they fire in a fixed order). +2 slots and +1 patience are particularly flat ('a bigger number'). 'appraise' arguably reduces engagement by removing the read-the-price guessing. None opens a new strategy or playstyle; none requires a tradeoff. With only 4 distinct perks (two of which repeat), there's no build identity even if choice were added.
findings.recommendation: Redesign perks into a draftable pool of ~10-12 with real strategic flavor and tradeoffs, chosen 1-of-3 at each tier (ties into the meta/build-variety finding). Examples: 'Silver Tongue' (Kaito concedes faster but starts higher); 'Collector's Eye' (see a value RANGE + tomorrow's wants); 'Deep Pockets' (+3 slots but slower rapport); 'Regular's Rapport' (streak tips +50% but insults cost double); 'Bulk Buyer' (buy 2 of a category at once); 'Appraiser' (exact value but Kaito haggles 10% harder — info for a price). Mutually-exclusive picks force build identity and make the rapport climb a series of meaningful choices instead of a conveyor belt.

summary: KAITO'S CURIOS is unusually polished for a portfolio mini-game: the haggle modal has a thoughtfully-painted slider, the HUD surfaces day/gold/rent/rapport/streak, a11y labels are dense and mostly accurate, focus is trapped and restored, reduced-motion and coarse-pointer are handled. The core loop (buy low / sell into demand / survive rent) is also genuinely well-explained IF the player reads the 6-line intro dialog and the help panel. The problems are concentrated in three areas. (1) Onboarding survives only because of text walls — a first-timer who skips the intro (the Skip button is right there) lands on a screen where the single most important mechanic, "haggle the price DOWN/UP," is never visibly demonstrated; the first haggle modal does not teach itself. (2) The haggle modal is over-instrumented (slider + stepper + free-text input all driving one value) and under-explained at the decision points: "Quick deal" silently accepts Kaito's number which, for an out-of-demand sell, is a 62%-of-value lowball trap; the gold/ember ticks and the sage/terracotta band are never labeled; patience pips have no inline legend. (3) Feedback is fragile: a single 3.4s toast slot means a day-start event banner is instantly clobbered by the first deal toast (or vice-versa), important inflection points (tier-up next deal, last day, near-bankruptcy where you literally cannot afford the cheapest shelf item) are never surfaced, and the offscreen always-running run silently burns the player's "first impression" seed before they ever arrive. None of these are crashes; they are the gap between "good" and the "AAA-feeling" north star. Highest-leverage fixes: a one-time interactive coachmark on the first haggle, splitting/queuing the toast channel, relabeling "Quick deal" contextually (and warning on lowball self-accept), surfacing a "tier-up on your next fair deal" cue, and gating/resuming the run on focus instead of starting it at page load.

findings.title: Always-running offscreen run burns the player's first-impression seed before they arrive
findings.problem: createRun(Date.now()) is called at component mount, which on this site is page load (all sections mount simultaneously, Home.jsx maps every section into the DOM). The run is fully live and ticking in state the moment the page loads, long before the user scrolls to section 4. There is no concept of 'start when focused' or 'continue/new run'. Consequence: the day-1 board (wants, shelf, rent, event) is fixed by a timestamp the player never experiences as a beginning. There is also no resume affordance — if a returning visitor scrolls away mid-run and the component never unmounts it's fine, but there's no 'you have a run in progress' framing, and conversely no fresh-start-on-arrival. The intro dialog and the actual game state are decoupled: Kaito says 'Welcome, a customer!' while a day is already half-defined behind him.
findings.evidence: Shop.jsx:149 `const seedRef = useRef((Date.now() >>> 0) || 1);` then :150-152 `useReducer(reduce, undefined, () => createRun(seedRef.current))` runs at mount. Home.jsx mounts all sections (:180 `Sections.map(...)`) translated off-screen. The intro dialog only fires later, on first focus (Shop.jsx:213-222).
findings.recommendation: Defer run creation until first focus: keep state null until `isfocus` first becomes true, then `dispatch({type:'RESTART', seed: Date.now()})` (or lazily createRun). Seed the run at the moment the intro dialog completes (in the openDialogWithCallback callback) so day 1 is generated when the player actually starts. If you want persistence across page loads, serialize the run to localStorage and offer a 'Continue run / New run' choice on arrival instead of silently resetting or silently continuing.

verification.reasoning:
Every factual claim in the finding checks out against the code:

- Shop.jsx:149 `const seedRef = useRef((Date.now() >>> 0) || 1)` captures the seed at component mount.
- Shop.jsx:150-152 lazily initializes useReducer with `createRun(seedRef.current)`, which runs once at mount.
- shopEngine.js:174-202 `createRun` immediately calls `generateDay(state)` (line 200), and generateDay (97-171) fully fixes day-1 wants, shelf, rent, and event from the seeded RNG. So the day-1 board IS fully determined at the moment of mount.
- Home.jsx:180 `Sections.map(...)` mounts all sections into the DOM simultaneously (translated off-screen via transform at :176), so Shop mounts at page load, not when scrolled to. Confirmed.
- There is no focus-gated or intro-gated reseed. `isfocus` (Shop.jsx:230) is used only for scroll-lock, never to create/gate the run. RESTART is dispatched only from the run-end modal (Shop.jsx:997). The intro-dialog callback (Shop.jsx:220) merely sets `{initDialog:false}` and does not reseed. So the intro and game state are indeed decoupled.

Why partial rather than confirmed: the finding's framing overstates the harm. The reducer (shopEngine.js:508-531) only advances on explicit user dispatch and there are NO timers/intervals — nothing 'ticks,' decays, or progresses while the section is offscreen. The phrases 'fully live and ticking in state the moment the page loads' and 'a day is already half-defined behind him' imply ongoing state evolution that does not occur; the state is merely pre-generated and inert. Because the day-1 board is random regardless and the player has no prior expectation of what 'their' seed should yield, the fixed-at-load board is not perceptible as wrong during play. The genuine issues that remain are real but cosmetic/structural: (1) a missed thematic beat (Kaito's 'Welcome, a customer!' intro is disconnected from an already-generated day), and (2) no continue/new-run affordance for a returning visitor (records persist via loadRecords/saveRecords at Shop.jsx:160-208, but the run itself does not, and there's no resume framing). These are polish/enhancement gaps, not a functional defect — hence 'high' is too strong; low/enhancement is accurate.

The recommendation is technically valid and actionable, though it leans on the incorrect 'ticking' premise.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Treat this as a thematic-polish + persistence enhancement, not a live-state bug (nothing ticks offscreen; the reducer only advances on user dispatch). Two concrete options:

1. Defer/refresh the seed at the true start. Keep `seedRef` but instead of seeding at mount, capture the seed when the intro dialog completes: in the openDialogWithCallback callback (Shop.jsx:220), dispatch `{ type: 'RESTART', seed: (Date.now() >>> 0) || 1 }` if the run is still pristine (day===1 and stats.deals===0). This regenerates day 1 (RESTART -> createRun -> generateDay, engine:526-527) at the moment Kaito actually 'opens,' aligning the intro beat with the generated board. Low risk since RESTART already exists.

2. Add real run persistence + a Continue/New choice. Records already persist (loadRecords/saveRecords, Shop.jsx:160-208) but the run does not. Serialize the full reducer state (it's plain JSON: seed, rngState, day, gold, bag, etc.) to localStorage on each dispatch via a useEffect, and on arrival offer 'Continue run / New run' in the intro flow. This is the more complete fix and turns the offscreen-mount quirk into a feature (returning visitors resume).

Minimum viable fix is option 1. Avoid the original's 'silently continue vs silently reset' wording — make the choice explicit if persisting.

findings.title: Core 'haggle up/down' mechanic is never demonstrated; skippable intro is the only teacher
findings.problem: A first-time player understands the loop ONLY by reading the 6-line intro dialog, which has a prominent Skip button (DialogMain.jsx:51). If skipped, the first thing they see is a shelf of cards showing a price and (without the appraise perk) no 'worth' — there is zero on-screen indication that tapping a card opens a negotiation, or that the goal is to push the number. The shelf title hint 'buy low · sell into demand' (Shop.jsx:359) is the only standing instruction and it does not explain haggling. The haggle modal itself does not teach: it drops the player straight into a slider+stepper+input with the goal implicit. There is no first-run coachmark, no 'try moving the slider down' nudge, no example.
findings.evidence: Skip exists at DialogMain.jsx:51-61. Shelf cards (ShelfItem, Shop.jsx:542-569) render name/price/icon only; the only standing copy is `buy low · sell into demand` (Shop.jsx:359). The haggle form (Shop.jsx:780-865) has hint text but it's about insulting, not about the basic 'drag toward his floor' goal.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-time interactive coachmark gated on a localStorage flag (e.g. kaitosCurios.taught.v1): on the FIRST haggle modal, point an arrow at the slider with 'Drag down to offer less — get as close to what it's worth as he'll allow' (buy) / 'Drag up' (sell), and highlight Quick deal vs Offer. Also add a persistent micro-legend under the slider naming the two ticks (his price / his limit) and the two bands. Make the first shelf card pulse with a 'Tap to haggle' tooltip on first run.

verification.reasoning:
The CORE issue is real: there is no proactive, in-context onboarding for the haggle mechanic. The intro dialog auto-opens once on first focus (Shop.jsx:213-222) and is fully skippable (DialogMain.jsx:32-41 skipDialog, button at :51-61). A player who skips it and never opens Help is left with only the shelf hint 'buy low · sell into demand' (Shop.jsx:359) as standing copy. ShelfItem does render name/price/icon only, with 'worth' gated behind the appraise perk (Shop.jsx:564-567), and there is genuinely no first-run coachmark/nudge anywhere — I grepped for taught/coachmark/tutorial/firstRun/tooltip and found nothing (only unrelated draggable matches). So the gap exists.

BUT the finding is mis-stated on three counts, which is why this is PARTIAL, not confirmed:

1) 'the only teacher' / 'the only standing instruction' is FALSE. The finding completely ignores the persistent '?' How-to-Play button in the HUD (Shop.jsx:336-346) which opens HelpPanel (Shop.jsx:1007-1069). That panel explicitly teaches the exact mechanic the finding says is undocumented: 'Buy low. Tap something on Kaito's shelf and haggle his price down toward what it's worth.' (lines 1024-1027) and the FLIP / sell-into-demand loop (lines 1028-1032). It is opt-in rather than auto-surfaced, but it is a standing, always-available teacher of haggling — directly contradicting the finding's central premise.

2) The claim that the haggle hint 'is about insulting, not about the basic drag toward his floor goal' is partly FALSE. The DEFAULT (non-insulting) hint at Shop.jsx:845-846 states the direction explicitly: 'Offer below his ask — but lowball him and he'll bristle' (buy) / 'Ask above his offer — but push too far and he'll balk' (sell). Combined with the 'Kaito asks/offers {N}' anchor label (Shop.jsx:782-786) and the 'Quick deal ({anchor})' button (line 859), the modal does convey the directional goal; it isn't purely implicit.

3) The cited location 'src/Pages/Home/Shop/Dialogs.jsx:178-215' is WRONG — that file doesn't exist there. The Shop1 intro is in src/Components/Dialog/Dialogs.jsx:178-215 (content/lines otherwise correct). Also note Dialogs.jsx:193-199 already states the loop in-dialog: 'Buy low off my shelf, then sell back whatever the town's after' and 'Haggle me down, haggle me up... but watch my face.'

Severity: 'high' is too strong for a portfolio mini-game whose loop is taught in TWO places (auto intro dialog + persistent Help panel) and whose modal already shows the anchor and a directional hint. The remaining defect is the absence of proactive, in-context onboarding for a player who dismisses both — a legitimate polish/UX gap but not blocking. Downgrade to medium.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Reframe from 'no teacher exists' (false — there is an auto intro dialog AND a persistent ? How-to-Play panel at Shop.jsx:336-346 / 1007-1069) to 'no proactive, in-context onboarding for players who skip the intro.' Concrete, accurate fixes:

1) First-haggle coachmark gated on a localStorage flag (e.g. kaitosCurios.taught.v1, persisted alongside the existing records in saveRecords): on the FIRST time HaggleModal opens, anchor an arrow to the slider with 'Drag toward what it's worth — closer to his floor = more profit, but lowball him and patience drops' (buy) / 'Drag up toward his ceiling' (sell), and call out Quick deal vs Offer. Dismiss on first slider interaction.

2) Make the existing directional hint (Shop.jsx:845-846) a persistent micro-legend, not just a one-liner: under the slider, label the gold tick ('Kaito's price') and the ember tick ('he won't cross this') and the sage/terracotta bands ('fair' / 'he'll balk'). These ticks/bands already render (Shop.jsx:663-675) but are unlabelled, so first-timers can't decode the painted track.

3) On first run only, pulse the first affordable shelf card and show a 'Tap to haggle' tooltip (the title attribute at Shop.jsx:550 already carries flavor+flipHint but is hover-only and silent on touch). Clear it once any card is tapped.

4) Cheapest high-leverage fix: auto-open the existing HelpPanel once on the very first run (same localStorage flag) instead of building new coachmark UI — it already explains 'Tap something on Kaito's shelf and haggle his price down' (Shop.jsx:1025-1026). This alone closes most of the gap with minimal code.

Also correct the finding's citation: the intro dialog is in src/Components/Dialog/Dialogs.jsx (not src/Pages/Home/Shop/Dialogs.jsx).

findings.title: Single 3.4s toast slot: day-start event banner and deal/error toasts clobber each other
findings.problem: Toast is a single render slot driven by state.toast.n; each new toast replaces the last and resets the 3.4s timer. The engine emits the day-event description as a toast at day start (sleep:467, ackBackstory:486) — 'Town Festival: Everyone's buying!' This is important, multi-clause copy. But the very first action a player takes that day (a failed buy, a bag-full attempt, an insult) also fires a toast and instantly overwrites the event banner — or, if the player acts fast, the event banner overwrites their action feedback. Important context and action feedback compete for one ephemeral channel. There is no queue and no persistence of the day event (the eventChip in WantsBoard does persist it, but only if an event exists AND the player looks left — the toast is the attention-grabber).
findings.evidence: Toast.jsx logic: `setShown(toast.text); setTimeout(()=>setShown(null),3400)` keyed on `[n,toast]` (Shop.jsx:1139-1144) — one slot, last-write-wins. toast() in engine just increments n (shopEngine.js:61-63). Day event toast fired at sleep (shopEngine.js:467) and ackBackstory (:486). Errors like 'Your bag is full' (startHaggle, :222) and 'You don't have the coin' (completeBuy, :342) use the same channel.
findings.recommendation: Separate channels: render the day-event as a distinct, longer-lived 'today's news' banner (or auto-open a small day-start card) and keep the toast strictly for transient action feedback. For the toast itself, implement a small FIFO queue (cap 2-3) so a deal toast doesn't eat an error toast; show each for 2.5-3s sequentially. At minimum, make error toasts (bag full, can't afford) sticky until the player's next interaction since they're actionable.

verification.reasoning:
The core mechanical claim is CONFIRMED by reading the code. Toast is a single render slot with last-write-wins semantics: Shop.jsx:1136-1149 keeps one `shown` state, calls `setTimeout(()=>setShown(null),3400)` keyed on `[n,toast]`, and the cleanup clears the prior timer — so every new toast replaces the text and resets the 3.4s clock. It is fed directly from engine state via `<Toast toast={state.toast} />` (Shop.jsx:440). The engine's `toast()` just bumps `n` (shopEngine.js:61-63). The day-event banner IS emitted as a toast at day start in both `sleep` (shopEngine.js:467) and `ackBackstory` (:486) as `${event.title}: ${event.text}`, and the two error toasts ("Your bag is full" at :220, "You don't have the coin" at :341) share the exact same single channel with no queue. So event banner vs. action feedback genuinely compete for one ephemeral slot — the described defect exists.

However, the finding is PARTIAL/mis-stated in three ways:\n1) Line-number sloppiness: the location lists "222/297/317/342 (other toasts)" but only lines 220 and 341 are actual `toast()` calls. Lines 297 and 317 are `sfx(next,\"BackClick\")` on insults, not toasts (verified via grep — the ONLY toast call sites in the engine are 220, 341, 467, 486). So \"other toasts\" at 297/317 is wrong.\n2) The recommendation's premise \"a deal toast doesn't eat an error toast\" is false: deal completions (completeBuy :345-360, completeSell :363+) resolve into the haggle \"deal\" status panel + sfx, never a toast. There are no deal-success toasts. The only real collisions are event-banner-vs-error and error-vs-error.\n3) Impact is meaningfully mitigated, which the finding admits but then largely discounts: the event persists in the always-visible `eventChip` in the WantsBoard left column (Shop.jsx:516-521) for the entire day. So the *information* is never lost — only the transient toast can be clobbered. Likewise the two errors are short, self-explanatory, and immediately re-triggerable by repeating the blocked action.

Given the persistent eventChip and the absence of deal toasts (the worst-case \"important deal feedback eaten\" scenario doesn't exist), this is a genuine but minor polish issue, not high severity. Adjusting to medium (arguably low).
verification.refinedRecommendation: Keep the fix but correct its framing. There are only three toast sources: the day-event banner (shopEngine.js:467,486) and two error toasts (bag full :220, can't afford :341) — there are no deal-success toasts, so don't justify the queue with that. Concrete actions: (1) Stop routing the day-event through the toast channel entirely — it already persists in the eventChip (Shop.jsx:516-521). Instead, briefly highlight/pulse the existing eventChip at day start (e.g. an `isNew` flag that adds an animated outline for ~4s), or auto-open a small dismissable \"Today's News\" card on the first day a non-trivial event occurs. This frees the toast slot for transient feedback and removes the most jarring collision. (2) For the two error toasts, since they are actionable, make them sticky: render them in their own dedicated error slot that persists until the player's next dispatch (clear on any subsequent action), rather than auto-dismissing at 3.4s and sharing the slot. (3) Only if you keep multiple transient toasts, a small FIFO (cap 2) showing each ~2.5s sequentially is sufficient — but with only two short error strings it's likely overkill; the dedicated error slot in (2) is the higher-value, lower-effort fix. Net effort: S–M, mostly a channel split rather than a full queue.

findings.title: 'Quick deal' on an out-of-demand sell silently accepts a 62%-of-value lowball — a trap with no warning
findings.location: src/Pages/Home/Shop/Shop.jsx:853-860 (Quick deal button); shopEngine.js:246-247 (opening offer), 333 (quickDeal accepts h.offer)
findings.problem: For a sell, Kaito's opening offer for an UNWANTED item is value*0.38 (shopEngine.js:247). 'Quick deal (Naccept)' dispatches QUICK_DEAL which calls completeSell at exactly h.offer (shopEngine.js:333) — i.e. it accepts that 38% opening lowball, not the dumpFactor ceiling (0.62). A new player reads 'Quick deal' as 'the fast, fair option' and clicks it, dumping the item for far below even its already-poor non-demand ceiling, almost always at a steep loss. The button shows the number but never frames it as 'his opening lowball' vs 'the most he'll pay (Nceil)'. The showLoss note (Shop.jsx:788-793) explains the ceiling but does not warn that Quick deal is BELOW that ceiling.
findings.evidence: shopEngine.js:247 `const offer = round(inst.value * (wanted ? 0.85 : 0.38));`. Quick deal label uses `anchor` = h.offer for sells (Shop.jsx:613, 859 `Quick deal ({g(anchor)})`). quickDeal -> completeSell(next, h.offer) (shopEngine.js:333). The dumpFactor ceiling 0.62 is what sellProjection shows on the card (shopEngine.js:502), so the card promises ~0.62 but Quick deal delivers 0.38.
findings.recommendation: Relabel 'Quick deal' contextually: for sells it is 'Take his offer (Nx)' — and when that offer is below the achievable ceiling or below paid, add inline subtext '(his opening — you can do better by asking up)'. Optionally disable/secondary-style Quick deal for sells when it would lock a loss, or add a one-time confirm. Long-term, raise the unwanted opening offer closer to the ceiling (e.g. dumpFactor*0.85) so Quick deal isn't a punishment for trusting the obvious button.

verification.reasoning: Every factual claim is accurate against the actual code. (1) For an UNWANTED sell, the opening offer is value*0.38 — shopEngine.js:247 `const offer = round(inst.value * (wanted ? 0.85 : 0.38));`. (2) The unwanted ceiling is the dumpFactor 0.62 — shopEngine.js:246 and the card/sell selector both surface it via sellProjection (shopEngine.js:502 `const ceil = round(inst.value * (wanted ? 1 + w.bonus : CONFIG.dumpFactor));`). (3) Quick deal dispatches QUICK_DEAL → quickDeal() → completeSell(next, h.offer) at shopEngine.js:333, i.e. it accepts the 0.38 opening, NOT the 0.62 ceiling. (4) The button is labelled `Quick deal ({g(anchor)})` where anchor = h.offer for sells (Shop.jsx:613, 859) — it shows the raw number but never frames it as "his opening lowball" vs the achievable ceiling. (5) The showLoss note (Shop.jsx:788-793) explains the ceiling ("best you'll get is ~{g(proj.ceil)}") but does not warn that Quick deal lands BELOW that ceiling. So a player who trusts "Quick deal" as the fast/fair option locks in ~0.38 of value, almost always a loss versus what they paid.
