The defect and its mechanism are real and correctly described.\n\nTwo mitigations the finding under-states, which is why I downgrade severity from high to medium rather than confirming high outright: (a) Quick deal is the SECONDARY-styled button (Shop.jsx:855 `className={styles.btnSecondary}`), not the primary. The PRIMARY button defaults to "Offer {price}" where price is pre-seeded a third up the fair band — h.offer + (h.ceil - h.offer) * 0.33 ≈ value*0.46 (Shop.jsx:625, 641) — so the most prominent action already beats Quick deal and pushes the player to negotiate. (b) The trap is specifically the PRE-counter click; in the patience-exhausted final state the "Accept {h.offer}" button (Shop.jsx:771) uses the negotiated offer that has been ratcheted up toward the ceiling by offer() (shopEngine.js:303-305), which is legitimate. So the worst-case "silently accept 38%" only fires when a fresh-haggle Quick deal is clicked. It's a genuine, unwarned loss-trap (and in a rent-driven roguelike a lost flip can be fatal), but the secondary styling plus a better-default primary button meaningfully reduce how often a player blunders into it — medium, not high.
verification.refinedRecommendation: The fix direction is correct; tighten it. (1) Make the label contextual and honest about what it is: for sells render "Take his offer ({g(h.offer)})" instead of "Quick deal", since "Quick deal" wrongly implies a fair fast-track. (2) When h.offer < h.ceil (always true for unwanted, value*0.38 < value*0.62) OR h.offer < paid, add inline subtext under the button, e.g. "his opening — ask up to ~{g(h.ceil)}", reusing the proj.ceil already computed for showLoss (Shop.jsx:657). (3) Keep it btnSecondary (already done) and gate a loss-locking sell behind a one-time confirm, or simply suppress the Quick-deal button entirely on sells when h.offer would lock a loss (h.offer + projected tip < (h.inst.paid ?? h.value)), nudging the player to the negotiate path. (4) Best long-term tuning fix: raise the unwanted opening offer from 0.38 closer to the ceiling, e.g. `0.38` → `CONFIG.dumpFactor * 0.8` (≈0.50), at shopEngine.js:247, so the gap between "take his offer" and the achievable ceiling is a haggling reward rather than a punishment for trusting the obvious button. Note the primary "Offer" default (~0.46) already sits between these, so 0.50 keeps Quick-deal a hair below the negotiate default — preserving the incentive to haggle without the steep 0.38 trap.

findings.title: Slider band colors and the two ticks are never labeled — the modal's central affordance is a guess
findings.problem: The slider track is painted with a sage 'fair' band, a terracotta 'he'll balk' band, a gold tick at Kaito's number, and an ember tick at his hard threshold (floor/ceil). This is a lot of encoded meaning with zero visible legend. The only textual help is the slideHint ('lowball him and he'll bristle'), which never says what the gold line vs the ember line mean, or that green=safe / red=insult. A sighted new player cannot map 'that orange vertical line' to 'the lowest he'll go.' Screen-reader users get even less — the slider's aria-valuetext is just 'N gold' (Shop.jsx:837) with no fair/insult context, and the ticks/bands are pure CSS background with no semantic equivalent.
findings.evidence: trackBg composes two ticks + a band via CSS gradients (Shop.jsx:673-675); the gold tick is anchorPct (Kaito's number), the ember tick is threshPct (floor/ceil). The slider aria is `aria-valuetext={`${Math.round(price)} gold`}` (Shop.jsx:837) — no band context. No legend element exists near the slider.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact legend row under the slider: a gold swatch 'his price' and an ember swatch 'his limit', plus 'green = he'll deal · red = insult'. Enrich aria-valuetext to e.g. `${price} gold — fair, he'll likely counter` / `...too low, he'll take it as an insult` based on the insulting/atAnchor flags. Consider labeling the ticks with tiny inline captions on first run.

findings.title: No surfacing of near-bankruptcy / soft-lock: player can be unable to afford the cheapest item with no guidance
findings.problem: If gold drops below the cheapest shelf floor and the bag is empty (or holds only loss-making items), every shelf card is disabled (affordable=false) and the player has nothing profitable to sell. The UI offers no diagnosis — cards just look locked, the only path forward is CLOSE UP SHOP into a rent they can't pay. There's no 'you're low on coin — sell something or close up' nudge, and no explicit 'this is your last viable move' framing. A new player can sit confused at an all-locked shelf. Relatedly, the all-locked state and the legit 'sold out' state look different (sold out shows a message, all-locked just dims everything) but both end the productive day.
findings.evidence: ShelfItem affordable = `state.gold >= it.floor && state.bag.length < slots` (Shop.jsx:370); locked cards get cardLocked and disabled (Shop.jsx:544-549). The only empty-shelf message is soldOut (Shop.jsx:377-379). No engine state or UI flags 'all shelf items unaffordable' or 'cannot make rent this turn'.
findings.recommendation: Detect the stuck state in the component (no affordable shelf item AND no profitable bag sale) and show a persistent helper line in the shelf area: 'Low on coin — sell what's in your bag, or close up to settle rent.' If gold < cheapest floor AND bag empty, surface it explicitly. Optionally add a small safety valve (a guaranteed cheap flip each day already exists via the cheap-want bias in generateDay:122 — make sure its floor is reliably affordable from start gold).

findings.title: Imminent rapport tier-up (next perk + backstory) is never previewed as 'one good deal away'
findings.location: src/Pages/Home/Shop/Shop.jsx:446-481 (Rapport); shopEngine.js:451-462 (tier crossed only at sleep)
findings.problem: Rapport tiers unlock a perk AND a backstory card — the single biggest progression payoff and the whole point of the 'deal fairly' loop. But the only signal is the small HUD progress bar caption ('N / 12 -> Appraising eye'). When the player is one fair deal away from a tier, nothing celebrates that or nudges 'deal fairly now to unlock.' Worse, the tier is only resolved at sleep (shopEngine.js:451), so even after crossing the threshold mid-day, the bar shows 'full/over' with no 'unlocks at day's end' messaging — the payoff is deferred and unannounced until the backstory modal appears next morning, which can feel disconnected from the deal that earned it.
findings.evidence: Tier crossing handled only in sleep() (shopEngine.js:451-462) producing phase 'backstory' next morning. Rapport bar caption is the sole live indicator (Shop.jsx:455-457). No 'tier-up imminent' or 'unlocked, opens tonight' cue anywhere.
findings.recommendation: When state.rapport is within ~3 of the next tier.at, add a glow/pulse to the rapport bar and a tooltip 'One fair deal from: <perk> + a memory.' The instant the threshold is crossed mid-day, fire a toast 'Kaito's warming up — he'll share something at day's end' and mark the bar 'ready'. This ties the reward to the action that earned it instead of surfacing it a screen later.

findings.title: Last-day / win-imminent stakes are not surfaced; 'DAY n / 8' is the only signal
findings.problem: Winning = surviving to the morning of day 9 (8 trading days). The only indication of how close you are is 'DAY n / 8' in the corner. On the final trading day there is no 'last day — survive tonight's rent to win' framing, and the rent escalation (×1.18/day, so day 8 rent ≈ 45×1.18^7 ≈ 144g, more with a taxman event) is never previewed as a climbing curve. A new player has no sense of the finish line approaching or whether they're on track. The CLOSE UP SHOP button shows tonight's rent but not 'this is the last one' on day 8.
findings.evidence: hudDay shows `DAY {state.day}` + `/ {LAST_TRADING_DAY}` (Shop.jsx:278-281). Victory at newDay>=victoryDay in sleep (shopEngine.js:442). endDay button sub is static `rent {g(state.rent)} due` (Shop.jsx:416). No last-day or 'on track to win' messaging.
findings.recommendation: On the final trading day, change the day chip / end-day button to 'FINAL DAY — pay tonight's rent to win' and color it. Add a tiny rent-trend indicator (e.g. 'rent +N tomorrow') so the climb is legible. Consider a 'days left: N' pill and, on day-end ledger, 'cover rent N more night(s) to win.'

findings.title: Modal Kaito quip is duplicated; the standing portrait bubble is merely hidden (visibility), wasting layout and confusing reduced-motion
findings.problem: During any modal, the standing Kaito's speech bubble is set to visibility:hidden but keeps its reserved height (Shop.jsx:488), while the modal renders its own portrait + quip (Shop.jsx:701-704). Two Kaito portraits coexist on screen (one behind the scrim, one in the dialog), and the same character speaks from two places conceptually. The comment acknowledges this ('single source... keep reserved height') but the result is a ghost empty bubble and a redundant second portrait. It's a minor immersion break and slightly wasteful, and the muted state is keyed off modalUp which includes Help/Codex where Kaito isn't even speaking.
findings.evidence:
KaitoPortrait bubble: `aria-hidden={muted} style={muted ? {visibility:'hidden'} : undefined}` (Shop.jsx:488). HaggleModal renders its own `` + `

{state.quip}

` (Shop.jsx:701-704). modalUp = showHelp||showCodex||phase!=='shop' (Shop.jsx:225).
findings.recommendation: Since the modal scrim already darkens the stage and owns the conversation, fully fade the standing portrait+bubble (opacity, pointer-events none) rather than just hiding the bubble text — or better, have the modal visually 'lift' the same portrait (shared element) so it reads as one Kaito stepping forward to haggle. Don't mute the standing quip for Help/Codex (he's not talking there); scope muted to haggle/dayEnd/backstory only.

findings.title: Three redundant controls for one value (slider + stepper + free-text) with subtle sync seams
findings.problem: The offer value is driven by a slider, a +/- stepper, AND an editable text input. This is power-user generous but adds cognitive load for a casual cozy-game audience and creates sync seams: the text draft is only committed on blur (onBlur=commitDraft, Shop.jsx:814), but submitOffer reads draftPrice() directly so a typed-not-blurred value is honored on submit (good) — yet the slider/stepper continue to show the OLD committed price until blur, so for a moment the input says 120 while the slider thumb sits at 100. The step is value-relative (2%, Shop.jsx:614) so stepper increments are non-round numbers that don't match what a player typing whole numbers expects. For a cozy game, three inputs is over-engineered.
findings.evidence: price state + draft state (Shop.jsx:627-628); commitDraft on blur (:814); submitOffer uses draftPrice() (:683-687) while slider value={clampP(price)} (:834) and stepper mutate price (:801,820). step = `Math.max(1, Math.round(h.value*0.02))` (:614).
findings.recommendation: For the casual audience, consider demoting the free-text input to an optional 'type exact' affordance (or remove it) and lead with the slider + stepper, which are self-evident. If keeping all three, unify on a single source of truth: update price live as the user types (debounced) so the slider thumb tracks the text, eliminating the blur seam. Round the stepper to a friendly increment (5g or 10g) rather than 2% of value.

findings.title: Information scent without the appraise perk: cards hide 'worth', so buy decisions are blind early game
findings.problem: Until the appraise perk unlocks (rapport tier 1 at 12), shelf cards show only the ask price and a flip% tag — never 'worth ~Ng'. A first-time player therefore cannot judge whether an ask is good or a ripoff; 'buy low' is unactionable when 'low relative to what?' is hidden. The flip tag (+N%) helps for wanted items but the math (buy near floor, sell at value×(1+bonus)) is opaque. Bag cards do show est-profit even without appraise (BagItem, Shop.jsx:572-606) which is great — but the buy side, where the player spends scarce starting coin, is the blind one. This makes the crucial first few buys feel like guesses, which undercuts the 'I understand the loop' feeling.
findings.evidence: ShelfItem worth line gated: `{appraise && worth ~{g(item.value)}}` (Shop.jsx:567); aria label similarly conditional (:537-539). Appraise unlocks only at rapport 12 (shopData.js:166-170).
findings.recommendation: Give the player at least a coarse buy-side signal pre-appraise: e.g. show a rough 'deal quality' chip on shelf cards (Good price / Fair / Steep) derived from ask vs value bands without revealing the exact number, or surface the flip ceiling for wanted items ('flips to ~Ng'). Reserve the exact 'worth ~Ng' for the appraise perk so it still feels like a reward, but don't leave new players fully blind on their most consequential decisions.

findings.title: Selling-at-a-loss is explained but the est-profit ceiling can mislead (shows ≤ best case, not likely outcome)
findings.problem: BagItem shows est-profit as the CEILING (best case if you haggle to the top), prefixed with ≤ when positive (Shop.jsx:600-601). This is honest but easy to misread as the expected value — a player sees '≤+40g', haggles imperfectly, lands at the opening offer, and nets far less (and for unwanted items the opening is 0.38×value, a big gap from the 0.62 ceiling). The ≤ glyph is subtle and unexplained; many players won't parse it. So the headline number systematically over-promises relative to a typical (non-perfect) haggle, which erodes trust in the UI's numbers.
findings.evidence: bagProfit renders `{estProfit > 0 ? '≤' : ''}{gSigned(estProfit)}` (Shop.jsx:600-601). estProfit = ceil - basis (shopEngine.js:504) i.e. best case. Opening sell offer is 0.85×value (wanted) or 0.38×value (unwanted) (shopEngine.js:247), far below ceil for unwanted.
findings.recommendation: Show a range rather than just the ceiling on bag cards (e.g. '+10 to +40g'), or label the ceiling explicitly ('up to +40g'). For unwanted items where the spread is huge, the range communicates the risk far better than a lone optimistic number. Add a tiny tooltip on the ≤ explaining 'best case if you haggle him to his limit.'

findings.title: Backstory card button says 'Open the shop' but the prior day-end already 'opened' — sequencing of dayEnd -> backstory -> shop is unsignposted
findings.problem: The night sequence is: CLOSE UP SHOP -> DayEnd ledger ('Pay rent & turn in') -> SLEEP. If a tier was crossed, sleep routes to a Backstory modal BEFORE generating the next day; its button reads 'Open the shop' and ACK regenerates the day. So on a tier night the player clicks through two committing modals (pay rent, then read story) with no indication a story is coming — it can feel like an extra unexpected gate, and the 'Open the shop' button gives no sense that this is the NEXT day starting. The day number also advances silently between these modals (sleep increments day at shopEngine.js:438-439 before the backstory branch).
findings.evidence: DayEnd primary button 'Pay rent & turn in' -> SLEEP (Shop.jsx:921-924). sleep increments day (shopEngine.js:438-439) then may set phase 'backstory' (:459). Backstory button 'Open the shop' -> ACK_BACKSTORY -> generateDay (Shop.jsx:945, shopEngine.js:480-488).
findings.recommendation: Add a small 'Day N+1' or 'The next morning...' header to the Backstory card so the day-advance is legible, and change the button to 'Open Day N+1'. On the DayEnd ledger, if a tier will cross, tease it ('Kaito has something to share tonight ♥'). This turns an unexpected gate into an anticipated reward.

findings.title: Patience drain has no inline explanation at the point of cost; pips are decorative until you read a tooltip
findings.problem: Patience is a core haggle resource (a normal counter costs 1, an insult costs 2, at 0 he goes final). The pips have a good aria-label and title (Shop.jsx:877-879) but no VISIBLE caption — a mouse player who doesn't hover, or a touch player, sees dots quietly disappear with no inline 'why'. When a pip drains there's no transient '−1 patience' feedback tied to the offer that caused it, and the jump to 'final offer' (final=true) can feel abrupt: the form is replaced by a take-it-or-leave-it screen (Shop.jsx:753-778) with no recap of what spent the last pip.
findings.evidence: Patience pips rendered with title/aria only (Shop.jsx:876-889). offer() decrements patience silently (shopEngine.js:286 `hh.patience -= 1`, :294/:312 `-= 2` on insult). Final screen at h.final (Shop.jsx:753-778).
findings.recommendation: Add a tiny visible caption under the pips ('Patience — bad offers cost more') and a transient '−1' / '−2 (insult!)' float on the pip row when it drops. When patience hits 1, color it as a warning (pipLow class exists, Shop.jsx:885 — ensure it's visually loud). On the final screen, prepend one line: 'You've worn out his patience — last offer.'

findings.title: 'Rotate your device' gate locks out all portrait users entirely — the whole site (and game) is landscape-only with no fallback
findings.problem: When viewport width <= height, the entire site renders HorizontalEnjoyer ('Please tilt your device Horizontally') and nothing else. On a phone held normally (portrait), a visitor sees only a rotate prompt — the game is unreachable. Many users browse one-handed in portrait and won't rotate; the bounce rate cost is real for a portfolio piece. The Shop in particular is dense (left column + shelf + bag bar) and was clearly designed for landscape, but a 'rotate to play this game' gate scoped to the section would be far less hostile than gating the entire portfolio.
findings.evidence: Home.jsx:45 `const [isPortrait, setIsPortrait]`; :48-50 sets true when `innerWidth <= innerHeight`; :160 `{isPortrait && <HorizontalEnjoyer />}` renders over everything. HorizontalEnjoyer is a full-screen prompt with no dismiss/continue.
findings.recommendation: At minimum, scope the rotate gate to the Shop section only (let the rest of the portfolio render in portrait). Better: design a portrait fallback layout for the Shop (stack left column above shelf, shelf as 2-col grid, bag as a horizontal scroller) — the vmin-based scaling and coarse-pointer media query (Shop.module.css:1577) suggest it's close. If a true landscape requirement remains, make HorizontalEnjoyer dismissible ('Continue anyway') so users aren't hard-blocked.

findings.title: Toast is the day-event's only loud announcement, but it's a polite aria-live that can be missed and isn't re-surfaceable
findings.problem: The day event (which materially changes rent, wants, patience, or shelf prices) is announced via a transient toast (aria-live polite, 3.4s) and persisted only in the left-column eventChip — which the player must notice and read. There's no way to re-open 'what's special about today' once the toast fades, beyond glancing at the small chip. A screen-reader user gets the polite announcement once; if they were navigating elsewhere it's lost. For a mechanic that can swing rent +40% (taxman) this is under-weighted.
findings.evidence: Toast role=status aria-live=polite (Shop.jsx:1147). eventChip persists in WantsBoard (Shop.jsx:516-521) but is small and easy to miss. No 'today's news' re-open affordance.
findings.recommendation: Make the day event a persistent, prominent banner for the whole day (not just a 3.4s toast), include it in the day-end ledger context, and surface it in the Help/HUD area as a re-checkable 'Today' readout. For a major event (rent multiplier) consider a brief day-start card the player must dismiss so it can't be missed.

findings.title: Restart always reseeds with Date.now() — no daily/seeded challenge or 'replay this run', limiting replay UX
findings.problem: Replay is a single 'New run' button that always uses a fresh timestamp seed. There's no 'try the same run again' (to learn from a loss), no daily seed for fair comparison, and the records panel shows bests but offers no goal to chase beyond 'beat your gold.' For a roguelike, the seeded RNG infrastructure is already in place (mulberry32 threaded through state) — exposing it would make replay much more compelling for the portfolio audience that lingers.
findings.evidence: RunEnd New run: `dispatch({type:'RESTART', seed:(Date.now()>>>0)||1})` (Shop.jsx:997). Engine is fully deterministic per seed (shopEngine.js:22-39, createRun:174). Records exist (Shop.jsx:104-208) but only as passive bests.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional 'Daily run' (seed = date) so anyone can compare scores, plus a 'Replay this seed' on the run-end screen. Surface a clear goal ('Best: 540g — beat it'). This leverages existing determinism for near-zero engine cost and meaningfully improves the replay loop's legibility and motivation.

summary: The cozy wood/parchment theme is genuinely above-average for a portfolio piece and clearly authored with care: a single coherent color system (CSS custom props), considered layered box-shadows that give each ware a real "sits-on-the-shelf" contact shadow, a restrained radial candlelight ::before, well-thought-out detail props (chalk-tray rail, kraft price-chit with eyelet, wax-seal toast, candle-socket patience pips), and a cohesive from-scratch 23-icon SVG set on a shared 64x64 / #2b2118-ink / warm palette. Accessibility hooks (reduced-motion, coarse-pointer, focus-visible) are present and unusually complete. It does NOT yet read "AAA," and the gap is mostly mechanical, not taste: (1) the whole UI is sized in vmin, which on a full-screen vertical scroller means it scales with the SHORTER viewport axis — text that is fine at 1280x800 becomes either microscopic on short-wide laptops or oversized on tall/4K, and the dozen 1.0-1.35vmin labels (flipTag 1vmin, wantsTitle 1.35vmin, cardWorth 1.2vmin, newBadge 1.05vmin, rapportNext 1.15vmin) are already at or below the legibility floor on a 13" laptop; the partial clamp() band-aids at the bottom only cover a handful. (2) Typography hierarchy is undercut by a font-loading bug: Fraunces is loaded only at weights 600/700 but every display use sets weight 800, so the browser synthesizes a faux-bold and you lose Fraunces' actual high-contrast cut where it matters most (shop sign, panel titles, haggle name). (3) Real CSS-health issues: .offerValue (lines 1000-1006) is dead; .flipTag and .wantedTag are byte-for-byte duplicates (45+ lines), as are the repeated 5-line shadow recipes and the duplicated rarity-pip gradient (.rarityPip vs .helpLegendPip); there are no design tokens for shadow/radius/spacing despite obvious repetition. (4) Polish gaps: no transition on the rapportFill width is fine but the .card hover is the ONLY rich interaction — bag cards, the demand board, wants rows, and the shelf sign have no hover; there's no transition on opacity for cardLocked; the haggle modal, the most important screen, is visually lighter than the panels and lacks a "deal struck" celebratory beat. The icons are cohesive and legible at shelf size but a few (hand-axe, carved-mask, music-box) carry more line detail than survives 5.4vmin in the bag. Direction: keep the art direction wholesale, fix the font weights, migrate vmin->clamp(rem,vmin,rem) via tokens, dedupe into shared classes + a token block, and add a second tier of micro-interactions + a haggle-success moment.

findings.title: vmin-only sizing scales the whole UI to the SHORT axis; on a full-screen scroller this breaks at common laptop and 4K/ultrawide sizes
findings.location: Shop.module.css — pervasive (e.g. .root padding 3vmin 4vmin; .icon 7vmin; .shelf minmax(13vmin,1fr); ~120 vmin values total)
findings.problem: Every dimension and font-size is in vmin, which resolves against min(vw,vh). The Shop is one section of a 100vh vertical-scroll page, so its usable height is locked to viewport height while width varies hugely. On a 1366x768 laptop vmin=7.68px, so a 1.0vmin flipTag is ~7.7px and a 1.2vmin cardWorth is ~9px — below the ~11px practical legibility floor. On a 27" 1440p or 4K display vmin balloons (vmin≈10.8px at 1440p, ~21.6px at 4K) so 2.4vmin gold (line 116) becomes 26px+ and the layout reads cartoonishly large with no max cap. Ultrawide (e.g. 3440x1440) makes vmin track height only, so the shelf grid (minmax(13vmin) ≈169px columns) leaves the wide shelf sparsely populated.
findings.evidence: L116 .hudGold font-size:2.4vmin; L522 .flipTag font-size:1vmin; L598 .cardWorth 1.2vmin; L425 grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(13vmin,1fr)); only L1637 media query retrofits clamp() onto ~6 labels.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a token-based clamp() scale and replace raw vmin. Define in :root e.g. --fs-label: clamp(11px, 1.3vmin, 14px); --fs-body: clamp(13px, 1.6vmin, 18px); --fs-h2: clamp(18px, 2.4vmin, 30px); --fs-display: clamp(20px, 2.7vmin, 36px); and a spacing scale --sp-1..--sp-6 as clamp() too. Switch grid columns to minmax(clamp(120px,13vmin,180px),1fr). Cap the whole game by setting a max font-size context (e.g. wrap .root content in a container that clamps). This single change is the biggest lever toward an AAA feel across 1280x800 -> 4K -> ultrawide.

verification.reasoning:
Read Shop.module.css in full and verified against Home.jsx. The core premise and every load-bearing claim hold up; severity is correctly rated high.

Layout premise CONFIRMED: .root is width:100vw (L30) inside a 100dvh scroller with sections translated by -100dvh (Home.jsx L159, L176). So each section's height is locked to viewport height while width varies independently — exactly the condition that makes vmin=min(vw,vh) track the short axis (height on landscape; height on ultrawide). The finding's framing is correct.

Values/selectors CONFIRMED (minor line drift, not material): .hudGold 2.4vmin (L116, exact); grid minmax(13vmin,1fr) (L425, exact); .flipTag font-size:1vmin (L521, finding said L522); .cardWorth 1.2vmin (L596, finding said L598). Counted 245 vmin matches; clamp() appears on only 8 lines — 5 panel widths (L809/1175/1308/1399), one portrait height (L284), and the L1637 retrofit. There is NO global clamp scale and NO max font-size cap anywhere.

Small-text floor CONFIRMED and actually UNDERSTATED: the only legibility retrofit (L1637) fires at max-width:1100px OR max-height:740px. A 1366x768 laptop satisfies NEITHER (1366>1100, 768>740), so .flipTag (~7.7px) and .cardWorth (~9.2px) get zero clamp protection at the single most common laptop resolution — worse than the finding implies.

Large-display CONFIRMED and understated: no max cap means .hudGold 2.4vmin = ~51.8px at 4K (vmin=21.6px); finding's '26px+' is conservative.

Ultrawide shelf: directionally correct (minmax(13vmin) ties column size to height, ~169px at 1440p) but slightly overstated — auto-fill + 1fr does still fill the width, so it's not literally 'sparsely populated', just height-driven density rather than width-driven.

This is a real, code-confirmed defect (a legibility/accessibility floor on common hardware), not a subjective preference. High severity stands.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Adopt a token-based clamp() type/space scale in :root and replace raw vmin sitewide for this module. Concretely:

1) Define tokens on .root AND .overlay (modals portal out of .root, L8-9, so they need the vars too): --fs-micro: clamp(11px, 1.1vmin, 13px); --fs-label: clamp(12px, 1.3vmin, 15px); --fs-body: clamp(13px, 1.6vmin, 18px); --fs-h2: clamp(18px, 2.4vmin, 28px); --fs-display: clamp(20px, 2.7vmin, 34px); plus --sp-1..--sp-6 as clamp() spacing tokens. Map the smallest game-critical readouts (.cardWorth, .flipTag, .wantedTag, .bagProfit, .rapportNext, .newBadge) to --fs-micro so they can never drop below 11px — this is the key fix, since the existing L1637 retrofit does NOT cover 1366x768 (its breakpoints are max-width:1100px / max-height:740px, which that resolution fails on both axes).

2) Grid: change L425/L1633 to grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(clamp(120px, 13vmin, 170px), 1fr)) so column size is bounded and not purely height-driven; this also fixes ultrawide density.

3) Cap the overall scale: wrap .root content (or set on .root) a max font/size context, e.g. font-size: clamp(14px, 1.6vmin, 19px) as the rem-like base and express child sizes in em, OR add a max-width container + max() guard, so a 4K display doesn't render .hudGold at ~52px.

4) After migration, delete the L1637 patch-up media query (it becomes redundant once clamps are global) but KEEP the L1577 (pointer:coarse) and L1611 (max-height:800px) blocks. Net effect: legible 11px floor everywhere, sane cap on 4K/ultrawide, and width-bounded shelf columns — the single biggest lever toward an AAA feel from 1280x800 to 4K.

findings.title: Fraunces is loaded only at weight 600/700 but every display style requests 800 -> faux-bold synthesis on all titles
findings.location: index.html:30 (font href) vs Shop.module.css L394/398, L874, L919, L1194, L1156, L1283, L1453
findings.problem: The Google Fonts URL requests Fraunces at opsz 9..144 but only weights 600 and 700. The CSS sets font-weight:800 on the most prominent display elements (shop sign .shelfTitle span, .haggleName, .priceAnchor, .panelTitle, .dealBig, .storyTitle, .codexCardTitle). Since no 800 face exists, the browser fakes bold by smearing the 700 outline — exactly the high-end serif where faux-bold is most visible and most cheapening. The headline 'storybook serif' moment is the one place the polish leaks.
findings.evidence: href: 'Fraunces:opsz,wght@9..144,600;9..144,700'. CSS display rules all use font-weight:800. No font-optical-sizing declared either, so opsz axis is left to default.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) add 900 (and 800 if desired) to the Fraunces request: 'Fraunces:opsz,wght@9..144,600;9..144,700;9..144,900' and use 700/900 in CSS, or (b) change every Fraunces font-weight:800 to 700 to use the real face. Also add 'font-optical-sizing: auto;' on .root so Fraunces uses its display optical size at large sizes. Verify Nunito Sans 800 is actually loaded (it is in the href: ...700;800;900) — so body weights are fine; only the serif is broken.

verification.reasoning:
Verified the technical claim in full. index.html:30 loads `Fraunces:opsz,wght@9..144,600;9..144,700` — only weights 600 and 700, no 800. The `--display` (Fraunces) family is applied to exactly 7 display elements, every one of which resolves to font-weight 800:
- L397 `.shelfTitle span:first-child` (the shop sign): no own font-weight, but inherits 800 from `.shelfTitle` at L389 — so it does render at 800. The finding's location label "L394/398" is slightly off (the 800 is on the parent at L389) but the conclusion is correct.
- L871/873 `.haggleName` = 800.
- L917/919 `.priceAnchor` = 800.
- L1156/1158 `.dealBig` = 800.
- L1191/1193 `.panelTitle` = 800.
- L1280/1282 `.storyTitle` = 800.
- L1453/1455 `.codexCardTitle` = 800.
Grepped the whole repo: there is NO `font-synthesis` declaration anywhere, so the CSS default (`font-synthesis: weight style`) applies and the browser WILL faux-bold the missing 800 by smearing the 700 outline. This is exactly the storybook-serif moment where synthesis is most visible — the claim holds.
The ancillary note that Nunito Sans 800 IS loaded (URL: `Nunito+Sans:wght@...700;800;900`) is also correct, so body weights are unaffected; only the serif is broken.

One overstatement to flag: the evidence says "no font-optical-sizing declared either, so opsz axis is left to default." That is technically true that it isn't declared (confirmed via grep — zero matches), but `font-optical-sizing: auto` is already the browser DEFAULT for variable fonts exposing an `opsz` axis, so opsz is in fact already doing the right thing. Adding it explicitly is harmless but does not fix a real bug — that secondary point is cosmetic, not a defect.

Severity: the finding rates "high." This is a real, accurately-described visible defect, but it's a subtle polish issue on a portfolio side-game, not functional/accessibility breakage — most users won't consciously perceive it, and the fix is trivial (S). "Medium" is the honest rating for a real-but-low-impact polish defect.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Pick ONE of two fixes (both correct; choose by design intent):
(a) Cheapest, zero payload change — change all 7 Fraunces display rules from `font-weight: 800` to `font-weight: 700` so they use the real loaded 700 face. Affected: Shop.module.css L389 (`.shelfTitle`, which the sign span inherits), L873, L919, L1158, L1193, L1282, L1455.
(b) If you specifically want heavier display weight, add the weight to the request in index.html:30 — `Fraunces:opsz,wght@9..144,600;9..144,700;9..144,900` — then change the seven `800`s to `900` (or `700`/`900` as desired). Note this adds one more font face to download.

Belt-and-suspenders regardless of choice: add `font-synthesis: none;` to `.root, .overlay` so any future weight mismatch fails visibly (real face missing) rather than silently faux-bolding — this surfaces the bug instead of hiding it.

Drop the `font-optical-sizing: auto` suggestion as a "fix": `auto` is already the default for Fraunces' `opsz` axis, so it changes nothing. Adding it explicitly is fine for documentation/clarity but is not load-bearing.

findings.title: .offerValue rule is dead code (offer is rendered via .offerInput/.offerField)
findings.problem: .offerValue { font-size:2.8vmin; ... min-width:7vmin } is never referenced in Shop.jsx. The live offer display uses .offerField + .offerInput (Shop.jsx L807) and .offerG (L815). Confirmed via grep: no styles.offerValue anywhere in the component.
findings.evidence: grep 'offerValue' over Shop.jsx returns zero matches; the class exists only in the CSS module.
findings.recommendation: Delete the .offerValue block. (Likely a leftover from before the editable text input was added.)

findings.title: .flipTag and .wantedTag are byte-identical duplicates (45+ duplicated lines)
findings.problem: The two ribbon tags are completely identical declarations including the ::before pin pseudo-element — same gradient, padding, radius, shadow, the only difference being which JSX uses them (FLIP on shelf, WANTED in bag). This is ~46 lines of pure duplication that will drift.
findings.evidence: L519-529 vs L726-736 are character-for-character the same; L531-541 vs L737-747 likewise.
findings.recommendation: Collapse to one base class .ribbonTag (with its ::before) and apply it to both, e.g. className={`${styles.ribbonTag}`}. If you want per-context tint later, add a modifier. Removes ~23 lines and a future drift bug.

findings.title: Repeated shadow/gradient recipes with no tokens — magic-number sprawl across 1573 lines
findings.location: Shop.module.css — the 'card stack' shadow (L468-470, repeated at 477-479, 483-485, 686-688, 717-719); rarity-pip gradient (L608-613 == L1379-1384); panel/haggle shadow (L818-819 == L1181-1182)
findings.problem: The same 4-layer 'object on wood' box-shadow recipe is hand-copied across .card, .card:hover, .card:active, .bagCard, .wantedCard with tiny y/blur deltas. The radial wax-seal gradient is duplicated verbatim between .rarityPip and .helpLegendPip. The pooled-lamplight panel shadow is duplicated between .haggle and .panel. There are no design tokens for radius (values 4/5/6/7/8/10/12/14/18px appear ad hoc), shadow, or spacing.
findings.evidence: Identical 'inset 0 0 5vmin rgba(224,165,43,0.1)' panel shadow at L818 and L1181; identical radial-gradient(circle at 38% 32%,...) pip at L608 and L1379.
findings.recommendation: Add a token block to :root: --r-sm/-md/-lg (6/12/18px), --sh-card / --sh-card-hover / --sh-card-press, --sh-panel, --grad-seal, --sp scale. Reference tokens everywhere. Extract a shared .pip class consumed by both rarity contexts. Cuts the file substantially and makes a future re-skin a 10-line edit instead of a 50-site find/replace.

findings.title: 1573-line single CSS module mixes layout, theme, animation, responsive, and 5 modal skins — hard to maintain
findings.problem: Everything from the HUD to five distinct modal panels (haggle/day-end/story/run-end/help/codex) to keyframes to media queries lives in one file. It's well-commented, but there's no internal structure beyond banner comments, and selectors like .panel/.helpPanel/.codexPanel/.storyPanel/.winPanel/.overPanel are scattered.
findings.evidence: 5 modal variants share .panel base then override border-color across L1266/1291/1294/1304/1396; keyframes at L1508-1547 sit between toast styling and media queries.
findings.recommendation: Split into co-located modules: Shop.tokens.css (the :root block), Shop.module.css (game board), HaggleModal.module.css, Panels.module.css. Or, at minimum, move the :root token/palette block into its own imported file so it's reusable by the haggle modal (which currently re-declares the palette on .overlay, L8-26, precisely because it portals out). Composing a single .themeVars class would remove that whole workaround.

findings.title: Hover/interaction polish is concentrated on .card only; most surfaces are static
findings.location: Shop.module.css — .card L475-490 (rich) vs .wantRow, .eventChip, .shelfTitle span, .bagCard, .rapportBar, .ledger lines (no hover/transition)
findings.problem: The shelf card has a beautiful three-state lift/press, but it's the only element with that craft. The hung shop sign (.shelfTitle span:first-child) looks interactive (it's a sign) but is inert. The demand board rows, the help/codex cards, and the streak chip have no hover affordance. The result is an inconsistent interaction language — one element feels AAA, the rest feel like a static mockup.
findings.evidence: Only .card/.helpBtn/.endDay/.btn* declare :hover. No :hover on .codexCard, .wantRow, .bagCard (bag cards ARE buttons — L583 — yet inherit no distinct hover beyond the base .card).
findings.recommendation: Define a shared --transition token and add subtle, consistent hover states: codex/help cards lift 1px + border lightens; wantRow gets a faint background tint on hover; the streak chip gets a gentle scale on update (you already have streakPop — extend). Give a hover/active to bagCard explicitly. Keep it under reduced-motion (already gated).

findings.title: The haggle modal — the core screen — is visually lighter than the day-end panels and lacks a 'deal struck' moment
findings.location: Shop.module.css .haggle L805-821 vs .panel L1173-1189; deal result L982-999, L1148-1163
findings.problem: Haggling is the entire game loop, but .haggle uses a semi-transparent top half (linear-gradient(180deg,#34251699,#241a10)) and shares the exact same shadow as the passive day-end .panel, so the most active screen has no extra visual weight or focus. When a deal closes, the result is just text (.dealBig color flip, L1155-1160) — there is no animation, no coin burst, no portrait reaction beat. goldPop exists for the HUD coin but isn't tied to the haggle success.
findings.evidence: L818-819 (.haggle shadow) == L1181-1182 (.panel shadow). Deal outcome rendered as static .dealRow/.dealBig with no keyframe. goldPop (L1538) only on .hudGoldUp.
findings.recommendation: Give .haggle a heavier frame (thicker border / stronger interior amber pool / a subtle vignette) so it reads as the focal modal. On a successful flip, animate .dealBig in (scale+fade), pulse the patience candles, and trigger a one-shot coin/sparkle burst near the gold readout. Add a tiny portrait expression swap on success/insult (the QUIPS already vary by outcome — pair art with them). This is the single biggest 'feel' upgrade for the price.

findings.title: cardLocked has no transition and desaturates harshly; affordability changes pop with no easing
findings.location: Shop.module.css .cardLocked L491-494; .card transition L473 only covers transform/box-shadow
findings.problem: .cardLocked applies opacity:0.5 + filter:saturate(0.6) but .card's transition list is 'transform 0.12s, box-shadow 0.12s' — opacity and filter aren't transitioned, so when gold changes and a card flips affordable/locked it snaps instantly. saturate(0.6)+opacity 0.5 stacked also makes locked wares quite muddy on the dark shelf.
findings.evidence: L473 transition omits opacity/filter; L492-493 opacity:0.5; filter:saturate(0.6).
findings.recommendation: Add 'opacity .15s ease, filter .15s ease' to the .card transition. Consider opacity:0.55 with filter:grayscale(0.35) instead of saturate(0.6) for a cleaner 'out of reach' look, and add a small '🔒'/dimmed price affordance so locked state reads as price-gated not disabled.

findings.title: A few SVG icons carry detail that won't survive bag size (5.4vmin ≈ 41-58px) and one set-consistency wobble
findings.location: itemIcons.jsx — carved-mask L268-281, hand-axe L105-112, music-box L220-232, treasure-map L157-172
findings.problem: The set is impressively cohesive (shared ink, ground-shadow ellipse, warm palette, highlight stroke). But carved-mask packs eyes+brows+nose+mouth+forehead-stripe into the face, music-box has a tiny crank+star+two clasps, and treasure-map has 5 dotted-path segments plus an X plus a compass star — at 41-46px these collapse into noise where the simpler icons (ruby, sapphire, honey-jar, gold-bangle) stay crisp. The hand-axe's rotated handle (transform rotate(22 39 32)) makes it the only off-axis, visually lighter member of the set. The fire-opal palette (#e0722a/#c4521d oranges) is the one icon using a hue family not present anywhere else (no orange in the theme tokens) — it stands slightly apart from the gem siblings.
findings.evidence: carved-mask: 11 path/line children inside a 52px-tall face; treasure-map: 5 separate dotted stroke lines L164-168; hand-axe single rotated handle L107.
findings.recommendation: For bag rendering, the small size argues for a simplified detail tier or just thicker min stroke-widths on the busiest icons (bump 1.2-1.5 strokes to 2). Specifically: reduce carved-mask facial linework, fatten treasure-map dotted path, and consider centering the hand-axe head. fire-opal is fine to keep (opals are warm) but you could add a faint orange accent token so it reads as intentional. Optionally add an SVG drop-shadow/contact consistency check. Net: the set is already a strength — these are touch-ups.

findings.title: Rarity is communicated almost entirely by a 1.6vmin colored pip; the color->rarity mapping is non-obvious and the only legend is hidden in Help
findings.location: Shop.module.css .rarityPip L601-624; shopData.js RARITY hues L29-32 (common #8a7a5c, uncommon #c98a3a, rare #3f6f9e, legendary #6d4a87); legend only in helpLegend L1349
findings.problem: Rarity tier is encoded as a ~12-17px wax-seal whose only differentiator is hue (brown/amber/blue/purple), plus a gold ring for legendary. The hues are arbitrary (purple=legendary, blue=rare) with no in-context label — the legend lives behind the Help modal. On the warm parchment card the brown 'common' pip nearly disappears, and the amber 'uncommon' is close to the gold UI accents. This is both a discoverability and a color-only-encoding (WCAG 1.4.1) concern, only partly mitigated by the role=img aria-label on the pip (good — screen readers get it).
findings.evidence: rarityPip(rarity) returns r.hue inline (Shop.jsx L526-527); common hue #8a7a5c on parch-2 #f7ecd2 is low-contrast; legend only rendered in helpPanel (Shop.jsx L1052).
findings.recommendation: Strengthen the non-color signal: keep the gold ring for legendary but add distinct ring treatments per tier (e.g. rare=blue ring, uncommon=single ring, common=no ring/flat) OR a tiny tier glyph/dot-count so rarity is readable without learned color mapping. Brighten the common hue or give it a darker outline so it doesn't vanish on parchment. Surface a one-line rarity key on the shelf header (or a hover tooltip on the pip) rather than only in Help.

findings.title: Several persistent labels sit at/below 1.1vmin — under legibility floor on small laptops, only partially clamped
findings.location: Shop.module.css .newBadge 1.05vmin L1249; .rapportNext 1.15vmin L192; .endDaySub 1.1vmin L777; .flipTag/.wantedTag 1vmin L522/729; .wantsTitle 1.35vmin L336; .codexSub/.helpLegendItem 1.3vmin
findings.problem: At 1280x800 vmin=8px, so 1.0vmin=8px (flip/wanted tags), 1.05vmin=8.4px (newBadge), 1.1vmin=8.8px (endDaySub) — all well under the ~11-12px legibility floor for UI labels. The L1637 media query adds clamp() floors for cardName/flipTag/wantedTag/newBadge/rapportNext/cardWorth/endDaySub/haggleNote/slideHint, but ONLY below 1100px width or 740px height, so a 1280x800 or 1366x768 laptop (above those thresholds) still renders raw sub-9px text.
findings.evidence: clamp() floors gated behind '@media (max-width:1100px),(max-height:740px)' (L1637) — 1280x800 escapes the height clause (800>740) and the width clause (1280>1100).
findings.recommendation: Move to clamp() tokens globally (see vmin finding) so floors apply at ALL sizes, not just below arbitrary breakpoints. As an immediate fix, change the media query to (max-height: 820px) to catch 1280x800/1366x768, and raise the floor on flipTag/wantedTag/newBadge from 9px to 10-11px.

findings.title: Grid.png grain texture loaded at 3px tile via background-image — works, but it's a coupling/fragility note and a perf micro-cost
findings.problem: The 'plank grain' is a 5%-opacity raster tiled at 3x3px over the whole section. At 0.05 opacity over a dark wood base it's barely perceptible (questionable ROI), it depends on a shared /Grid.png asset reused from the HUD site (cross-section coupling — if that asset changes the shop grain changes), and tiling a bitmap at 3px is more expensive than an equivalent CSS gradient/SVG noise.
findings.evidence: L63 url('/Grid.png'); opacity:0.05; the candlelight ::before (L48-57) already provides a repeating-linear-gradient plank texture, so two texture layers stack.
findings.recommendation: Either drop .grain entirely (the ::before plank lines already carry the texture) or replace with an inline SVG feTurbulence noise as a data-URI so it's self-contained and resolution-independent. If kept, raise opacity slightly (0.07-0.08) or it's invisible work.

findings.title: No empty/loading state for the shelf beyond a text line; bag empty slots are good but the 'sold out' state is plain
findings.location: Shop.module.css .soldOut L446-452; .bagEmpty L706-714 (this one is nicely done)
findings.problem: .bagEmpty (dashed sewn compartments) is a genuinely premium empty state. By contrast .soldOut is just centered muted text 'Sold out for today...' (Shop.jsx L378) on the bare shelf — a missed opportunity for the same craft (e.g. a 'CLOSED'/curtain/swept-shelf motif). There's also no skeleton/placeholder while the morning restock animates in (the wareIn stagger covers this somewhat).
findings.evidence: L446-452 .soldOut is text-only; compare the detailed .bagEmpty L706-714.
findings.recommendation: Give the sold-out shelf a themed empty state: a faint 'come back tomorrow' chalk scrawl on the cabinet back, or a small swept-broom/curtain SVG, matching the care put into .bagEmpty. Low effort, noticeable polish.

findings.title: rarityPipTop (legendary gold ring) is the only per-tier visual distinction in shadow; rare/uncommon get identical chrome
findings.problem: Only legendary gets bespoke chrome (gold-leaf ring). Common/uncommon/rare share the exact same wax-seal frame and differ solely by the inline hue. Given how subtle the hues are, the rarity ladder visually flattens to 'normal vs legendary' rather than a satisfying 4-step progression.
findings.evidence: L615-617 shared seal shadow for all non-legendary; only L620-623 overrides for legendary.
findings.recommendation: Add a .rarityPipRare modifier (slightly brighter/cooler ring) and optionally a faint sheen so the four tiers form a readable gradient of specialness. Ties into the broader rarity-legibility finding.

summary: This is an unusually conscientious accessibility implementation for a portfolio game: a real focus trap with trigger restoration, role=dialog/aria-modal on every overlay, role=progressbar with aria-valuetext on rapport, role=img + aria-label on the patience meter, aria-hidden on decorative SVG icons and emoji, prefers-reduced-motion coverage, coarse-pointer 44px hit targets, and a deliberately high-contrast palette. My computed contrast ratios confirm the color story is essentially solved — virtually every text/background pair clears AA (most clear AAA): muted labels #c9b894/#d8c4a0/#cdb88f/#b9a583 land at 6.6–10:1 on the dark wood, --red-lit rent at 5.5:1, white-on-green flip tags at 5.2–7.2:1, profit reds/greens at 4.7–8:1. The _audit/contrast.json file is stale garbage (it describes a #7cc1f6 blue "Home/Oldest" element from a different page, not the Shop at all) and should be deleted or regenerated. The genuine, serious gaps are NOT visual — they are in the screen-reader announcement layer (live regions) and a handful of focus/semantics edge cases. The single biggest defect: the entire haggle interaction is silent to a screen reader. Kaito's quips, his counter-offer/anchor changing, patience draining, "insult"/"final offer" state transitions, the deal outcome (price/profit/tip/rapport), and rapport tier-ups produce no announcement at all — only the toast and aria-valuetext are wired to live regions, and aria-valuetext on the slider is itself buggy (reads stale price). A blind player can operate the controls but cannot perceive the consequences of their actions, which makes the core loop unplayable non-visually. Secondary issues: a missing h1 / heading-hierarchy break, no programmatic dialog title association (aria-labelledby), an aria-valuetext that omits the fair-band/insult context entirely, chatty duplicated card labels, the slider's "fair band" being conveyed by color/position only, and the run auto-starting on page load (a runaway timer-free but state-mutating background section). Effort to close the gaps is mostly Small–Medium.

findings.title: The entire haggle exchange is silent to screen readers — no live region announces Kaito's counter, patience, insult, final offer, or deal outcome
findings.problem:
The haggle modal is the core game loop, and almost none of its dynamic state changes are announced. When the player submits an offer, the engine mutates h.ask/h.offer (Kaito's counter), h.patience, state.quip, and on insult drops rapport and switches to an 'insult' face — but the modal renders these as plain non-live DOM. There is NO aria-live region in the haggle at all. .haggleQuip (line 703) is a static

, the .priceAnchor counter (785) is static, (717/873) is role=img with a static aria-label that is recomputed but never re-announced, and the deal result block (720-752: 'BOUGHT/SOLD for X', profit, hot-streak tip, rapport up) is static markup that the SR user never hears. The only role=status in the whole modal is the narrow 'more coin than you're carrying' note (759). A blind player can move the slider and press Offer, but receives zero feedback on whether Kaito accepted, countered, was insulted, ran out of patience, or what they paid/earned. The loop is effectively unplayable without sight. WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA) and 1.3.1.
findings.recommendation: Add a single visually-hidden polite live region inside the modal (e.g. <div className={styles.srOnly} aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">) and feed it a composed string on each haggle transition: on a counter, '{quip} Kaito now asks {ask}. Patience {patience} of {max}.'; on insult, 'That offended him — patience {patience}, rapport dropped.'; on final, 'Kaito's final word: {price}, take it or leave it.'; on deal, the same text already in dealLabel (689-691). Drive it off h.status / h.patience / h.lastOffer changing (useEffect keyed on those). Because completeBuy/Sell flip status to 'deal' and re-render the deal block with autoFocus on Continue, also announce the outcome there (assertive is acceptable for the deal result). Keep aria-atomic so partial strings aren't half-read.

verification.reasoning:
Verified against the actual code. The core claim — the haggle exchange's dynamic state changes are not announced to screen readers — is accurate. LIVE REGIONS: A grep for aria-live/role="status"/role="alert"/srOnly across Shop.jsx returns exactly two hits: the narrow "more coin than you're carrying" note (line 759, only shown on a final buy you can't afford) and the global Toast (line 1147). No srOnly/visually-hidden class exists in Shop.module.css (grep: no matches). The Scrim wrapper (lines 79-96) is a focus-trapped portal with NO aria-live. So no live region covers the haggle's dynamic content. THE SILENT TRANSITIONS (the real defect): In engine offer() (shopEngine.js:270-326), the counter path (lines 282-289 / 302-309) and the insult path (290-298 / 310-317) leave h.status === "active". On these transitions: h.ask/h.offer change -> .priceAnchor (Shop.jsx:785) is a static , not announced; state.quip changes -> .haggleQuip (line 703) is a static

, not announced; h.patience decrements -> (lines 717, 873-879) is role="img" with an aria-label that recomputes but sits on a non-live element, so SRs do not re-announce it; rapport drops on insult with no announcement. Critically, on a counter/insult NO element receives fresh autoFocus, so focus stays on the (still-mounted) submit button and nothing new is read. A blind player offering and getting countered/insulted receives ZERO feedback. These are the MOST frequent outcomes in the core loop, so it is effectively unplayable without sight. This squarely violates WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages and 1.3.1, and severity "critical" is correct (it breaks the central game loop for SR users). NUANCE / minor overstatement in the finding: The deal-result block (lines 720-752) and the final-offer block (753-778) are partially mitigated and not fully "never heard." The deal block's Continue button has autoFocus (748) and aria-label={dealLabel} (747), where dealLabel (689-691) is "Continue. Bought/Sold for X[, profit Y][, rapport up]." — so on a struck deal a screen reader DOES announce the outcome when focus lands on the button. Likewise the final-offer block's primary button has autoFocus (769) and a label "Pay {ask}"/"Accept {offer}" (771) conveying the final price. So "the deal result block ... the SR user never hears" and "no announcement of what they paid/earned" are slightly inaccurate for the deal/final paths. However: the "Kaito's final word: ... take it or leave it" prose (755-757), the hot-streak tip, the profit/loss detail, and the rapport note are still only visual; and the COUNTER and INSULT transitions — the crux of the finding — are genuinely 100% silent. The toast is not a mitigation because offer()'s counter/insult/final branches never call toast() (only completeBuy line 341 does, for the can't-afford case). Net: a real, accurately-described critical defect with one minor overstatement about the already-partially-covered deal/final outcomes. Verdict confirmed; severity confirmed critical.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Add a single visually-hidden polite live region INSIDE the haggle dialog (so it is announced only while the modal is open and not duplicated by the global toast). First add the missing CSS class to Shop.module.css, e.g. `.srOnly { position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px; padding:0; margin:-1px; overflow:hidden; clip:rect(0 0 0 0); white-space:nowrap; border:0; }` (the finding references styles.srOnly, which does not yet exist). Render `
{liveMsg}
` inside the modal, and drive liveMsg from a useEffect keyed on the transition inputs — specifically h.ask, h.offer, h.patience, state.quip (NOT h.status, which the existing autoFocus already covers). Compose per outcome: - Counter (status active, patience unchanged-vs-prev not needed; just rebuild): "{state.quip} Kaito now {buy ? 'asks' : 'offers'} {g(anchor)}. Patience {h.patience} of {h.maxPatience}." - Insult: detect the insult branch (you can flag it from the engine, e.g. set hh.lastInsult = true in offer() lines 296/315, or infer it client-side when patience dropped by 2). Announce assertively: set aria-live="assertive" conditionally or use a second assertive region — "That offended him. Patience {h.patience} of {h.maxPatience}, rapport dropped." - Final (h.final): "Kaito's final word: {g(buy ? h.ask : h.offer)}. Take it or leave it." (the autoFocused button conveys the price, but the "take it or leave it" framing is otherwise visual-only.) For the deal outcome (status === "deal"), the autoFocused Continue button already announces dealLabel, so a redundant assertive announcement risks double-speech — prefer to ENRICH dealLabel instead to include the hot-streak tip and exact profit/loss that are currently visual-only (lines 735-740): e.g. append `${h.tip>0 ? `, hot-streak tip +${g(h.tip)} (${h.streak} in a row)` : ''}`. Keep aria-atomic="true" so partial strings aren't half-read, and ensure the engine exposes enough state to distinguish insult from ordinary counter (cleanest: add an explicit hh.outcome = 'counter'|'insult'|'final' field in offer() so the component doesn't have to reverse-engineer patience deltas).

findings.title: Slider aria-valuetext reads a stale value (lags one render) and omits all fair-band / insult context
findings.problem: Two bugs. (1) Staleness: value={clampP(price)} but aria-valuetext={`${Math.round(price)} gold`} reads the un-clamped state value. More importantly React updates value and aria-valuetext in the same commit, but the engine/clamp can change the effective slider value while the announced text describes the prior price; on the very first arrow-key press in a re-clamped band the SR can read the pre-clamp number. (2) Information loss: the slider's entire meaning is the colored track — a sage 'fair' band, a terracotta 'he'll balk' band, a gold tick at Kaito's number, an ember tick at his threshold (trackBg, 664-675). None of that is in aria-valuetext, which says only 'N gold'. A screen-reader user dragging the slider has no idea when they cross from 'fair' into 'insult', i.e. they cannot perceive the single most important affordance of the control. WCAG 1.1.1, 1.3.1, 1.4.1 (Use of Color), 4.1.2.
findings.recommendation: Compute valuetext from the same clamped value used for value: const shown = clampP(price). Then enrich it: `${shown} gold — ${insulting ? (buy ? 'below his floor, he'll take it as an insult' : 'above his ceiling, he'll balk') : 'within the fair range'}. Kaito's ${buy ? 'ask' : 'offer'} is ${anchor}g`. This makes the band crossing audible and replaces the color-only signal. Also add aria-valuemin/valuemax-aligned describedtext so the player knows the bounds.

verification.reasoning:
I read Shop.jsx:608-871 (the whole HaggleModal), shopEngine.js:86-333 (counter/clamp logic), and grepped for aria-live/role=status. The finding has two sub-claims; they verify differently. SUB-CLAIM 1 (staleness) — REAL BUT OVERSTATED / NEAR-UNREACHABLE. value={clampP(price)} (Shop.jsx:834) vs aria-valuetext={`${Math.round(price)} gold`} (837) do reference different expressions, and a genuine disagreeing frame exists: when Kaito counters, the engine narrows h.ask/h.offer (shopEngine.js:285,305), which narrows min/max (Shop.jsx:618-619); for the one committed render before the reconciling useEffect (634-646) runs, clampP(price) is the new clamped value while Math.round(price) is the stale out-of-band value. BUT the specific harm the finding describes — "on the very first arrow-key press in a re-clamped band the SR reads the pre-clamp number" — is not reachable: (a) the useEffect deps include min,max,h.ask,h.floor,h.offer,h.ceil so it ALWAYS runs and reconciles price synchronously after commit, before any user input; (b) after OFFER the focus goes to the submit button (autoFocus, 850), not the slider, so the disagreeing frame is never announced. All setPrice paths already clamp (801,820,835,688). Real-world SR impact: negligible. Also Math.round() is pointless since price is always an integer. So the fix (use clampP(price) for both) is correct and trivial, but the staleness is a latent inconsistency, not the practical bug claimed. SUB-CLAIM 2 (information loss) — REAL, the substantive defect. aria-valuetext announces only "N gold" (837); the fair/insult bands, gold anchor tick, and ember threshold tick are painted purely in trackBg (664-675) with no textual equivalent in the announced value. HOWEVER the finding omits a mitigating fact I verified: the slideHint

(839-847) DOES render a textual equivalent of the insult state ("That low? He'll take it as an insult."), and the input gets an offerInsult style (807). The problem is that slideHint has NO role=status/aria-live (confirmed by grep — only lines 759, 1147 have it), so it is not ANNOUNCED as the SR user drags across the band boundary. So the band info is present as visible text but not audible during slider manipulation. That makes raw 1.4.1 (Use of Color) and 1.1.1 weak/partly-mitigated citations; the accurate ones are 4.1.2 and 1.3.1. Net: the recommendation is correct and worth doing, but the finding is mis-stated (staleness manifestation is theoretical; it overlooks the existing slideHint textual equivalent and overclaims WCAG SCs). Hence partial, and medium not high — degraded-but-not-absent perception of the key affordance, in one modal of a portfolio toy.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Two separate, small fixes: 1) Make the announced value consistent (cheap, do it regardless): derive both attributes from one source — value={shown} and aria-valuetext from shown, where const shown = clampP(price). Drop Math.round (price is already integer). 2) Make the band crossing AUDIBLE — this is the real win. Enrich aria-valuetext so every slider move announces position relative to Kaito's number and his threshold, e.g.: `${shown} gold — ${insulting ? (buy ? "below his floor; he'll take it as an insult" : "above his ceiling; he'll balk") : "within the fair range"}. Kaito's ${buy ? "ask" : "offer"} is ${anchor}g.` This replaces the color-only track signal in the value that actually fires on each arrow/drag. 3) Independently, make the existing slideHint

(839) a live region by adding role="status" (it already mirrors `insulting`), so the warning is announced even for users who rely on it visually-adjacent but use SR — low cost, complements (2). Do NOT bother framing this as a 1.1.1 issue (a range input is not non-text content) and note 1.4.1 is partly mitigated by the slideHint text; lead with 4.1.2/1.3.1.

findings.title: Rapport tier-up (perk unlocked + story revealed) is never announced as a status; it only surfaces via a modal that opens on the NEXT day-break
findings.location: shopEngine.js:355-356, 395-396 (rapport increment) and 450-462 (tier crossing deferred to sleep); Shop.jsx:446-481 (Rapport progressbar)
findings.problem: Rapport changes every deal (gain 1–4) and crossing a threshold unlocks a perk and a backstory card. The Rapport component is role=progressbar with aria-valuetext (good), but a progressbar's valuetext is only read when focused — it is not a live region, so a sighted-independent player gets no notification that their rapport moved or that they just crossed a tier. The deal modal's static .rapportNote ('Kaito warms to you — rapport up', 741-743) is not in a live region either (covered by finding #1). Worse, the perk grant + story reveal is deferred to the sleep() transition (lines 451-462) and shown as the Backstory modal — which does get focus and is readable — but the moment-of-earning ('rapport up, a perk is coming') is lost. WCAG 4.1.3.
findings.recommendation: Roll the rapport delta into the haggle live-region announcement from finding #1 ('rapport up' / actual +N). Separately, add aria-live to a small HUD status node so tier-ups and perk unlocks are announced even outside a modal. The Backstory modal itself is fine (role=dialog, autoFocus, Escape acks) — just make sure its aria-label uses the tier title (it does, line 940) and consider announcing the perk gained in its body text since PERK_LABELS isn't surfaced there.

verification.reasoning:
I read shopEngine.js:340-469 and Shop.jsx:445-481, 670-759, 920-951, plus the toast live region (1140-1151) and PERK_LABELS (shopData.js:154-159). Most of the finding's component facts check out, but its central severity claim ("the moment-of-earning is lost") is overstated and partly contradicted by code it did not account for.

CONFIRMED facts:
- Rapport increments on every deal: completeBuy (shopEngine.js:353-355, gain 1-3) and completeSell (390-396, gain 1-4). True.
- The Rapport progressbar (Shop.jsx:459-468) has role=progressbar + aria-valuetext but NO aria-live, so valuetext is only read on focus. True; it is not a live region.
- The deal-row .rapportNote (Shop.jsx:741-743) is a plain <div>, not in a live region. True.
- Tier crossing is deferred to sleep(): shopEngine.js:451-462 sets next.tier++, applyPerk, pendingTier, and phase="backstory" only at day-break — never at the moment rapport crosses the threshold during trading. True.
- The Backstory modal (Shop.jsx:931-951) is a proper role=dialog/aria-modal with autoFocus and Escape-acks, aria-label uses tier.title (940). True, and it is genuinely announced.
- PERK_LABELS is NOT surfaced in the Backstory body — it only renders tier.title + tier.text (943-944). True; PERK_LABELS is only used in the HUD progressbar caption (456).

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG / OVERSTATED:
1. It claims "the moment-of-earning ('rapport up') is lost." But dealLabel (Shop.jsx:689-691) appends ", rapport up" when h.rapportGain >= 2, and that string is the aria-label of the auto-focused Continue button (747-748, autoFocus). So after every qualifying deal a screen reader DOES announce "...rapport up." on focus. The per-deal gain is surfaced (binary, on autofocus) — not "lost." Caveats: it is binary (only when gain>=2, so a +1 gain says nothing) and never says "+N" or "a perk is coming."
2. It frames tier-ups as needing announcement "outside a modal." But a tier-up is ALWAYS a forced phase transition to the Backstory dialog at day-break (phase="backstory"); it is never silent-and-outside-a-modal. The finding itself concedes the Backstory modal is fine. So the only genuinely missing live-region need is the *in-trading per-deal* rapport delta granularity and the *perk name* in the Backstory body — not the tier-up event itself, which is already announced via a focus-trapped dialog.

So: a real WCAG 4.1.3 gap exists (no live status for rapport movement; the autofocus-label is binary and easy to miss; perk name absent from Backstory body), but the finding mis-states it as "lost"/"no notification" when partial focus-based announcement already exists. That makes it partial, and severity should drop from high to medium — the most consequential rapport event (the tier-up + story) is already in a properly-announced dialog, and a degraded-but-present per-deal signal exists.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Three concrete fixes: 1. Make the per-deal rapport delta granular and non-binary. In Shop.jsx:691, dealLabel currently only appends ", rapport up" when h.rapportGain >= 2 — replace with the actual amount, e.g. `${h.rapportGain ? `, rapport +${h.rapportGain}` : ""}`, so even a +1 gain is announced and the magnitude is clear on the auto-focused Continue button. 2. Add a single dedicated aria-live="polite" status node in the HUD (NOT reusing the toast, which is consumed by event/error messages) that emits a transient string whenever rapport changes during trading and especially when state.tier increments — e.g. "Rapport 30. Tier reached: Friend's discount unlocked." Drive it off a useEffect keyed on state.rapport / state.tier so it announces during play, decoupled from focus. This is the actual missing 4.1.3 piece (the in-trading signal), since the tier-up dialog itself is already announced. 3. Surface the perk in the Backstory modal body (Shop.jsx:943-944). It already imports PERK_LABELS; add a line like `

Unlocked: {PERK_LABELS[tier.perk]}

` so the reward (not just the lore) is conveyed in the announced dialog. Drop the claim that the tier-up itself is unannounced — it forces the Backstory dialog (shopEngine.js:459), which is a correctly-announced role=dialog with autoFocus.

findings.title: No h1 on the section and heading hierarchy is broken — h2 'KAITO'S WARES' with no document/section heading above it
findings.problem: The Shop renders an h2 ('KAITO'S WARES') and an h3 ('TODAY'S DEMAND') but there is no h1 anywhere in the section, and no accessible name for the game region itself. Because all sections are mounted simultaneously in Home.jsx (off-screen ones are inert), there is also no landmark structure distinguishing the game. A screen-reader user navigating by heading lands on an h2 with nothing above it (3.1 of WCAG technique G141 — skipped heading level / missing top level). The 'SHOP' section has no programmatic name; the demand board h3 outranks nothing.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the game in <section aria-labelledby> or <main>/role=region with an accessible name ('Kaito's Curios — haggling game'). Add a visually-hidden h1 (or h2 if the site reserves h1 for the page title) naming the game, then keep 'KAITO'S WARES' / 'TODAY'S DEMAND' as h2/h3 beneath it so the order is h1→h2→h3. Verify the host page's overall heading order across sections since they coexist in the DOM.

findings.title: Dialogs use aria-label strings instead of aria-labelledby pointing at the visible title — and the haggle dialog has no programmatic description
findings.problem: Every modal sets aria-label to a string that duplicates (or paraphrases) the visible <h2> title, rather than aria-labelledby referencing the heading element. This means the visible title and the accessible name can drift, and the rich on-screen heading (e.g. 'CLOSING TIME — DAY 3') is announced as a flatter aria-label. The haggle dialog (aria-label 'Buying X') has no aria-describedby tying it to the price/quip/loss-warning content, so a SR user entering the dialog hears only 'Buying X, dialog' and must hunt. WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2 (name from content is preferred).
findings.recommendation:
Give each panel title an id and reference it:

…

+ role=dialog aria-labelledby="dayEndTitle". For the haggle, add aria-describedby pointing at the price row and the loss/affordability note so the salient numbers are read on open. This is a small refactor and removes the duplicate-string maintenance hazard.

findings.title: Card aria-labels are extremely chatty and partly duplicate the title attribute, producing long, repetitive SR announcements
findings.problem: ShelfItem builds a label like 'Health Potion, common Potion, Kaito asks 32g. Worth about 28g. In demand — flips for +70%. Not enough coin. Buy.' — up to ~30 words — and ALSO sets title={item.flavor + flipHint} (a different long string). The aria-label restates rarity/category/demand that are also conveyed by the visible flip tag and rarity pip (which itself has its own role=img aria-label 'common rarity', line 562 — so rarity is announced twice). On a 5–7 card shelf this is a wall of speech; the 'Buy.' / 'Tap to sell.' verb appended to a <button> is redundant (the role already says 'button'). The bag label even says 'Tap to sell' on a control reached by keyboard. WCAG 1.3.1, plus 2.5.3-adjacent verbosity / 4.1.2 best practice.
findings.recommendation: Trim to: name + price + one demand/affordability clause, e.g. 'Health Potion, 32g, common Potion. In demand, flips for +70%.' Drop the rarity pip's separate role=img aria-label (or drop rarity from the button label — pick one source). Remove trailing 'Buy.'/'Tap to sell.' verbs (button role implies action). Move the long flavor/strategy text to aria-describedby on the button so it's available on demand rather than read every time. Keep the disabled reason ('Not enough coin') because disabled buttons aren't focusable so it must ride on... — actually since disabled cards (line 549) are removed from the tab order entirely, the 'reason' text is unreachable by keyboard; surface affordability in the still-focusable state or don't disable (see next finding).

findings.title: Unaffordable shelf cards are `disabled`, removing them from the tab order so keyboard/SR users can't inspect why or what they cost
findings.problem: When the player can't afford an item or the bag is full, the card gets disabled. Disabled buttons are not focusable, so a keyboard or screen-reader user tabbing the shelf simply skips them — they cannot read the item name, price, or the 'Not enough coin / bag full' reason that's baked into the aria-label (which now never gets announced). They also can't tell how much they'd need. Sighted users at least see the dimmed card (opacity .5, contrast still fine per my audit). This hides game state from non-visual users. WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2; also a usability regression for keyboard users.
findings.recommendation: Don't disable; instead keep the button focusable with aria-disabled="true" and on activation either no-op + announce 'Not enough coin — you have Xg of Yg' via the toast/live region, or open the haggle and let the existing 'can't pay' path (completeBuy 338-344) handle it. This keeps the card inspectable and the reason audible. Retain the visual .cardLocked styling.

findings.title: Toast (role=status) is the only live region, but it's used for events/errors and is unmounted after 3.4s — outcomes that should be polite-announced ride nothing
findings.location: Shop.jsx:1136-1151 (Toast role=status aria-live=polite), engine toast() shopEngine.js:61-63
findings.problem: The lone live region is the toast, which is correctly role=status aria-live=polite aria-atomic-ish. But it only fires for: bag-full, can't-afford, and day events. Critically, the toast TEXT is set in the engine and the component keys its setShown effect on [n, toast] — if two toasts share identical text the n counter handles it, but the toast unmounts (returns null) after 3.4s, so a SR that's mid-utterance on something else may never voice it. More importantly, the big-ticket outcomes (deal struck, rent paid, day advanced, win/lose) do NOT use the toast and have no other live region. So the toast gives a false sense that 'status messages are handled.'
findings.recommendation: Keep the toast for transient events, but add the dedicated polite live region from finding #1 for deal/rapport/day-transition outcomes. Consider not fully unmounting the toast node (render an empty live region container that's always present and only swap its text) so assistive tech keeps a stable live region rather than one that mounts/unmounts — mount/unmount of an aria-live node is unreliable across SRs (WCAG 4.1.3 best practice).

findings.title: Gold counter changes are not announced; the visual 'goldPop' flourish has no non-visual equivalent
findings.problem: When gold ticks up from a sale/tip, the code adds a 0.6s visual pop animation (goldUp). The .hudGold span (282) has only a title attribute ('Coin on hand') and is not a live region, so the actual coin total change is invisible to SR users. Combined with finding #1 (deal outcome silent), a blind player has no way to track their money except by tabbing back to the counter and re-reading it. WCAG 1.4.1 (info conveyed by animation only) / 4.1.3.
findings.recommendation: Fold the new gold total into the deal live-region announcement ('...you now hold 187g'). Optionally make .hudGold a polite live region, but beware over-announcing during rent deduction — prefer announcing the total as part of explicit deal/day-end messages rather than auto-on-every-change.

findings.title: Kaito's portrait quip changes are announced only when a modal is up (and duplicated/hidden via aria-hidden) — the standing shop quip is mute and the bubble's aria-hidden toggling is fragile
findings.problem: The portrait bubble shows state.quip and is aria-hidden={muted} with visibility:hidden when any modal is up — sensible to avoid a duplicate of the modal's own quip. But the standing bubble is plain text in no live region, so when the quip changes outside a haggle (e.g. greet on day start) it's never announced. And aria-hidden is set to the boolean `muted` (true/false) rather than the string 'true'/undefined; React serializes false to aria-hidden="false" which is harmless but the intent (remove from a11y tree only when muted) is what's wanted — verify it's not accidentally hiding the bubble's text from the tree at the wrong time. The img alt 'Kaito the shopkeeper' (496) is fine; the haggle portrait alt is just 'Kaito' (702) and the story/codex/end portraits use alt 'Kaito' or alt="" (codex 1099) — that last empty alt on an unlocked story portrait is arguably under-described but acceptable as decorative beside the title.
findings.recommendation: Tie quip announcements to the live region (finding #1) rather than the visible bubble. Confirm aria-hidden serialization: prefer aria-hidden={muted || undefined} so it's absent when not muted rather than aria-hidden="false". Standardize portrait alt text ('Kaito the shopkeeper' everywhere) for consistency; the codex alt="" is fine since the title labels the card.

findings.title: Patience meter (role=img) recomputes its aria-label but never re-announces; candle pips convey state by color only
findings.problem: Patience is a row of styled spans wrapped in a role=img with a good aria-label ('Kaito's patience: 2 of 3...'). Because it's role=img the inner pips are correctly hidden, and the label updates when patience drops. But role=img is not a live region, so the drain is only heard if the user re-focuses/re-reads it — and patience draining is a key tactical signal (at 0 he makes a final offer). The 'low' state is a flicker animation (pipLow) plus color, with no text distinction beyond the count. This is mostly covered by finding #1's announcement, but worth calling out as its own non-visual signal.
findings.recommendation: Include patience in the per-offer live announcement ('patience down to 1 of 3 — one more and he makes his final offer'). The static role=img label is a fine on-demand fallback; just ensure the live region carries the change.

findings.title: Focus trap: FOCUSABLE filter `el.offsetParent !== null` mis-handles position:fixed children and can drop the only focusable element
findings.problem: The Tab handler filters focusables by `el.offsetParent !== null || el === document.activeElement`. offsetParent is null for any element with position:fixed (and for display:none), so if a future modal control were position:fixed it would be excluded from the trap even though it's visible. The fallback `|| el === document.activeElement` partly saves it, but the wrap-around math (first/last) would then be computed from a list that may exclude the active element's true neighbors. In the current modals all controls are static-position so this doesn't bite today, but it's a latent correctness bug. Also FOCUSABLE omits `audio[controls]`, `video[controls]`, `[contenteditable]`, and `summary` — fine here since none are used. WCAG 2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap) / 2.4.3.
findings.recommendation: Replace the offsetParent check with a robust visibility test: filter on `el.getClientRects().length > 0 && getComputedStyle(el).visibility !== 'hidden'`. This handles fixed-position and is the pattern focus-trap libraries use. Keep the activeElement fallback. Low priority given current static layouts.

findings.title: Help/Codex panels can be open when a phase modal mounts; the cleanup closes them but focus restoration can land on a now-removed trigger
findings.location: Shop.jsx:38-73 (useFocusTrap restoration), 239-244 (effect closing help/codex when phase changes), 435-438
