findings.problem: useFocusTrap captures triggerRef during first render and restores focus to it on unmount (line 70-71), guarded by document.contains(t). When a phase modal (e.g. backstory) appears while Help is open, the effect at 239 closes Help — both scrims unmount around the same commit. Help's trigger was the '?' HUD button (still in DOM, fine), but if the trigger element was itself inside a modal that also unmounted (e.g. Codex opened from... it can't today), restoration would no-op and focus falls to <body>, stranding keyboard users. More realistically: when the haggle deal block swaps the active→deal panel, the autoFocus moves to Continue, but the trap's triggerRef still points at the shelf card; on close focus correctly returns there — verify the active→deal transition (status change, same Scrim instance, no remount) doesn't re-run the trap (it doesn't, since Scrim stays mounted) so the deal block's autoFocus on Continue (748) is what actually fires. That's correct, but it means Escape-after-deal and the trap share one trigger ref — OK. Net: a real but narrow edge where focus can fall to body.
findings.recommendation: After restoring, if document.contains(trigger) is false or focus landed on body, fall back to focusing a stable element (the game region or the HUD '?' button). Add `if (document.activeElement === document.body) gameRegionRef.current?.focus()` in the trap cleanup. Also consider preventing two scrims from ever coexisting by gating Help/Codex behind state.phase === 'shop' at render time, not just via the cleanup effect.

findings.title: Run silently starts and mutates on page load before the user reaches the Shop; off-screen section is inert but the game state advances on first focus's intro dialog
findings.location: Shop.jsx:149-152 (seedRef Date.now() at mount), Home.jsx:63-71 (inert), Shop.jsx:213-222 (intro dialog on first focus)
findings.problem: createRun(Date.now()) runs at component mount — i.e. on page load, while the Shop is off-screen — so a run is already in progress before the player scrolls there. Home.jsx correctly sets child.inert on non-current sections (good: keeps off-screen controls out of the tab order and unclickable, satisfying 2.4.3/4.1.2 for hidden content). However, inert is a relatively recent property; on older engines without the inert reflection it would silently do nothing and the off-screen game's ~15 buttons would be in the tab order. More of a robustness note than a present-day defect. Separately, the autoplaying portrait bob + flame flicker are correctly disabled under prefers-reduced-motion (CSS 1549-1555) — good.
findings.recommendation: No functional a11y fix required if inert is acceptable for the target browsers (it is, 2023+). For belt-and-suspenders, also set aria-hidden + tabindex management or confirm the inert polyfill is bundled. Optionally defer createRun until first focus so the game doesn't run invisibly. Document the inert reliance.

findings.title: Color-only signals: flip/wanted tags, rarity pips, and profit pos/neg rely on color + a tiny star glyph; the fair-band slider is color+position only
findings.problem: Most color signals DO have a redundant text/glyph cue (flip tag carries '★ FLIP +70%' text, wanted tag '★ WANTED', profit shows a signed number with +/−, rarity has a role=img label) — so 1.4.1 is largely satisfied and contrast is fine (white-on-green 5.2–7.2:1, profit red on parch 4.7:1 per my audit). The remaining color-only conveyance is the slider track's sage/terracotta bands (covered by finding #2) and the rarity PIP color which only has meaning via the help-panel legend (the role=img says 'rare rarity' so SR is fine; sighted color-blind users rely on the legend, which is acceptable). The profit +/− sign disambiguates green/red, so deuteranopia is handled. So this is minor.
findings.recommendation: Primary fix is the slider valuetext (finding #2). Optionally add a tiny shape/letter difference to rarity pips for colorblind sighted users (e.g. legendary already gets a gold ring — extend with a notch/initial), but this is enhancement-grade since the legend + text labels cover it.

findings.title: Stale/incorrect _audit/contrast.json describes a different page entirely
findings.problem: Every entry in the prior contrast pass references an element 'Home'/'Oldest' with fg #ffffff on bg #7cc1f6 / #0b81b7 at sizes 50/14px — that is a blue UI from elsewhere on the site (likely a nav/age toggle), NOT the Shop's wood/parchment theme. The ratios it flags (1.94 'need 3', 4.33 'need 4.5') are real failures but for the WRONG component, so this artifact gives a misleading picture of the Shop and could cause someone to 'fix' nonexistent Shop issues. My own computed audit of the Shop palette shows it passes AA comprehensively (lowest text pair I found was profitNeg #b23b2c on parch at 4.67:1, still ≥4.5).
findings.recommendation: Delete _audit/contrast.json or regenerate it scoped to the Shop section. The 1.94:1 white-on-#7cc1f6 finding it contains is a genuine failure that belongs to whichever blue component it actually sampled — track that separately, outside this game's audit.

findings.title: Escape semantics are inconsistent across modals and not discoverable; some dialogs trap with no documented exit
findings.location: Shop.jsx:660-661 (haggle: Escape=Walk or Close), 897 (DayEnd: no Escape, comment), 932-933 (Backstory: Escape=ack), 958 (RunEnd: no Escape), 1008/1072 (Help/Codex: Escape=close + backdrop)
findings.problem: Escape behavior varies by modal — fine and intentional (committing gates like DayEnd/RunEnd deliberately have no Escape, focus stays trapped on the primary button). That's defensible (2.1.2 is satisfied because the primary button advances the flow). The issue is discoverability and consistency: there's no instructions text saying Escape walks/closes, the haggle's Escape behavior changes meaning mid-flow (Walk before deal, Close after), and the committing gates give a keyboard user no spoken cue that Escape won't work and they must press the button. Not a hard WCAG failure but a usability/expectation gap (3.2.x consistency).
findings.recommendation: Add a visually-hidden instruction in each dialog's describedby ('Press Escape to walk away' / 'Press the button to continue — this choice is required'). Keep the committing-gate design. Ensure the haggle's Escape meaning change is announced via the live region when status flips to deal.

dimension: Responsive layout, viewport robustness & host integration
summary: The Shop is built almost exclusively in vmin with a 100dvh root, which makes it scale gracefully across DESKTOP/LAPTOP heights — I verified the vertical budget holds at 1920×1080, 1366×768, 1280×800, and even 1280×720: the @media(max-height:800) tweaks plus the wants board's overflow-y:auto escape hatch keep the HUD + stage + bagBar fitting with ~5 shelf rows visible and no clipping. So the laptop story is genuinely solid. The cracks are elsewhere: (1) On small landscape phones/tablets (height ~360–430px), vmin collapses to ~3.6–4.3px, so the game's many 1.0–1.6vmin labels render at literally 4–7px — illegible — and the clamp() legibility net only covers a handful of classes, missing most of the HUD, wants board, prices, buttons, ledger and modal body text. The pointer:coarse block bumps a few hit targets to 44px but the surrounding text is still microscopic, so landscape mobile is technically reachable but practically unusable. (2) Portrait is hard-blocked for ALL devices via window.innerWidth<=window.innerHeight, which also gates tablets and large phones held upright — a heavy stance for a 2026 portfolio whose 4th-section showpiece is a game. (3) A real integration bug: Home.jsx's global touchmove listener calls preventDefault() unconditionally on a non-passive window handler, which suppresses native scrolling inside the scrollable Codex/Help modals on any touch device. (4) Architectural smells: the run seeds with Date.now() at mount so a game silently starts before the user ever scrolls to it; dvh is used with no vh/JS fallback for older Safari/Firefox; a fixed 150px portraitFrame floor and 8vmin bagEmpty min-height don't scale down on short viewports. The vmin-only strategy is the root cause — it conflates "scale with screen" with "stay legible," which works on big screens and fails on small ones. The fix is a hybrid clamp() type scale, a couple of small-viewport media tweaks, decoupling the run seed from mount, a touch-scroll guard, and a decision on real mobile support.

findings.title: Global touchmove preventDefault() blocks scrolling inside Codex/Help modals on touch devices
findings.problem: Home registers a non-passive window touchmove listener that calls event.preventDefault() UNCONDITIONALLY at the top of the handler (line 110), before any guard. This is intended to stop the page from native-scrolling so the section-snap can take over. But the Shop's Codex and Help modals are taller than the viewport and rely on overflow:auto (Shop.module.css:1311, 1402 with max-height:calc(100dvh - 12vmin)). On a touch device, every touch-drag inside those modals is preventDefault'd by the window listener, so the modal body cannot be scrolled by finger — the bottom story cards and the rarity legend become unreachable. The modal scrim sets overscroll-behavior:contain but that does not re-enable scrolling once the ancestor has called preventDefault.
findings.evidence: handleTouchMove starts with `event.preventDefault();` (Home.jsx:110) and is attached `{ passive: false }` (Home.jsx:137); modals use `overflow: auto` (Shop.module.css:1311 .helpPanel, 1402 .codexPanel).
findings.recommendation: Make preventDefault conditional: only call it when the touch target is NOT inside a scrollable overlay. e.g. `if (e.target.closest('#overlay-root')) return;` at the top of handleTouchMove, or skip preventDefault when isScrollable.current is false AND a modal is up. Better: gate the whole section-snap touch handler on `!modalUp` state lifted to Home, mirroring the existing setScrollable(!modalUp) logic.

verification.reasoning:
Verified against the actual code. The mechanism is real and accurately described:

1. Home.jsx:109-110 — handleTouchMove's FIRST statement is `event.preventDefault();`, executed before any guard (the isScrollable/scrollTimerOn/initDone checks are at lines 116-121, AFTER the preventDefault).
2. Home.jsx:137 — the listener is attached to `window` with `{ passive: false }`, so the preventDefault is effective and can cancel the browser's default touch-scroll.
3. The modals are portaled to #overlay-root (Shop.jsx:97-101, a body-level fixed layer per index.css:75-80), which is still a descendant of `window`, so touchmove events inside the modal reach the window listener.
4. .helpPanel (Shop.module.css:1304-1311) and .codexPanel (1396-1402) both use `overflow: auto` + `max-height: calc(100dvh - 12vmin)`, so they genuinely require internal finger-scrolling to reach the bottom story cards / rarity legend. The .overlay scrim (789-803) is also overflow-y:auto.
5. Confirmed via grep that NO touchmove/stopPropagation handler exists anywhere in Shop.jsx — nothing stops propagation to the window listener, and overscroll-behavior:contain (used on .overlay 798 and .haggle 812) only governs scroll-chaining at boundaries; it cannot restore a scroll an ancestor already cancelled. The finding states this correctly.

On touch devices, a non-passive ancestor calling preventDefault() on touchmove cancels the default scroll for that gesture, including descendant overflow scrolling — so dragging inside the modal body does nothing, exactly as claimed.

A detail the finding under-states (but that strengthens it): Shop.jsx:234 already calls setScrollable(!modalUp), forcing isScrollable.current=false while a modal is up. So the section-snap branch (guarded at Home.jsx:117) is already disabled in the modal state — meaning the unconditional preventDefault at line 110 is not only harmful but functionally pointless while a modal is open. It blocks scrolling for no benefit.

Severity note: the host gates the whole site behind a landscape check (HorizontalEnjoyer when innerWidth<=innerHeight, Home.jsx:45-58,160), so this only bites touch devices held in landscape (tablets / large phones). That narrows the affected population for a desktop-leaning portfolio, so a 'medium' rating is defensible. But within that device class the bug makes real content (bottom story cards, rarity legend) genuinely unreachable with no workaround, which justifies keeping high. I confirm high as reasonable.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Early-return before preventDefault when a modal/overlay is up, reusing the existing signal rather than adding a DOM query. Two equivalent options:

(A) Cheapest: since Shop already drives setScrollable(!modalUp) (Shop.jsx:234), and isScrollable.current is the single source of truth for whether the section-scroller should respond, gate preventDefault on it. Change Home.jsx:109-110 to:
```
const handleTouchMove = (event) => {
  if (!isScrollable.current) return; // a modal/overlay is up — let it scroll natively
  event.preventDefault();
  ...
```
This also makes the preventDefault match the wheel handler's logic (which already no-ops when !isScrollable.current) and removes the now-redundant isScrollable check later in the function.

(B) More targeted (survives if scrollable semantics ever change): keep preventDefault for genuine page-snap gestures but bail when the touch originates inside the portal layer:
```
if (event.target.closest('#overlay-root')) return;
```
at the very top of handleTouchMove.

Option (A) is preferred — it is one line, reuses existing state, and fixes the root cause (preventDefault firing while the page is intentionally non-snapping). Note the original recommendation's `closest('#overlay-root')` is correct (the portal target id is indeed 'overlay-root', confirmed at Shop.jsx:99 / index.css:75), not the haggle modal's own panel. Also add `touch-action: pan-y` to .helpPanel/.codexPanel/.overlay as defense-in-depth so the browser hints these regions are scrollable.

findings.title: vmin-only typography renders 4–7px text on landscape phones/tablets; legibility clamp net is incomplete
findings.location: src/Pages/Home/Shop/Shop.module.css (pervasive 1.0–1.6vmin font-sizes); legibility floor only at 1637-1653
findings.problem: Nearly every text size is expressed in raw vmin. On a landscape phone (e.g. 812×375, vmin=3.75px) or tablet (~430px height) the body sizes resolve to: wantsTitle 1.35vmin≈5px, eventChip 1.3vmin≈5px, cardWorth 1.2vmin≈4.5px, flipTag/wantedTag 1vmin≈3.8px, cardName 1.4vmin≈5.3px, rapportNext 1.15vmin≈4.3px, ledger .line 1.8vmin≈6.8px, most buttons 1.6vmin≈6px. The only legibility safety net is one media block (max-width:1100px),(max-height:740px) that clamps a SMALL SUBSET — cardName, flipTag/wantedTag/newBadge, and rapportNext/cardWorth/endDaySub/haggleNote/slideHint. It misses the HUD (hudDay, hudRent, streakChip), wantsTitle/wantRow/eventChip, cardPrice, all modal/ledger text, all primary/secondary/ghost buttons, haggleSub, codex/help body. So at phone heights the game is unreadable even though pointer:coarse enlarges a few buttons.
findings.evidence: Computed: at 812×375 vmin=3.75px; e.g. .flipTag font-size:1vmin (line 521)=3.75px, .cardWorth 1.2vmin (598)=4.5px, .line 1.8vmin (1232)=6.8px. The clamp block at 1637-1653 only lists ~9 selectors.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a hybrid type scale: replace bare vmin font-sizes with clamp(min, Nvmin, max) site-wide for text, e.g. cardName clamp(12px,1.4vmin,16px), buttons clamp(13px,1.6vmin,18px), ledger clamp(13px,1.8vmin,20px), HUD readouts clamp(13px,1.9–2.4vmin,26px). This keeps the big-screen scaling you have while guaranteeing a readable floor. Consider a single --fs-* token set in :root to avoid scattering clamps.

verification.reasoning:
Verified against the actual CSS and host. The legibility clamp net is the only font-size clamp in the file and it covers just a small subset: Shop.module.css:1637-1653 sets font-size clamps for .cardName (1639, floor 11px), .flipTag/.wantedTag/.newBadge (1644, floor 9px), and .rapportNext/.cardWorth/.endDaySub/.haggleNote/.slideHint (1651, floor 10px). Every other text size is bare vmin and uncovered, exactly as claimed. Confirmed specific examples: .hudDay 1.9vmin (97), .hudGold 2.4vmin (116), .streakChip 1.6vmin (134), .hudRent 1.7vmin (150), .wantsTitle 1.35vmin (336), .wantRow 1.6vmin (351), .eventChip 1.3vmin (364), .cardPrice 1.7vmin (574), .line (ledger) 1.8vmin (1231), and the modal action buttons .btnPrimary/.btnSecondary/.btnGhost 1.6vmin (1097) — none of these appear in the clamp block. The only other clamp() uses (284, 809, 1175, 1308, 1399) are widths/heights, not text. The @media(max-height:800px) block (1611-1630) only touches padding/gap and .wants max-height; @media(max-width:1200px) only changes grid columns; the @media(pointer:coarse) block (1577-1606) enlarges helpBtn/stepper/slider control boxes but sets no font-size — so it does nothing for text legibility, matching the finding's wording.

Math confirmed at 812x375 (vmin=3.75px): flipTag 1vmin=3.75px, cardWorth 1.2vmin=4.5px, wantsTitle 1.35vmin=5.06px, eventChip 1.3vmin=4.875px, ledger .line 1.8vmin=6.75px, buttons 1.6vmin=6px. All within rounding of the finding's numbers.

Reachability is real: Home.jsx:49 gates only width<=height (portrait) via HorizontalEnjoyer; a landscape phone (width>height) passes the gate and renders the full game with raw-vmin text. Since the site funnels mobile users into landscape, this is the intended mobile surface, not an obscure edge case — so unreadable core text there is a genuine defect, not a subjective preference. Severity high is appropriate (breaks the mobile-landscape path the site steers users toward; does not affect desktop, the primary target, and does not crash — so not critical).

One minor internal inconsistency in the finding (does not change the verdict): its opening 'Computed' list cites 'cardName 1.4vmin≈5.3px' as unreadable, but cardName IS already clamped at line 1639 (floor 11px), and the finding's own problem text correctly acknowledges cardName is in the covered subset. So cardName specifically does not render at 5px on phone heights; the dozens of other selectors do.
verification.refinedRecommendation: Adopt a tokenized hybrid type scale rather than scattering ad-hoc clamps. Define a --fs-* set in :root (e.g. --fs-hud, --fs-hud-gold, --fs-body, --fs-label, --fs-micro, --fs-btn, --fs-title) each as clamp(min, Nvmin, max), and replace the bare-vmin font-size declarations throughout with these tokens. Suggested floors/ceilings: HUD readouts (hudDay/hudGold/hudRent/streakChip) clamp(13px, ~1.9-2.4vmin, 26px); buttons (.btnPrimary/.btnSecondary/.btnGhost, .endDay) clamp(13px, 1.6vmin, 18px); ledger .line clamp(13px, 1.8vmin, 20px); body/quip/bubble/haggleQuip clamp(12px, 1.6-1.7vmin, 18px); labels (wantsTitle/wantRow/eventChip/cardPrice/priceLabel/haggleSub/recordsLine) clamp(11px, ~1.3-1.6vmin, 14-16px); micro (cardWorth/flipTag/wantedTag/rapportNext/newBadge) clamp(9-10px, ~1-1.2vmin, 12-13px); codex/help body (.codexText p, codexCardTitle, modal copy) clamp(12px, 1.5vmin, 16px). Once tokens carry the floor, delete the partial 1637-1653 clamp block to avoid two competing nets. Drop cardName from the 'needs new clamp' list — it is already clamped at line 1639 (fold it into --fs-label). Additionally, because clamping text to a floor will overflow the vmin-sized boxes/HUD bar on a 375px-tall landscape phone, add a min-height/scroll or stacking fallback for the .hud and .wants regions at small heights (the @media(max-height:800px) block already special-cases .wants), and verify no truncation after the floor takes effect. Effort M is accurate.

findings.title: Portrait is hard-blocked for ALL devices including tablets, with no real mobile/touch experience
findings.problem: isPortrait is set whenever window.innerWidth <= window.innerHeight, which renders a full-screen black 'tilt your device Horizontally' gate over the ENTIRE site (z-index 999999). This blocks: any phone held upright, any TABLET in portrait (iPad portrait is a very common reading posture), and even a narrow/tall desktop window. For a portfolio in 2026 whose headline 4th section is a game, gating all portrait + delivering an unusable landscape-phone experience effectively means the site shows nothing playable to the large share of mobile/tablet visitors. The gate copy ('tilt/adjust your device/screen Horizontally for optimal viewing') is also vague and uses a raster image with no responsive sizing (width:30vw fixed).
findings.evidence: `setIsPortrait(window.innerWidth <= window.innerHeight)` (Home.jsx:49); `{isPortrait && <HorizontalEnjoyer />}` (Home.jsx:160); HoriRoot z-index:999999 covers everything (HorizontalEnjoyer.module.css:8).
findings.recommendation: Pick one of two paths. (A) If keeping landscape-only: at minimum make the landscape experience actually usable (the clamp type scale above) and replace the portrait gate with a friendlier, branded rotate prompt that exempts tablets above a width threshold (e.g. allow portrait when min(w,h) >= 700px). (B) Recommended for AAA-feel: build a true portrait layout for the Shop specifically — it is the most layout-flexible section (HUD can stack, leftCol can move above the shelf, bag can become a horizontal scroll strip). The Shop already has all logic decoupled in the engine, so a portrait CSS variant is the highest-ROI mobile investment. At a minimum, ship (A) now and scope (B) as the revamp's mobile milestone.

verification.reasoning:
I read Home.jsx, HorizontalEnjoyer.jsx, and HorizontalEnjoyer.module.css in full, and grepped the whole repo for any width/orientation escape hatch. Every cited piece of evidence checks out exactly:

- Home.jsx:49 `setIsPortrait(window.innerWidth <= window.innerHeight)` — the gate condition is purely aspect-ratio based with NO minimum-dimension threshold. So an iPad in portrait (e.g. 820x1180) satisfies 820 <= 1180 and is gated; a square window (==) is also gated; a narrow/tall desktop window is gated. The claim "blocks any phone upright, any tablet in portrait, and even a narrow/tall desktop window" is exactly correct.
- Home.jsx:160 `{isPortrait && <HorizontalEnjoyer />}` — confirmed.
- HorizontalEnjoyer.module.css:1-8 — `.HoriRoot { position: fixed; top:0; left:0; width:100vw; height:100%; background-color: black; z-index: 999999 }` covers the ENTIRE site over everything. Confirmed.
- HorizontalEnjoyer.jsx:7 copy "Please tilt/adjust your device/screen Horizontally for optimal viewing" — vague, confirmed verbatim.
- HorizontalEnjoyer.module.css:24-27 — the image is a `.png` raster with fixed `width: 30vw` and no responsive sizing/media queries. Confirmed.

A repo-wide grep for isPortrait/innerWidth/innerHeight/orientation found the gate is defined only at Home.jsx:45/49 and used only at Home.jsx:160 — there is no width-threshold exemption anywhere, so the tablet/desktop-portrait blocking is real and unmitigated.

The central defect is real and accurately described, so this is "confirmed" rather than "partial." The only part that is an unverified extrapolation (not a defect I independently confirmed) is the secondary assertion that the LANDSCAPE phone experience is "unusable" / that the site "shows nothing playable to a large share of mobile/tablet visitors" — I verified the gate logic, not the quality of the Shop's landscape responsive layout, so that supporting claim is a reasonable opinion rather than proven. It does not undermine the core finding.

Severity "high" is appropriate and I keep it: for a 2026 portfolio whose headline 4th section is a game, hard-blocking all portrait viewers including the very common iPad-portrait reading posture is a significant reach/accessibility loss. It is not "critical" because (a) it does not crash or corrupt anything, (b) landscape users are unaffected, and (c) the gate problem itself has a genuinely cheap mitigation (add a min-dimension exemption), which the recommendation already notes.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Two-tier fix, both verified as feasible against the code:

QUICK FIX (S effort, ship now) — make the gate dimension-aware instead of pure aspect ratio. At Home.jsx:49 replace `setIsPortrait(window.innerWidth <= window.innerHeight)` with a guard that only gates genuinely small portrait viewports, e.g.:
`const w = window.innerWidth, h = window.innerHeight; setIsPortrait(w < h && Math.min(w, h) < 700);`
This exempts iPad/tablet portrait and tall desktop windows while still nudging phones. Prefer the matchMedia orientation API plus a width query (`window.matchMedia('(orientation: portrait) and (max-width: 700px)')`) and listen to its `change` event rather than `resize`, which also fixes mobile-browser address-bar resize churn. While there, address the gate polish the finding flags: (1) rewrite the copy to a single clear instruction ("Rotate your device to landscape to play"), (2) give the image responsive sizing with `max-width` and a sensible `clamp()` instead of fixed `width:30vw` (HorizontalEnjoyer.module.css:26), and consider replacing the raster `.png` with an inline SVG to match the project's existing inline-SVG icon approach (itemIcons.jsx). The z-index:999999 is fine to keep as an intentional full-cover overlay.

PROPER FIX (L effort, revamp milestone) — build a real portrait layout for the Shop section specifically, since its logic is fully decoupled in shopEngine.js. A portrait Shop CSS variant should: stack the HUD vertically, move leftCol (portrait/quip + demand board) above the shelf grid, collapse the shelf to a 2-wide grid, and turn the bag bar into a horizontal scroll strip. Gate ONLY the non-Shop sections in portrait if those layouts can't be made responsive in scope. This is the highest-ROI mobile investment because the engine requires no changes — only Shop.module.css media queries.

Validation note for whoever implements: the gate currently re-fires on every `resize`; ensure the new matchMedia listener is the single source of truth and that the existing touch-scroll handlers (Home.jsx:109-133) still drive section navigation on touch devices once portrait is no longer universally blocked.

findings.title: Run silently starts on page load (Date.now() seed at mount) before user reaches the section
findings.problem: All sections are mounted simultaneously (Home maps Sections and only translates them off-screen). Shop computes `seedRef = useRef(Date.now())` and initializes the reducer with createRun(seed) at mount (Shop.jsx:149-152). So a full run — day 1, shelf, wants, rent clock conceptually — is generated on initial page load, long before the visitor scrolls to section 4. Because the engine is turn-based (no wall-clock timer) this is not a correctness bug today, but it (a) does meaningful RNG/day-generation work for every visitor who never reaches the game, (b) means the 'intro dialog on first focus' and the records-banking effects are armed from load, and (c) makes the seed a function of when the PAGE loaded, not when the player started — surprising if a timer mechanic is ever added.
findings.evidence: `const seedRef = useRef((Date.now() >>> 0) || 1); const [state,dispatch]=useReducer(reduce, undefined, ()=>createRun(seedRef.current));` (Shop.jsx:149-152). Section mounted via React.cloneElement in the always-rendered map (Home.jsx:180-188).
findings.recommendation: Defer run creation until first focus: keep state lazily null/idle until isfocus becomes true the first time, then dispatch a START action that creates the run with a fresh Date.now() seed. This aligns the seed with actual play, avoids wasted work for non-players, and gives a natural 'press to begin' moment. Alternatively gate createRun behind a one-shot effect keyed on isfocus.

findings.title: dvh used everywhere with no vh fallback for browsers lacking dynamic viewport units
findings.problem: The host scroller height, the per-section -100dvh translate, the Shop root height, and all four modal max-heights use dvh exclusively. dvh (dynamic viewport height) is unsupported in Safari <15.4 and older Firefox/Chromium. In those browsers `height:100dvh` and `calc(100dvh - 12vmin)` are invalid declarations that are dropped, so the root has NO height (collapses) and modals lose their max-height clamp (tall modals overflow the viewport). index.css already hints at the old workaround (`height:-webkit-fill-available` on html/body) but the inline dvh styles do not benefit from it.
findings.evidence: Inline `style={{ height: '100dvh' }}` (Home.jsx:159, Shop.jsx:271, SectionContainer.jsx:9); `translateY(calc(${currentSection} * -100dvh))` (Home.jsx:176); `max-height: calc(100dvh - 12vmin)` (Shop.module.css:810 etc). No vh fallback anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Provide a cascade fallback: in CSS, declare `height:100vh; height:100dvh;` (older browsers take the vh line, modern ones override with dvh). For the inline styles, either move them to CSS classes with the two-line fallback, or set a `--app-h` CSS var from JS (visualViewport/innerHeight) and use `height: var(--app-h)`. For modal max-heights, write `max-height: calc(100vh - 12vmin); max-height: calc(100dvh - 12vmin);`.

findings.title: Fixed 150px portraitFrame floor + 8vmin bagEmpty min-height don't scale on short viewports
findings.problem: Two fixed-ish vertical costs resist the otherwise-graceful vmin shrink. (1) .portraitFrame height is clamp(150px,24vmin,240px): below ~625px viewport min-dimension the 150px floor dominates, so on a 375–430px-tall landscape phone the portrait alone consumes 150px of a ~300px stage — half the playfield — squeezing the wants board and shelf. (2) .bagEmpty min-height:8vmin plus bagBar padding makes the bag bar the single largest fixed-by-vmin band; combined with the portrait floor, the @media(max-height:800) block (which only trims padding/gaps and caps the wants board) is not enough headroom relief below ~700px. My budget calc shows it still technically fits to ~360px tall but with the portrait eating 50%+ of the stage and text already illegible.
findings.evidence: `height: clamp(150px, 24vmin, 240px)` (line 284); at 812×375 24vmin=90px so the 150px floor wins, vs a 299px stage budget (computed). `.bagEmpty { min-height: 8vmin }` (line 710).
findings.recommendation: Add a short-height media block (e.g. @media(max-height:560px) or (max-height:430px)) that lowers the portrait clamp floor (e.g. clamp(96px,22vmin,240px)), reduces bagEmpty min-height to ~6vmin, and tightens bag/portrait. Better long-term: in a portrait/mobile layout move the portrait beside the HUD or shrink it to a header bust so it stops competing with the shelf for vertical space.

findings.title: Shelf grid minmax(13vmin) yields very few columns on narrow desktop and oversized cards on ultrawide/4K
findings.problem: The shelf is `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(13vmin,1fr))` inside the 70%-width shelfWrap (leftCol is a fixed 30%). On ultrawide/4K, vmin tracks the (large) height, so 13vmin cards balloon (at 3840×2160, 13vmin=281px per card) and the shelf shows only a few enormous wares with lots of dead space — the fixed 30% leftCol also leaves a very wide, sparse demand column. On narrow desktop the 1200px breakpoint drops to 11vmin which helps, but the 30% leftCol stays fixed so the playfield can feel cramped. The grid scales by height (vmin) rather than by available width, which is the wrong axis for a column count.
findings.evidence: `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(13vmin, 1fr))` (line 425); at 2560×1440 13vmin=187px, at 3840×2160=281px; leftCol `flex: 0 0 30%` (line 236).
findings.recommendation: Drive card sizing by a px/rem-anchored clamp so column count tracks width, e.g. `minmax(clamp(120px, 13vmin, 180px), 1fr)`, capping max card size on 4K. Consider making leftCol `flex: 0 0 clamp(260px, 30%, 360px)` so it stops widening indefinitely on ultrawide and frees more width for the shelf. Optionally add a max-width container to the whole .root on very wide screens (e.g. center within max-width:2200px) so 4K doesn't stretch everything.

findings.title: Long item names, many wants, and long event text can overflow cards and the demand board
findings.problem: cardName has line-height:1.1, no max-height/clamp, and text-align:center, so a long name like 'Wheel of Cheese' (already 2 lines) plus the price chit and 'worth ~' line can make wanted cards taller than peers, breaking the shelf row rhythm (the shelf background draws plank ledges every 15vmin, so a card taller than the ledge band visually overruns the carved shelf line). The wants board lists 2–3 categories plus an event chip with multi-sentence text (e.g. the taxman/collector events); the board is flex:1 1 auto but under max-height:800 it gets max-height:26vmin and overflow-y:auto, so with 3 wants + a long event the chip can become a tiny inner-scroll region — easy to miss the event text. wantRow uses justify-content:space-between with no wrapping, fine for current short category names but brittle.
findings.evidence: `.cardName { line-height:1.1 }` no clamp (560-566); `.wants { max-height:26vmin; overflow-y:auto }` only under max-height:800 (1625-1629); event text up to multi-sentence (shopData.js:144-150).
findings.recommendation: Give cardName a 2-line clamp (display:-webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp:2; overflow:hidden) and a min-height so wanted vs normal cards stay the same height, preserving the shelf ledge alignment. For the demand board, ensure the event chip is always visible — either don't cap the wants board height (let the leftCol scroll as a whole) or move the event into its own non-scrolling row beneath the wants list. Verify with the longest event strings in shopData.js.

findings.title: Modals top-anchor + page padding 6vmin can cut off tall modals on short screens despite max-height clamp
findings.problem: The overlay uses align-items:flex-start with padding:6vmin and each panel max-height:calc(100dvh - 12vmin). On a SHORT landscape phone (375px tall) 6vmin top + 6vmin bottom = ~45px of padding, leaving the Codex (6 story cards) only ~330px of max-height to scroll within, with internal text already at ~4–6px. The overlay itself is overflow-y:auto so it can scroll, which mostly saves it — but combined with the touchmove-preventDefault bug above, on touch devices the scroll is dead. So the clamp math is correct but only works if (a) the touch-scroll bug is fixed and (b) text is legible. Worth verifying the codex specifically since it is the tallest content.
findings.evidence: `.overlay { align-items:flex-start; overflow-y:auto; padding:6vmin }` (789-799); `.codexPanel { max-height:calc(100dvh - 12vmin); overflow:auto }` (1400-1401); 6 RAPPORT_TIERS cards (shopData.js:164-207).
findings.recommendation: Reduce overlay padding on short viewports (e.g. @media(max-height:560px){ .overlay{ padding:3vmin } } and panel max-height:calc(100dvh - 6vmin)). Confirm the Codex with all 6 cards unlocked scrolls smoothly after fixing the touchmove bug. Keep align-items:flex-start (correct choice for tall panels).

findings.title: 100vw on .root/.HoriRoot causes horizontal scrollbar / clipping when a vertical scrollbar is present
findings.problem: Several roots use width:100vw. 100vw includes the classic (non-overlay) scrollbar gutter, so on Windows/Chromium with a visible scrollbar, 100vw is wider than the content area, producing a 1–17px horizontal overflow / shifted layout. The site mitigates this by hiding scrollbars (body::-webkit-scrollbar display:none, index.css:56) and overflow:hidden on .root (Shop.module.css:31), so it is largely masked today — but it is fragile: any browser that ignores the scrollbar-hiding (Firefox without scrollbar-gutter, forced scrollbars in OS settings) gets a horizontal scroll on the game.
findings.evidence: `.root { width: 100vw; overflow: hidden; }` (Shop.module.css:30-31); `.HoriRoot { width:100vw }` (HorizontalEnjoyer.module.css:5); `.HomeScroller{ width:100vw }` (Home.module.css:3).
findings.recommendation: Prefer width:100% (the root fills its already-correct parent) or `width:100dvw`/`100vw` with `overflow-x:hidden` guaranteed on html/body. Given overflow:hidden is already on .root the risk is low, but switching to 100% removes the scrollbar-gutter dependency entirely.

findings.title: Section-snap wheel handler can interrupt browsing the shelf even when not on a modal
findings.problem: While in the Shop with no modal up, setScrollable(true) is intentional so the player can leave the section. But the wheel handler is global and snaps to the next/prev section on any deltaY past the cooldown. The Shop's shelf is itself `overflow:auto` (Shop.module.css:444) — if the shelf has more rows than fit (common on short laptops where ~5 rows show but 7 items at narrow widths can exceed it), a player scrolling the shelf with the wheel will instead be yanked to the next section because the window wheel listener fires first and there is no 'consume wheel inside scrollable shelf' guard. This is an inner-scroll-fighting-outer-snap conflict the prompt asked about.
findings.evidence: `window.addEventListener('wheel', handleScroll)` global (Home.jsx:135); shelf `overflow:auto` (Shop.module.css:444); setScrollable(true) when no modal (Shop.jsx:233-234).
findings.recommendation: In handleScroll, ignore wheel events whose target is inside a scrollable, not-yet-at-edge element (check e.target.closest of the shelf and that it can still scroll in the wheel direction). Or lock section-snap while the pointer is over the shelf and only allow leaving via the page indicator/keyboard. This keeps shelf browsing smooth without trapping the user.

findings.title: Offscreen-but-mounted Shop runs animations and holds a live run for every visitor
findings.location: src/Pages/Home/Home.jsx:63-71,180-191; src/Pages/Home/Shop/Shop.module.css:299 (portrait bob infinite), 145 (flameFlicker infinite), 901 (pipFlicker infinite)
findings.problem: Because all sections are always mounted and only translated away, the Shop's infinite CSS animations (portrait bob 4.5s infinite line 299, streakFlame infinite 145, pipFlicker infinite 901) keep ticking off-screen, and the component keeps a full reducer state + effects armed even when the user is on section 0. Sections are marked inert when not current (Home.jsx:66-69) which handles a11y/clicks, but inert does not pause animations or unmount. On low-end mobile this is wasted GPU/CPU for a section the user may never see. The prefers-reduced-motion block helps only those users.
findings.evidence: `child.inert = i !== currentSection` (Home.jsx:67); `.portrait { animation: bob 4.5s ease-in-out infinite }` (line 299); always-mounted map (Home.jsx:180-188).
findings.recommendation: Pause off-screen animations: add a CSS rule keyed on a data-active attribute (set from isfocus) like `:not([data-active]) * { animation-play-state: paused }`, or use `content-visibility:auto`/`contain` on off-screen section roots. Combined with deferring createRun until focus (separate finding), this cuts idle cost for non-players.

dimension: Content, writing & narrative as a portfolio device

findings.title: Best beats (3.94 GPA, Senior SWE at Finofo) are unreachable for players who play to WIN
findings.problem: 150-seed sim: greedy winners (53 percent win) median rapport 91, max 103 - never cross 110 (tier 6 Finofo), only 8/80 cross 88 (tier 5 GPA). Only generous play (overpay +3 :353, undersell +3 :391) maxes rapport to 140 and unlocks all six, but win rate drops to 29 percent and nothing signals the lever (help line Shop.jsx:1042 reads as gouge-Kaito, +1). Win-players never read the two best resume lines.
findings.recommendation: Reveal one beat per trading day survived regardless of rapport (keep tiers for perks); or compress gates and add baseline +1/deal. Toast +3 vs +1. Add a Hear-the-rest button on win/Codex.
findings.evidence: Sim: greedy med91 max103 tier6=0 tier5=8/80; fair med140 all tier6 at 29 vs 53 percent win.

verification.reasoning:
I read shopData.js (RAPPORT_TIERS at :164-207, gates 12/28/46/66/88/110; tier5=GPA at :194-199, tier6=Finofo at :200-206), shopEngine.js (buy rapport gain :352-353 needs overValue>=1.2 for +3; sell gain :390-392 needs price<=ceil*0.96 when wanted for +3; sleep/win at :442-462), and Shop.jsx (help line :1042, dealLabel :689-691, rapportNote :742, Codex :1071-1122, RunEnd :953-1005). I also wrote a 150-seed simulation driving the real engine.

CORE CLAIM CONFIRMED (directionally, strongly): A pure profit-maximizing ("greedy") player never crosses tier 5 (88) or tier 6 (110). My greedy AI (buy at floor, sell at ceil): 0/123 winners reached 88, max rapport 84 — strikingly consistent with the finding's "never cross 88." The +3 levers ARE both anti-profit moves: overpay (>=1.2x value) on buy and undersell (<=0.96x ceil, wanted) on sell. So you must trade against your own margin to climb, and nothing quantifies the +3 vs +1 distinction (the toast at :742 only says "rapport up" vs "a little trust earned" — no magnitude, no mechanic hint). Confirmed: the win modal (:953-1005) offers only "New run," and the Codex (:1108-1110) shows locked beats as "A memory not yet shared / Reach hearts X" — so there is genuinely NO post-game "hear the rest" path. The portfolio's best resume lines (3.94 GPA, Senior SWE at Finofo) really can be missed.

BUT THE FINDING IS MIS-STATED IN SPECIFICS, hence partial:
1. Its quantitative sim numbers don't reproduce. My greedy AI won 82% (not 53%), med rapport 55 / max 84 (not med 91 / max 103). The directional conclusion survives, but the cited "evidence" figures are not reliable.
2. "Win-players never read the two best resume lines" is too absolute. A pre-existing audit sim (_audit/reveal-schedule.mjs, which I ran) using a fair-but-efficient policy (buy ~1.12x value = +2/+3, undersell on sell) wins 2901/3000 AND ~46% of those winners see ALL six cards. So a player who deals fairly can both win and unlock everything roughly half the time. The dichotomy is real for *profit-optimal* play, not for *all* winning play.
3. The help-line characterization is wrong. Shop.jsx:1042 reads "Fair, generous deals raise hearts rapport, unlocking perks and real pieces of Kaito's story" — it does say "generous," not "gouge-Kaito." The real gap is that it never explains that overpaying/underselling specifically (acting against profit) is the lever, nor quantifies it.
4. The finding MISSES a more severe, adjacent structural bug: sleep() returns at :442-448 on the win-night BEFORE the tier check at :451, and only ONE tier is revealed per night (:451-462). So tier 6 (110) crossed on the final trading night is never shown, and reveals can fall behind rapport. This is the deeper reason ~54% of even rapport-maxing winners still miss the Finofo card.

Net: a real, important content/UX defect (lore gated behind an unsignposted anti-profit play-style with no post-game catch-up), but the finding's framing is overstated and its numbers don't hold, and it overlooks the stronger structural cause.
verification.refinedRecommendation:
Three layered fixes, in priority order:

1) GUARANTEE THE PAYOFF (root cause). Decouple narrative from the rapport+survival treadmill so the two best resume lines are reachable by any engaged player: (a) On win (Shop.jsx RunEnd, :953-1005) add a "Hear the rest" button that reveals every still-locked beat in sequence (or routes into the Codex unlocked) — and bank them into records.lore so the Codex (:1071-1122) shows them afterward. (b) Make the Codex's locked cards (:1108-1110) readable after a win even if the rapport gate wasn't crossed. This alone removes the "best lines unreachable" problem with an M-effort, low-risk change.

2) FIX THE STRUCTURAL LOCKOUT (engine bug the finding missed). In shopEngine.js sleep(), the win branch (:442-448) returns before the tier check (:451-462), and only one tier reveals per night. Before the victory return, drain any pending tiers (loop applyPerk + queue all crossed RAPPORT_TIERS up to current rapport), or reveal up to all eligible tiers per night, so a player at rapport>=110 on the final day actually sees the Finofo card. Otherwise even fix #1's "Hear the rest" is the only path for ~54% of max-rapport winners.

3) SIGNPOST THE LEVER (UX). The +3 vs +1 distinction is invisible. In the haggle deal screen (Shop.jsx :742) replace the binary "rapport up / a little trust earned" with the actual delta ("hearts +3 — Kaito appreciates a generous deal" vs "hearts +1"). When appraise is unlocked, surface a hint near the slider that paying above ~value (buy) or below ~ceiling (sell) earns extra trust. And amend the help line (:1042) to state plainly that *over*paying and *under*selling — not just "fair deals" — is what deepens the friendship.

Optional tuning if you keep tiers gating perks: lower tier 6 from 110 to ~95-100 and/or add a baseline +1 on every completed deal regardless of side so steady traders drift upward over 8 days. Do NOT adopt the original's "reveal one beat per day regardless of rapport" verbatim — it strips all meaning from rapport; prefer the win-time catch-up (fix #1) which preserves the in-run reward while guaranteeing the portfolio payoff.

findings.title: Relic category has only ONE item; there are 8 categories not 9
findings.problem: Relic = Ancient Coin only; on a Relic-wanted or Collector day the shelf fills from a 1-item pool so it shows the same coin. Food (2) too. A curio collector at a curio shop feels barren.
findings.recommendation: Floor every category at 3 items. Relics: Bronze Idol (130), Cracked Urn (70), Rune Tablet (185). Food: Spiced Wine (38), Dragonfruit Preserve (55).
findings.evidence: shopData.js:53 ancient-coin only Relic; CATEGORIES=8; Potion3 Trinket5 Tool3 Scroll3 Gem3 Relic1 Curio3 Food2.

verification.reasoning:
The factual catalog claims are all CONFIRMED by reading shopData.js:37-61: Relic has exactly ONE item (ancient-coin, line 53); CATEGORIES (line 65) derives 8 unique categories not 9; Food has 2 (Honey Jar line 56, Wheel of Cheese line 57). I parsed the catalog programmatically and got exactly the stated distribution: Potion 3, Trinket 5, Tool 3, Scroll 3, Gem 3, Relic 1, Curio 3, Food 2 (23 items total). The thematic critique is legitimate — Relic and Curio are the two most lore-flavored categories and the headline of the "A Collector Visits" event (shopData.js:146), yet Relic is a single item.

BUT the finding's mechanical description is INACCURATE in a way that matters. It claims "the shelf fills from a 1-item pool so it shows the same coin." That is false. The shelf builder (shopEngine.js:140-146) uses shuffled(wantedPool, rng).slice(0, nWanted), which selects WITHOUT replacement, and nWanted is hard-capped at wantedPool.length via Math.min (line 142). So the same coin can NEVER appear twice. Furthermore, Relic can never be a SOLE want: wantsMin is 2 (shopData.js:17), and the Collector event wants Curio+Relic, giving a wantedPool of 4 items (3 Curio + 1 Relic). I simulated this: Collector day shelf=5 -> nWanted=3, shelf=7 -> nWanted=4, so you see at most ONE relic plus 2-3 curios plus non-wanted filler — varied, not a wall of identical coins.

So the real, narrower defect is: only ever ONE relic instance can appear on any shelf, making the relic category structurally thin and reducing flip variety on relic-wanted days — NOT a duplicate-display bug, and not a barren shelf (otherPool fills the rest, flips remain possible). The game is fully playable; there is no functional break, soft-lock, or economy issue. This is a content-richness/polish gap, which is why I rate it medium rather than high.
verification.refinedRecommendation: Floor every category at 3 items so wanted-category days (especially the lore-driven "A Collector Visits" event) offer varied flips. Concretely: add 2 Relics — e.g. Bronze Idol (base ~130, rare) and Rune Tablet (base ~185, rare/legendary) — and 1 Food — e.g. Spiced Wine (base ~38, common). Each new item needs a matching 64x64 inline SVG in itemIcons.jsx (currently 23 icons), or the icon render via dangerouslySetInnerHTML will be blank. Correct the rationale in the report: the issue is NOT that "the shelf shows the same coin" (impossible — shopEngine.js:142-144 selects without replacement and caps nWanted at wantedPool.length, and wantsMin=2 means Relic is never a sole want). The accurate defect is that the Relic category has only one buyable instance, so relic demand on a Collector day funnels onto a single-item pool, thinning flip variety and undercutting the "curio collector" fantasy. Optionally also state CATEGORIES.length === 8 wherever the codebase/copy implies 9.

findings.title: Catalog and quip pools are too small and repetitive for an 8-day run
findings.problem: 23 items recycle by day 4-5 (only value re-rolls). The single 6-line deal bucket fires on both buy (:357) and sell (:397), repeating each line 5-7x; total pool 38 lines. Overpay (the rapport lever) has 3 lines, insult silently costs 3 rapport (:295,:314). Flavor overuses the X-and-Y joke (:45,46,50).
findings.recommendation: Grow items to 40-48 (5-6/category). Split deal into dealBuy/dealSell, triple buckets, add rarity/streak-keyed lines and a no-repeat guard. Toast the insult/overpay rapport delta. Cap the X-and-Y joke at 2.
findings.evidence: 23 ITEMS; deal=6 at :357,:397; buckets=38; overpay=3 insult=4; :295,:314 silent -3.

findings.title: Story is mis-ordered, never bridges to the real Kaito, and the intro hides the hook
findings.problem: Beats read as a chronological resume ending on the Finofo title; the memorable karate beat is buried mid-stack where most never reach. Win/Codex stay in-fiction with no link to projects, the game or a resume. The Shop1 intro is all mechanics and never plants the story hook; the run auto-starts at mount. The 11 events are market-weather with no Kaito flavor.
findings.recommendation: Reorder to hook early (gamedev, karate) and end personal. Add a fourth-wall close on the win screen plus a button to Projects, and a Codex CTA. Add an intro line teasing the real Kaito; seed on focus. Add Kaito-flavored events.
findings.evidence: Order at 28 SWE,46 gamedev,66 karate,88 GPA,110 Finofo; Shop.jsx:976 in-fiction; Codex no CTA; Dialogs.jsx:178-215 mechanics-only.
